headline: Delhi government to open Kejriwal’s ‘Sheesh Mahal’ for public visits, tickets likely at  ₹20
content: Public Works Department Minister Parvesh Verma announced on Thursday that the Delhi government will open former chief minister Arvind Kejriwal's 'Sheesh Mahal' residence for a media tour initially, and later to the public.The minister said a ticketing system will be set up for reservation of visits for the public by this week."The doors of Sheesh Mahal will open from tomorrow. We will show it to the media," Verma said in a post on X in Hindi, along with a video attached of Kejriwal's first oath-taking ceremony as chief minister of Delhi."Looking at public demand, we will open 'Sheesh Mahal' for public tour. We will show the biggest example of corruption to people, that how one person who said he will not even use a government vehicle, had built the lavish residence for himself by demolishing several other houses," the minister had said. Initially, media tours will be organised; later on, the public can buy tickets and see the interiors of the residence, he added.According to officials, the ticket price is likely to be around ₹20 and for senior citizens and college students, the entry would be free.Earlier, the government also announced plans to rope in a private hospitality firm to manage the residence, which would be used for official conferences, lunches and meetings. "The public viewing will be for a limited period of time; after that, the plan to hand it over to a private hospitality company is in the works; it will be finalised soon," a senior government official said.The 6, Flagstaff Road bungalow, where former Kejriwal lived during his tenure as chief minister from 2015 to 2024, was nicknamed "Sheesh Mahal" by the BJP to highlight the alleged corruption by the Aam Aadmi Party and its national convener during the Assembly polls held in February 2025.To maintain these facilities, around 10 staff members are deployed, carrying out sweeping and cleaning of the property. After the Kejriwal family moved out of the controversial residence, PWD carried out an extensive audit of the interiors of the bungalow.

headline: Operation Health: 1,477 food outlets inspected, 175 hotels found with unhygienic kitchens
content: Gandhinagar: The state health department has inspected 1,477 food establishments across Gujarat under its ‘Operation Health’ drive, targeting ice cream and frozen dessert manufacturers and sellers, besides hotels operating along major highways. The inspections revealed unhygienic conditions at 175 hotels, prompting notices and voluntary suspension of operations for cleaning and corrective measures.Health minister Praful Pansheriya said on Thursday that 786 ice cream and frozen dessert establishments were inspected. These included 590 selling only ice cream, 32 dealing exclusively in frozen desserts and 164 selling both products.The department has directed all establishments to display mandatory boards distinguishing ice cream from frozen desserts to ensure consumers are not misled into purchasing frozen desserts as ice cream.The drive also covered 691 highway hotels. Of these, 175 were found to have unhygienic kitchens, inadequate sanitation and improper food-handling practices. Notices were issued, following which the operators voluntarily shut their establishments to undertake cleaning and corrective measures. The remaining 516 hotels were advised to improve hygiene standards, an official statement said.Suspicious and potentially unsafe food stocks found at 14 hotels were destroyed on the spot. Samples were also collected and sent to laboratories for testing. The minister said legal proceedings would be initiated if samples failed quality tests or serious violations were detected.“If a food poisoning incident occurs or an establishment is found serving unhygienic food, the hotel operator will be held directly responsible and strict action will be initiated,” Pansheriya said.He added that the drive would continue across Gujarat and urged consumers to remain vigilant about kitchen hygiene, food storage and serving practices.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Ahmedabad | Silver Rate in Ahmedabad | Bank Holidays in Ahmedabad | Public Holidays in Ahmedabad | Ahmedabad AQI | Weather in Ahmedabad | Petrol Price in Ahmedabad | Diesel Price in Ahmedabad | CNG Price in Ahmedabad | LPG Price in AhmedabadStay updated with the latest Ahmedabad news. headline: Manotsava brings mental health conversations beyond hospital walls
content: Mental health conversations are often confined to clinical settings, but Manotsava hopes to take them beyond hospital walls and into everyday life. Returning to Bengaluru for its third edition on December 5 and 6, the National Mental Health Festival will bring together doctors, researchers, artists, comedians, and people with lived experiences under one roof..Organised by Rohini Nilekani Philanthropies, NIMHANS and the National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS), the festival is free and open to all. This year’s edition follows more than 20 sharing circles held in Bengaluru and Delhi between August and October, and is expected to bring together over 300 people to discuss concerns such as caregiving, adoption and midlife..“We need to put the public back squarely and firmly into public health,” says Rohini Nilekani, chairperson of Rohini Nilekani Philanthropies. She believes that scientific understanding and lived experiences must inform each other, which is reflected in the festival’s mix of speakers and formats..Bengaluru restaurants struggle with high staff turnover.The programme includes keynotes by neuroscientist Sophie Scott on the science of laughter, and Dr Devi Shetty on AI’s potential to transform healthcare. .Actor Anil Kapoor will be in conversation with Rohini, while Dr Shyam Bhat, psychiatrist and psychotherapist, will explore the idea of the self in psychotherapy..Dr Shyam’s session will draw on his Integral Self Therapy approach, bringing together psychotherapy, Eastern philosophical traditions and neuroscience. He believes conversations around identity, loneliness, relationships and the psychological effects of social media are particularly relevant as Indian society undergoes a cultural shift..The festival will also feature 25 exhibits, six film screenings, panel discussions on addiction, suicide, masculinity and sleep, as well as workshops on magic, clowning, rap writing and therapy dogs. A dedicated children’s zone, an expanded Kannada programme and sessions in English, Hindi and sign language aim to make it accessible to wider audiences..On December 5 and 6, at Jayamahal Palace Hotel, Jayamahal Main Road. Entry free. Register at nationalmentalhealthfestival.com

Respecting the Constitution is not the responsibility of any one political party or government, but the duty of every individual whom the people have entrusted with the opportunity to serve them,” said Mr. Saini, addressing the House during the special session of the Haryana State Assembly on the 77th anniversary of the adoption of the Constitution. However, when serious questions are raised about the integrity of electoral rolls, complaints emerge regarding the deletion of voters’ names and doubts arise over the transparency of the electoral process, it signals a grave threat to the entire democratic framework.” Mr. Hooda said that any attack on the Constitution is a direct attack on the country’s democratic framework and the rights of its citizens. “The Congress Party will continue its struggle, both on the streets and inside legislatures, to safeguard the Constitution, the independence of constitutional institutions and free and fair elections,” he said. headline: Beneficiaries of ‘Maawan Dhiyan Satkar Yojana’ hail Punjab Governments initiative
content: The AAP government invited women beneficiaries of the ‘Maawan Dhiyan Satkar Yojana’ to the stage during ‘Khushhaal Punjab Rally’ here on Thursday to share their experiences of how the scheme had benefited them.Under the scheme, the state government provides monthly financial assistance of Rs 1,000 to women belonging to the general category and Rs 1,500 to those belonging to the Scheduled Castes, through direct bank transfers.Veena Sharma, a beneficiary from Moga, said the scheme had proved beneficial, particularly in helping meet expenses on medicines. She appealed to the public to bring the Bhagwant Singh Mann government back to power.Tanveer Kaur, who works as a ‘Sakhi’, said she was receiving a double benefit under the scheme. She thanked Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann for the initiative.Another beneficiary, Paramjit Kaur, was invited by AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal to join him on the dais along with her granddaughter.Thanking the AAP government, she expressed hope that the party would return to power.Navjot Kaur, a student from the Dharamkot Assembly constituency, said her father worked as a labourer and found it difficult to manage household expenses. She said the financial assistance under the scheme had also helped her meet her educational expenses.

headline: Delhi HC sets aside Centre’s order cancelling FCRA licence of NGO
content: The Delhi High Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) set aside the Centre’s order cancelling the FCRA licence of NGO Socio Legal Information Centre (SLIC), holding that the allegation of the organisation engaging in “aggressive anti-government political activism” was unsupported by any material. Editorial | Troubling bill: On the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/editorial/troubling-bill-on-the-foreign-contribution-regulation-amendment-bill-2026/article71337639.ece “Based on the record, this court is unable to discern any material based on which it could be said that the appellant’s activities would likely prejudicially affect the sovereignty, integrity, or security of India or public interest,” Justice A.J. Bhambhani said. The judge added, “The respondent’s allegation that the appellant has indulged in “aggressive anti-government political activism”, is also not based on any material. No documents or other material has been placed on record by the respondent to support that allegation”. Editorial | ​Fear of the foreign: On the FCRA amendments https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/editorial/fear-of-the-foreign-on-the-fcra-amendments/article70820494.ece The court further opined that the October 17, 2022 cancellation order the organisation’s FCRA registration was “misconceived, untenable and illegal, apart from being disproportionate and excessive in its rigour and impact”. The court passed the judgment on a plea by the NGO seeking to set aside the October 2022 order of the Ministry of Home Affairs cancelling its Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act registration certificate. The NGO also challenged the freezing of its designated foreign contribution account and its utilisation accounts maintained with several banks across the country. Editorial | Onerous rules: On the amended FCRA Rules, the fallout https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/editorial/onerous-rules-on-the-amended-fcra-rules-the-fallout/article71145372.ece The high court said the violations alleged in the cancellation order principally arise from the conditions for grant of an FCRA registration certificate, the essence of the allegation being that the NGO is guilty of diversion or misutilisation of such funds, or of using such funds for personal gains or diverting them for undesirable purposes. “However, upon examining the use to which foreign contributions have been put by the appellant, it is seen that such funds have been utilised and deployed for activities that are perfectly in line with the stated objectives of the appellant, namely, of providing legal-aid and engaging in social welfare activities,” Justice Bhambhani said. The court, in its 69-page judgment, said unless something sinister comes through from material available against it, an organisation that is engaged in assisting aggrieved persons in raising their grievances before courts and statutory commissions, acting through the available constitutional machinery, cannot be characterised as engaging in “political activity” or in activities impinging on political and law-and-order domains. “In the impugned cancellation order, the respondent has also alleged that the appellant’s activities amount to an attempt to portray a ‘wrong image of public institutions of India in the eyes of international community’. This court would observe that this allegation strains credulity; and this court is dismayed by the respondent’s attempt to baselessly portray the appellant organisation in such light,” it said.

headline: Delhi high court nixes order to cancel NGO’s FCRA licence
content: NEW DELHI: Taking a dim view of the home ministry’s reluctance to share even with the court the inputs that led it to cancel the FCRA licence of an NGO engaged in legal aid, Delhi high court on Thursday set aside the decision. HC said the move to cancel the licence of NGO Socio Legal Information Centre (SLIC) based solely on the allegation that it has indulged in “aggressive anti-government political activism” was without any material.HC said no material was furnished by government to show that SLIC’s activities would likely prejudicially affect the sovereignty, integrity or security of India or the public interest.Delhi HC: No proof of ‘anti-government activism’ charge against NGOWhile government contends that the violations on the appellant’s NGO’s part were brought to its notice through ‘security inputs’, which cannot be divulged since they are ‘secret’; this court is of the view that such inputs cannot be kept secret to the point that no material is brought even to the notice of this court, though the appellant has faced the drastic action of having its FCRA registration cancelled, arising from such inputs,” Justice AJ Bhambhani of Delhi HC said.“The respondent’s (Centre) allegation that the appellant has indulged in ‘aggressive anti-government political activism’ is also not based on any material. No documents or other material has been placed on record by the respondent to support that allegation,” HC added in its judgement.It said unless something sinister comes through from material available against it, an organisation that is engaged in assisting aggrieved persons in raising their grievances before courts and statutory commissions, acting through the available constitutional machinery, cannot be characterised as engaging in “political activity” or in activities impinging on political and law-and-order domains. “In the impugned cancellation order, the respondent has also alleged that the appellant’s activities amount to an attempt to portray a ‘wrong image of public institutions of India in the eyes of international community’. This court would observe that this allegation strains credulity; and this court is dismayed by the respondent’s attempt to baselessly portray the appellant organisation in such light,” it said.HC’s verdict came on a plea by the NGO seeking to set aside the Oct 2022 order of the home ministry cancelling its Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act registration certificate. headline: Madhu Bangarappa sets April deadline to recruit government schoolteachers
content: Bengaluru: Minister for School Education and Literacy Madhu Bangarappa on Thursday instructed officials in his department to complete the recruitment process for government schoolteachers by April so that all schools are fully staffed when they reopen for classes in June 2027. .The department has already published the calendar for the recruitment of 15,000 teachers, and has even extended the deadline for submitting applications to December 21. The Common Entrance Test for aspiring teachers is slated to be held between January 18 to February 12, 2027. ."Hold the examinations in January, and issue appointment orders by March-April. The newly-recruited teachers should report to duty when schools reopen in June," said Madhu. .Extending benefits to employees of aided institutions .The minister also chaired a meeting of MLCs from teachers' and graduates' constituencies wherein several issues including the possibility of extending the Old Pension Scheme to employees of private-aided institutions notified for recruitment before April 1, 2006 was discussed. Also discussed was the implementation of the High Court's order on notional pay benefits for employees of private-aided educational institutions. .English teacher post aspirants in Karnataka seek fair share in GPT recruitment.The legislators called on the minister to take steps to fill posts lying vacant in aided schools and colleges since 2015. .The implementation of the House Committee report on simplifying renewal of recognition for schools was deliberated upon, as was the issue of disparities in time-bound promotion for teachers and lecturers who have transferred from primary schools to high schools and PU colleges. .Extending benefits of the Arogya Sanjeevini Health Insurance Scheme to employees of aided institutions, and offering menstrual leave to their women employees were also mulled over during the meeting. .Recruitment of physical education teachers for state-run schools and colleges, disbursing grants to Kannada-medium schools established after 1995 and extending the two-language policy to aided institutions were among the other issues discussed by the legislators and the minister. .Health insurance for employees of unaided schools, colleges .MLC A P Ranganath urged the government to bring employees of private-unaided schools and colleges under the cover of the health insurance scheme. Madhu was receptive to the suggestion and asked Ranganath to submit a representation in writing. "I will discuss this with the Health Minister before taking a decision," said Madhu.

headline: Judicial member must on bench to confirm PMLA attachment, says Supreme Court
content: NEW DELHI: In an important insertion into the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, the Supreme Court on Friday said the bench of the adjudicating authority (AA), tasked with deciding the confirmation of ED’s orders for provisional attachment of assets by terming them proceeds of crime, must have a judicial member.Deciding a host of petitions questioning the competence of administrative members forming single-member benches to decide questions of law and conflicting judgements from various HCs, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that to confirm confiscation of assets termed as ‘proceeds of crime’ under Section 8 of PMLA, the AA is required to analyse legal provisions.“The presence of a judicial member on the bench undertaking the same ensures legal objectivity in the determination recorded by the AA. The lifetime of experience of the administrative and financial members in the AA would undoubtedly render them to be exceptional experts in their fields, but impartial and legally sound adjudication necessitates judicial temperament and training,” the bench said.It added, however, that the judgment would operate prospectively and not provide grounds for the reopening of past decisions.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Bihar move illegal, says Supreme Court, quashes premature release of former MP Anand Mohan
content: NEW DELHI: Quoting former US President Theodore Roosevelt to say justice consisted not in being neutral between right and wrong, but in finding out the right and upholding it, the Supreme Court Thursday quashed Bihar’s decision to allow the premature release of former MP and strongman Anand Mohan in the 1994 lynching case of district magistrate G Krishnaiah.The state government had amended prison rules to pave the way for Mohan’s release by removing the provision that disqualifies a person from remission if he is convicted of a public servant’s murder. A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu quashed the amendment, saying it was indefensible and no rationale was given for changing the law. It directed Mohan to surrender within a month.“The notification dated April 10, 2023, is declared unconstitutional, invalid and inoperative, and is hereby set aside. The order dated April 24, 2023, granting premature release to (Mohan), is hereby quashed,” the bench said.The court said the state government could initiate a fresh procedure to amend the remission policy. “It is clarified that any future process to revise or amend Rule 481 shall not be initiated prior to (Mohan) surrendering within a month or being taken into custody, as the case may be,” it said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Supreme Court to banks: Give nod to try officials in 7 days
content: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has read out the riot act and asked HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Sammaan Capital and PNB Home Finance to grant unconditional sanction within a week to prosecute their bank officials, who are charged by CBI for colluding with builders in the alleged duping of homebuyers under the subvention schemes, or remain present in court to explain the lapse.Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati said CBI, as directed by the SC, had inquired into 55 cases pan-India and has filed chargesheets in 22 cases, closed 3 cases and expects to complete the probe into the rest in three months.Once sanction is granted, courts will expeditiously take cognisance of CBI chargesheets, start trial: SCBhati informed a bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalay Bagchi and V Mohana that in the 22 cases, HDFC, ICICI, Samman and PNB have granted conditional sanction for prosecution, which is creating doubts in the minds of trial courts in taking cognisance of the chargesheet and proceeding with framing of charges.When senior advocate Sanjiv Sen, appearing for HDFC, said that sanction has been granted but there are certain rulings of the constitutional courts that flag the issue of whether private bank officials are public servants requiring sanction for prosecution. Moreover, the officials charged have been exonerated of wrongdoing in the internal inquiry, Sen said.The CJI-led bench said what else but exoneration of officials is expected in internal inquiries by banks, which had hobnobbed with rogue builders and cheated the homebuyers by releasing large sums of loan instalments to the builders even when there was hardly any progress in the construction of housing projects.When Sen protested against grant of sanction citing a judgment, the bench differentiated and said this is a court-monitored investigation, and hence SC can direct the banks to grant unconditional sanction for prosecution of delinquent officials.The bench said, “We direct all banks to issue unconditional sanction for prosecution within a week, failing which their CMDs shall remain present in court to explain why action should not be taken against them.”The bench said once the sanction is granted, the trial courts will expeditiously take cognisance of CBI chargesheets and begin trial as per law. It also directed CBI to conclude investigations into the remaining cases expeditiously and not later than two months.On Aug 6, SC said that in court-monitored investigations, sanction for prosecution should be granted promptly and directed the banks to give necessary permissions within two weeks for prosecution of the accused bank officials. “Failure to accord sanction within two weeks would require banks to submit explanations to the court,” it had said and asked the CBI to share documents on the money trail with the ED to kick off an inquiry under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Natural sweetener stevia offers new farm-to-industry opportunity for Telangana
content: Hyderabad: Telangana could be looking at a new opportunity to expand its farm-based industry, with stevia, a natural sugar substitute, emerging as a potential commercial crop. Buyers and officials at National Stevia Summit 2026 have indicated that cultivation could initially be taken up across 500 to 1,000 acres, with scope for expansion depending on market response and processing opportunities.Sri Konda Laxman Telangana Horticultural University will maintain a stevia nursery at its College of Horticulture in Rajendranagar to ensure availability of quality planting material and provide scientific guidance to farmers. University vice-chancellor Danda Rajireddy, who was awarded a honorary fellowship of Association of Agrometerologists ( FAAM), said Telangana had favourable conditions for cultivation and farmers could explore growing stevia as an intercrop in oil palm and mango plantations.Stevia is gaining attention amid growing demand for natural sweeteners, opening up opportunities not just in cultivation but also in processing, extraction of sweetening compounds and manufacture of value-added products. A strong farm-to-industry ecosystem could create additional income for farmers while encouraging new agro-processing units and rural employment.Stevia offers scope for multiple harvests, with farmers able to cut crop up to four times a year under favourable conditions. Telangana’s climate is considered suitable, with crop growing well at temperatures of 25° to 35° C and in soils with a pH of 5.5 to 7.5. However, large-scale adoption will depend on availability of quality planting material, water management, cultivation costs and, crucially, assured buyers and market linkages.Awareness about stevia remains limited among farmers, consumers and entrepreneurs. The National Stevia Summit 2026 was organised for the first time in Hyderabad by Sri Konda Laxman Telangana Horticultural University, Participatory Rural Development Initiatives Society and Global Stevia Forum to bring farmers, researchers, buyers and industry representatives together.Experts at the summit discussed improved varieties, nursery development, scientific cultivation practices, processing technologies, extraction of sweetening compounds and applications in food and beverage industries. headline: 7 months on, mediation in Sunjay Kapur case hits deadlock
content: NEW DELHI: Seven months of mediation proceedings, which were conducted on the direction of the SC for amicable resolution of the property dispute between late industrialist Sunjay Kapur’s mother, Rani Kapur, and his widow, Priya Sachdev Kapur, fell flat, and the former CJI DY Chandrachud, who was the mediator, told the court Thursday that the mediation reached an impasse despite 15 sittings.He was roped in by the SC in May to settle the high-profile property dispute between them over Kapur’s Rs 30,000 crore estate.Taking note of the report filed by the mediator, a bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran closed the mediation. “One can never force a settlement,” it observed.As the lawyers appearing for the Kapurs blamed each other’s clients for mediation failure, the bench told the parties, “When you all decide to sit, talk, and try to find a way out, you need to show some flexibility, some understanding, and take a practical view of the matter... 15 sittings and you all couldn’t reach a conclusion.”The court said that it would pass a short order in the case.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Opposition worried, feels government won’t risk another defeat
content: NEW DELHI: Despite repeatedly expressing apprehensions about a “sinister plan” behind the Modi government not proroguing the monsoon session for 106 days, the opposition was Thursday surprised by the BJP’s convening of the Parliament session, with the delimitation bill as the likely agenda. INDIA bloc is likely to meet Sunday to take stock of the situation.There is uncertainty in the opposition about the numbers game given the buzz around NCP-SP that has made equivocal statements in recent days. DMK’s stance is also being watched with wariness, though it was against the bill in the past. There is a feeling that government will not risk a loss of face on the bill again, and the convening of Parliament has raised concerns.The fate of the contentious legislation that would take the strength of LS to around 850 seats would depend on these two regional parties, strategists said.Congress’s KC Venugopal said, “For 106 days, they did not prorogue the monsoon session. There has been a complete lack of transparency... While the old delimitation bill was defeated, the new bill has not been circulated. Everybody is in the dark.”Amid speculation for more than three months over the delimitation bill, Congress spokespersons have been exuding confidence about the numbers, even vouching for DMK, which is not with the INDIA bloc anymore. Many have pointed out that DMK is a signatory to the recent unanimous resolution of the Tamil Nadu assembly, which had demanded that LS’s strength be frozen at 543 seats.Congress’s Jairam Ramesh said “the fight is on”, adding, “On Constitution Day, after 105 days of Operation Lotus, Modi government announces a special session, hoping it will get its super-tainted two-thirds majority to pass an amendment bill. Can there be a greater insult to and assault on the Constitution?”CPM’s MA Baby termed the delimitation bill as designed to carry forward the divisive agenda of BJP-RSS. “I was in Parliament for 12 years but had never witnessed such surreptitious methods being used to subvert democracy,” he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Health insurer refused to pay for 9-year-old’s $27,000 ear surgery, calling it cosmetic; how his parents
content: A Brooklyn family’s fight with health insurer Aetna has drawn attention to how patients can challenge denied medical claims. After the company classified their 9-year-old son’s $27,000 ear surgery as “cosmetic”, despite his doctors describing it as medically necessary, his parents took the case to an independent external review, and won.Nadine Friedman and Jared Roberts had watched their son, Ozzie Roberts, deal with Goldenhar Syndrome, a rare condition that, according to his medical records, caused pain, redness and growth problems in his right ear.“A lot of nights during the week, just midway through the night, [he was] just crying, screaming. It was really tough to see,” Roberts said.In February, doctors performed an ear-pinning surgery on Ozzie, which helped address the problem. However, the family then faced a months-long dispute over the cost of the procedure after Aetna refused to cover it.Why Aetna denied the $27,000 surgeryAetna classified the procedure as cosmetic, even though Ozzie’s doctors had stated that it was medically necessary. His parents first appealed directly to the insurer, but their request was unsuccessful.“I would absolutely never do anything like this unless it absolutely impeded on his health and his life,” Friedman said.Aetna said the doctor’s “original submitted billing code is typically for coverage of a cosmetic procedure and warranted further review.” The company also acknowledged how challenging a healthcare episode can be for families, but declined to be interviewed by CBS News New York.How the parents overturned the insurance denialAfter the initial appeal failed, the family sought an external review. In New York, state-appointed independent organisations can examine insurance denials and decide whether they should be reversed.Earlier this fall, the family learned that the external appeal had succeeded and Aetna would cover the surgery.Friedman said the process required considerable time and effort, something not every family may be able to manage.“Which is great, but it's only because I have a flexible job, time to document these things,” she said. “I'm really pushy, I'm fighting these things, and in the end, you have to become, like, a part-time insurance lawyer, basically, to do these things.”Despite securing coverage, the experience has prompted Friedman to push for broader changes. She is supporting the Ensuring Lasting Smiles Act, a proposed federal bill that would require insurers to cover necessary treatments for people with congenital anomalies or birth defects.More than half of New York’s external appeals overturnedThe family’s experience comes amid wider questions about how often insurance denials are reversed when patients challenge them.Researchers Ayesha Rahim of Brown University and Joseph Dov Bruch of Weill Cornell have studied the outcomes of external appeals. They found that 52% of denials that reached external review in New York State last year were overturned.“We did find that a majority of external appeals are overturned,” Rahim said.Bruch said reversals could happen for several reasons, including human or technological errors, ambiguity in insurance policies or potentially inappropriate conduct by insurers.What insurers say about denied claimsCBS News New York also sought a response from the New York Health Plan Association, a nonprofit trade association representing around 20 major insurers in the state.Its CEO, Eric Linzer, said the vast majority of requested services are provided. However, he argued that a doctor’s assessment of medical necessity is not the only factor insurers consider when reviewing a claim.“Oftentimes, you wanna make sure that the services being requested abide by peer-reviewed evidence, specialty society guidelines,” Linzer said. He also noted that there can be significant variation among providers.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

headline: Ashwini Vaishnaw hits out at TVK government over deepam row: ‘hurts sentiments of millions'
content: Union Minister of Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw on Thursday mounted a sharp cultural and political offensive against the TVK government asserting that "stopping the lighting of a traditional deepam," hurts the sentiments of millions of people and warned against "attempts to erase the country's civilisational heritage and temple traditions."Addressing a Constitution Day event held by the BJP, Vaishnaw questioned whether citizens would eventually be barred from visiting temples if such restrictions went unchallenged."Tamil Nadu is intact. Stopping one deepam, you have stopped, you have hurt, you have destroyed and disturbed the emotions of millions of people. What will happen? Today you have stopped one deepam, tomorrow you will say that nobody can go to a temple? They'll shut down the temples. Is that what they want?" he asked.The minister claimed that “true respect for the Constitution means safeguarding religious freedom and taking pride in our culture, Lord Muruga, and our ancient heritage.” Turning his appeal directly toward TVK from the stage for railway schemes, Vaishnaw challenged the party to take up the cause of land acquisition, assuring that the Centre would provide all necessary funds and complete every project without hassle to deliver justice to the Tamil people.The minister claimed that out of approximately 4,800 hectares required for railway projects in Tamil Nadu, the state government has acquired only 1,253 hectares, a mere 24 per cent.Questioning how the railways can build without land, he called for cooperative federalism-where two steps by the Centre were met with one step by the state-so both Tamil Nadu and its people can progressUrging leaders not to shy away from their responsibilities, he remarked while opponents might succeed in stopping a single deepam (lamp) from being lit, they cannot halt the growth, development, or global standing of the Tamil people, whose pride remains intact.Vaishnaw also accused the Congress of "rejecting" constitutional methods of conducting elections and spreading nationwide confusion.Pointing to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, he noted that the process was successfully conducted in Tamil Nadu without any objection from the Congress."Congress wants to just blame SIR for their own failures. And they will keep failing like this. Because for them, it is not the Constitution, it is the family. That is the only thing which is important for them. They don't believe in Dr Ambedkar's philosophy", he said. Extending this argument to Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs), he dismissed the Congress party's recurring complaints that EVMs lead to their losses.He said, "EVM voting took place across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Kerala, Himachal Pradesh, and West Bengal where the Congress won zero seats."Further, he claimed that the Congress party "refuses to do grassroots hard work and continues to rely solely on a family name."

headline: Special Parliament session from November 30; women’s quota on agenda
content: NEW DELHI: Ending suspense, government Thursday moved to convene a short session of Parliament from November 30 during which it is expected to bring back the delimitation bills to implement the women’s quota law from 2029, which would increase Lok Sabha’s maximum strength to 850 from 550, reflecting confidence in NDA that it will muster a two-thirds majority this time to secure the bill’s passage.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju announced that government has requested Speaker Om Birla to reconvene Lok Sabha on November 30 and Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan to call a sitting of the House on Dec 2 to transact “essential government business”.“Subject to exigencies of business, the sitting of both Houses may conclude on Dec 3, 2026,” he said, suggesting government is hopeful of concluding its agenda in four days.This is the second attempt by government to secure passage of its ambitious legislative agenda. If passed, it will mark the biggest realignment of Lok Sabha constituencies since Independence. A united opposition had thwarted the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill in a similarly convened session, of three days, from April 16.The move comes amid strong indications that government is confident of its numbers in the second trial of strength that the opposition is determined to force. In any case, it will be loath to risk another embarrassment; that too one during the build-up to assembly elections in UP and other states.Passage of the bill, which will ensure reservation of one-third seats in Lok Sabha and pave the way for a similar quota in assemblies, will give BJP a major campaign point in the upcoming polls to showcase its pro-women credentials.Shah’s assurance may be added to delimitation bill, Cabinet nod todayIn an article on Thursday, PM Narendra Modi said the scuttling of the bill earlier this year “should fill our hearts with shame”, adding that a legislation aimed at giving adequate representation to women was prevented from being passed by one opposition party, in what was an attack at Congress.He assured women that “no force can prevent us from ensuring that justice is done to them.”Last time, among 528 MPs present in Lok Sabha, the bill had received support from 298 members while 230 opposed it, falling way short of the 352 needed for its passage.Smarting under the government’s first defeat on the floor of Parliament, BJP has since made determined moves to shore up its numbers, helped considerably by fractures in the opposition camp.The switchover of 20 of 29 Trinamool Congress Lok Sabha MPs to NDA has boosted its numbers. Going by the buzz within government, it is also counting on support of 22 DMK MPs and eight of NCP-SP, who had voted against the bill last time along with TMC’s entire lot.Lok Sabha’s current strength is 540, with NDA’s tally at 321. The support of DMK and NCP-SP will take it to 351. The expected support from four YSR Congress MPs will take it closer to the 360-mark required in case all 540 MPs vote, which is unlikely as a few abstentions are expected to NDA’s advantage.Government has maintained secrecy about its potential new backers. DMK and NCP-SP have not announced support but have suggested that they can back the bill if states are not discriminated against — a threshold that government can easily meet by writing into the bill, which is already in Parliament, a clause providing for 50 per cent increase in seats across the board.Union minister Amit Shah had assured Lok Sabha in April that no state would suffer erosion in its relative strength in the lower House as the number of seats in each state would rise by around 50 per cent. The strength of state assemblies will be next to go up if the bill is passed. Shah’s assurance may be pencilled into the bill, which the Union cabinet headed by PM Narendra Modi is likely to clear Friday.A DMK MP told TOI that party chief MK Stalin will finalise their stand after looking at the bill, reiterating that southern states should not suffer. DMK has anyway drifted away from the opposition after Congress dumped it to align with CM Vijay-led TVK in Tamil Nadu.NCP MP Supriya Sule said “let the bill be out first”, suggesting her openness to the proposal. She said the bill may be good and needed to be studied first, and that opposition and government had in the past supported decisions which were in national interest.The hard part for the government is in the Lok Sabha, as its numbers are more favourably aligned in the Rajya Sabha.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: India’s GDP growth seen at 7.6% in July-September quarter: Economist
content: New Delhi: India’s economy likely grew by 7.6% in the July-September quarter and the growth may slow further in the second half of the current financial year, a senior economist said..Devendra Kumar Pant, Chief Economist at India Ratings and Research, said the country’s economy showed resilience in second quarter, despite El-Nino and oil price shock from the West Asia crisis..In the first quarter of the current fiscal, GDP grew by 7.8%. In the July-September 2025 quarter, it stood at 8.1%..Most agencies have projected the FY27 growth at around 7%. The fiscal 2026-27 is likely to mark the sixth consecutive year of over 7.0% growth. The average annual GDP growth between FY22 and FY27 is likely to be 7.8%..Pant said investment remains the main growth driver (average growth FY22-FY27: 10.0%), supported by private consumption (7.7%)..Indian economy to grow at 6.8%-7.2% in 2026-27: Economic Survey.The National Statistics Office (NSO) is scheduled to officially release the GDP data for July-September quarter on November 30..Pant said the GDP growth is likely to ease in the second half of the year. “The consumption outlook for 2HFY27 is likely to come under some pressure due to a) fading GST impact, b) higher interest rate/monetary tightening, and c) El-Nino impact on agriculture,” he said..As per an Ind-Ra analysis, Gross Fixed Capital Formation (GFCF) likely grew by 10.5% YoY in the July-September quarter..Both production and import indicators of investment remained strong in Q2 FY27. IIP of capital goods grew 14.9% and import of capital goods grew 30.2%. Consumption growth, which was stable in July-September quarter, is likely to weaken in the second half of the current fiscal..Ind-Ra expects Private Final Consumption Expenditure (PFCE) growth to slow to 6.8% in Q2 FY27 from 7.1% recorded in the previous quarter..Consumption indicators such as GST collection, credit growth, automobile production, and durable goods production point to stable consumption..However, negative growth in indicators such as consumer non-durable production, consumption of petroleum products, and negative real wage growth of agricultural labour and urban minimum wages (government notified wage in construction activities) are burdening consumption, Pant said..The consumption outlook for the second half of the current fiscal may come under some pressure due to fading GST impact, higher interest rate and El-Nino impact on agriculture..Cut-off box - null

headline: Supreme Court raps MNCs for ‘double standard’ on food quality
content: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday called out the “double standard” of multinational companies in producing foodstuff for Indian consumers inferior in quality to what they did in Western countries, saying it was “deeply troubling”.While directing FSSAI to enforce front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FoPNL) to make consumers aware of the contents of packaged food, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran deliberated on the dual yardsticks MNCs follow.“Concerns have been raised that certain multinational FBOs operating in India adopt practices towards Indian consumers that differ from those they follow elsewhere, including in the composition of their products and in the information provided on their labels. Such companies comply with, and in some instances voluntarily adopt, FoPNL requirements in other jurisdictions, yet resist similar measures here. If true, such double standards are deeply troubling,” the bench said.Saying a consumer in India was entitled to “no less protection and no less information” than one in the US or UK, SC said, “We would urge such multinational FBOs to adopt uniform standards across jurisdictions, and to extend to Indian consumers the same regard and respect for their health that they extend to consumers elsewhere.”It also directed FSSAI to ensure FBOs do not conceal or alter the composition of their products, or add additives, artificial preservatives, emulsifiers, etc, to soften the effect of FoPNL. “The introduction of a warning label must not become an occasion for reformulation that is hidden from the consumer, or that places the consumer at comparable or greater risk,” SC said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Telangana tops HIV control with 31 districts rated safe
content: Hyderabad: Telangana has emerged as the country’s top-performing state in HIV/AIDS control, with 31 of its 33 districts securing ‘Surakshit’ status under the National AIDS Control Organisation’s (NACO) Mobilisation for AIDS Suraksha (MAS) programme. With a 94% success rate, the state has outperformed Maharashtra (92%) and West Bengal (83%), according to the national MAS dashboard as of Nov 25, 2026.Arunachal Pradesh (74%) and Tamil Nadu (71%) follow in the rankings. Telangana’s performance stands out against the national picture, with only 273 of 784 districts (35%) across the country achieving Surakshit status.Implemented under the Union ministry of health and family welfare (MoHFW), MAS tracks HIV prevention, testing, treatment and care through the SOCH digital platform. Districts are assessed against the national 95:95:99 targets, which aim to ensure that 95% of people living with HIV know their status, 95% of those diagnosed receive antiretroviral therapy (ART), and 99% of those on treatment achieve viral suppression.Districts meeting all three targets are classified as Surakshit, those meeting two as Saksham, and the rest as Sangharshsheel. Nationally, 251 districts are in the Saksham and 260 in the Sangharshsheel category.Health minister Damodar Rajanarsimha congratulated officials, doctors and healthcare teams, crediting the achievement to the collective efforts of TGSACS, district collectors and health officials. headline: BRS left Telangana debt-ridden, neglected irrigation: Revanth at Achampet
content: Hyderabad: Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy said the Congress govt was taking Telangana “from destruction to development”, accusing the previous BRS govt of accumulating borrowings of ₹8.11 lakh crore during its 10-year rule. He also blamed the BRS govt and former chief minister K Chandrasekhar Rao for water woes in the Krishna basin, particularly in the erstwhile Mahbubnagar district.Revanth also criticised KCR for confining himself to his farmhouse after losing power instead of addressing people’s problems.Addressing a public meeting at Achampet on Thursday evening after laying the foundation stone for various development works worth about ₹380 crore, Revanth listed various welfare schemes implemented by the Congress govt. He said the state govt had spent ₹1.78 lakh crore on farmers, including on Rythu Bharosa, loan waiver and Rythu Bima. The CM also launched the distribution of one crore sarees to women at the meeting.The CM accused the BRS govt of neglecting irrigation projects in the erstwhile Mahbubnagar district for a decade, including SLBC, Kalwakurthy, Nettampadu, Bheema and the Achampet lift irrigation scheme. Had these projects been completed, he said, there would have been no irrigation water shortage in the district and water could have been provided to lakhs of acres in Palamuru.He alleged that the BRS govt, which had spent about ₹1.80 lakh crore on the irrigation sector in 10 years, failed to spend even ₹10,000 crore on Palamuru irrigation projects and had compromised Telangana’s interests in Krishna river water-sharing arrangements.He also criticised KCR for failing to prevent Andhra Pradesh from drawing Krishna waters through projects such as Pothireddypadu, Rayalaseema Lift Irrigation, Handri-Neeva and Muchumarri. Referring to the proposed allocation of 811 tmcft of Krishna waters, he alleged that the previous BRS leadership had agreed to Telangana receiving only 299 tmcft, allowing Andhra Pradesh to draw 66% of the water.“While KCR was associated with AP CM Chandrababu Naidu and did gross injustice to Telangana, former minister T Harish Rao had political proximity to former AP CM YS Rajasekhara Reddy and now his son YS Jagan Mohan Reddy,” Revanth said.Taking a swipe at the BRS’s prospects of returning to power, he questioned what the party had done to deserve another mandate. He asserted that the Congress govt would return to power and continue in office until 2034. The CM announced that the govt would soon fill another 25,000 vacancies, while 75,000 posts had already been filled, taking the total number of govt job appointments to one lakh. He also highlighted the implementation of SC categorisation and the caste census, claiming that Telangana had set an example for the country, and challenged Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the issue.Targeting the BJP, the CM said the party could not come to power in Telangana despite the efforts of its leaders Bandi Sanjay, Ramchander Rao and G Kishan Reddy. He also challenged the BJP and BRS to contest together, saying he was ready to take them on in the assembly.He also vowed to transform Achampet into a model constituency in Telangana, asserting that he was a son of the soil and would personally take responsibility for its development.Dedicated Commission for STsAt another meeting, CM Revanth Reddy assured that the state govt would appoint a chairperson from the Lambada community to the dedicated ST Commission and construct a temple for Sant Sevalal Maharaj on a sprawling 20-acre site, which he said would become a landmark for the entire country.Speaking after laying the foundation stone for a statue of Sant Sevalal Maharaj on Thursday, the CM said the govt was committed to empowering Lambadas and increasing the community’s political representation in the state, and that it would pursue the issue with the Congress high command in Delhi.Appealing to the Lambada community to support the Congress, Revanth said he would work tirelessly to provide employment, livelihoods and opportunities for the community’s overall advancement. In addition to the existing 16 acres, the govt acquired another four acres for the construction of the Sant Sevalal Maharaj temple, for a total of 20 acres.Highlighting schemes benefiting Lambadas, the CM said that of the eight lakh houses provided under the Indiramma Illu scheme in the state, nearly four lakh were allocated to beneficiaries from the Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST). He said SC and ST communities were now living with self-respect in their own permanent homes. headline: ‘Make me the PM’: SP’s Azam Khan takes swipe at Azad-Owaisi alliance, rules out differences with Congress
content: Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan on Thursday quipped that he is "already 'Azam'", responding sarcastically to speculation that Azad Samaj Party chief Chandrashekhar Azad and AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi might announce a Muslim Deputy Chief Minister candidate.Speaking earlier in the day, Khan played on the Urdu term for Prime Minister (Wazir-e-Azam) while brushing aside questions on the reported move by the Azad-Owaisi combine."...Make me the Prime Minister. Only the word 'Wazir' remains to be added to my name; I am already 'Azam'," Khan said. The Samajik Parivartan Morcha was formally announced in Lucknow on November 12 by Owaisi and Azad. The two parties have declared their intention to contest all 403 Assembly constituencies together, with Azad projected as the alliance's chief ministerial face. They have also indicated that the platform remains open to other political parties willing to join their effort.Also read | MK Stalin to take call after Bill tabled: DMK amid delimitation buzzThe decision to project Azad as the chief ministerial candidate is central to the alliance's political positioning. It places a prominent Dalit leader at the forefront of a partnership with a major Muslim political figure, giving the Morcha an opportunity to present itself as a broader coalition centred on social justice and political representation.For Owaisi, the partnership provides an opportunity to expand AIMIM's political footprint in Uttar Pradesh, where the party has yet to emerge as a major electoral force.Separately, speaking to reporters in the national capital, the senior SP leader dismissed reports of differences between the Samajwadi Party and the Congress over seat-sharing for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.Refuting suggestions of any resentment within the opposition alliance over the Samajwadi Party's election manifesto, Khan maintained that the partnership remains intact."No, there is nothing like that. It is all false. It is a manifesto of the Samajwadi Party; what resentment can one have? Our alliance will continue," he said. Also read | Abhijeet Dipke launches nationwide ‘Save Democracy’ movement at Constitution Day rally in NagpurSamajwadi Party is slated to contest the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in an alliance with Congress. The SP has offered 26 seats to the Congress in the initial round of discussions, while the Congress has sought 120 seats and is unwilling to accept a lower number, according to sources. The two parties are continuing discussions to reach an agreement on seat-sharing ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.Samajwadi Party is eyeing a return to power after two back-to-back electoral defeats in the 2017 and 2022 polls. In the last elections, the party won 111 seats.

headline: More buses, better last-mile connectivity key to easing city’s traffic woes: Experts
content: Hyderabad: With the city facing a widening public transport deficit, experts have called for strengthening its bus network, investing in a bus rapid transit system (BRTS) and improving last-mile connectivity. Projections by World Resources Institute (WRI) indicate that the city will require around 9,000 buses by 2031, against its existing fleet of just 3,200.Addressing ‘Cyberabad Moves’, Anand said Hyderabad still had an opportunity to address its growing traffic challenges and avoid a Bengaluru-like situation, where congestion has become a major concern. He called for planned expansion into new urban centres, with wider roads, reliable public transport and mass transit infrastructure built into development plans from the outset.“Excessive dependence on private vehicles, particularly single-occupancy cars, was a major concern, compounded by inadequate public transport connectivity between residential areas and workplaces. Many employees travel alone in large cars, partly because reliable public transport does not adequately connect residential areas with workplaces. People prefer bringing their own vehicles because they can drive directly to their offices. Public transport does not reach many workplaces, and last-mile connectivity remains a major challenge,” he added.Anand also flagged the lack of predictable bus services and poor connectivity between Metro stations and workplaces. He stressed the need to integrate buses, Metro and feeder services to make public transport a convenient alternative to private vehicles. Calling for a more proactive approach to traffic management, he said authorities should not hesitate to experiment with new traffic measures for fear of public criticism during the initial days.“Traffic management is all about experimentation. Officials should not be afraid of public opinion during the first two or three days of implementing a new measure. They must have the courage to implement and assess such initiatives,” he added.Former two-time mayor of Bogotá Enrique Peñalosa said Hyderabad could learn from Colombia’s capital, which has ensured access to a bus stop or cable transport network within every 500 metres. Noting that Bogotá was comparable in size to Hyderabad, he advocated low-cost, high-frequency bus services and denser public transport networks to make commuting more accessible and sustainable.Experts also called for premium, comfortable and reliable bus services along the IT corridor to encourage employees to switch from personal vehicles to public transport. “Deploying more 9-metre and 12-metre buses, equipped with Wi-Fi and charging points, could make bus travel more attractive to IT professionals. Seamless integration of buses with Metro services, including frequent feeder services connecting Metro stations to workplaces, was also identified as a priority,” WRI India executive programme director, integrated transport, clean air and hydrogen, Pawan Mulukutla said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. headline: Batala rifle shooter Kanwar bags gold in state games
content: Batala based rifle-shooter Kanwar Himmat Singh Goraya won a gold medal in the Khedan Watan Punjab Diyan games which concluded in Mohali recently.The games are a flagship state-level sports initiative launched by the Punjab Government to promote sports culture, fitness and youth engagement across block, district and state levels.The competition drew huge crowds as the state has a rich tradition of producing national and international level shooters.Kanwar clinched a gold in the 50-metre 3P event for under-21 shooters. This is an Olympic and ISSF (International Shooting Sport Federation) event in which a shooter uses a .22 long rifle at a 50-metre target. Shooters have to fire in three positions of kneeling, prone and standing, in which a players balance, endurance and precision is put to test.Experts say his accomplishment carries all the more significance as he competed against some of the best shooters of Punjab.His coaches claimed that in the final round, which was played under intense pressure, Kanwar held his nerves and shot with precision to secure the gold medal.It is in this highly-technical sport that Himmat has excelled. His father Harman Goraya said, “My entire family is proud of Himmat’s achievement. Rifle shooting is much more than hitting a target. It teaches stillness in moments of pressure. Whether practiced for fun or during an Olympic competition, it rewards patience and honesty and steadies’ nerves.”Physical skill alone is not enough in rifle shooting. A tiny tremor or rushed breath can send a shot off the mark. Shooters learn to control their breathing, relax their muscles, and block out distractions. Even athletes with visual impairments compete in shooting sports by relying on sound cues to aim. That shows how much the sport depends on awareness and control.

headline: China’s Drones Are Reshaping Asia’s Militaries
content: Southeast Asian militaries have a modernization problem: They cannot afford to miss the global shift toward drone warfare, particularly after Ukraine demonstrated the importance of cheap unmanned systems and rapid adaptation. And yet some of the most affordable and readily available technology comes from China — and buying it risks creating a dependency that could bring its own dangers. That leaves the governments of a $4.5 trillion bloc, collectively the world’s fourth-largest economy, trying to hedge their bets on defense hardware between Washington and Beijing, without getting caught in the slipstream of their superpower rivalry. Thailand — a formal US treaty ally — offers an interesting case study. America is a long-standing military supplier, with more than $3 billion in active sales that include F-16 fighter jet upgrades, helicopters and armored vehicles. Still, it’s the country with the strongest Chinese defense penetration, including battle tanks, naval systems and UAV technology.Last year’s Thai-Cambodia border war, the worst ever conflict between two members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, offers a real-time indication of how a military simultaneously modernizing with both US and Chinese weapons might fight. Thailand used combat aircraft imported from Sweden and the US, armed with South Korean guided bombs, alongside a locally developed drone based on Chinese technology, while Cambodia employed Chinese rocket systems. At its height, air strikes and artillery exchanges displaced over 600,000 people in Cambodia and some 400,000 in Thailand, with at least 150 killed.The use of mixed arsenals is likely to become increasingly common in the region. Indonesia operates Chinese- and Turkish-made drones and is purchasing Indian cruise missiles, while the Philippines uses Israeli-made hardware and Australian-supplied systems. Both are adapting their UAV fleets for surveillance and operations in the South China Sea. Drones are also widely used by all sides in Myanmar’s civil war.Beijing’s role in Southeast Asian military modernization frequently involves technology transfer and local development, making the Chinese origin of the eventual system much less obvious. China is now one of a small group of countries dominating the international military-drone market, along with the US, Israel, Turkey and Iran — and has been particularly important in making armed UAVs available to countries that struggled to obtain American systems.China’s importance runs deeper than the weapons it sells, though it’s worth noting that it dominates the commercial drone market, worth more than $5 billion annually. Turkey may be the world’s largest exporter of finished military drones, but those rankings obscure Beijing’s grip on the components and supply chains that increasingly underpin drone warfare. Even Ukraine, which has one of the world’s fastest-growing domestic industries, relies on China for 71% of its imports of key inputs.Everyone is rushing to buy these new systems, and unlike the West, Beijing is far less picky about who it’s selling to. Most nations opting to buy Beijing’s stack aren’t abandoning Western equipment altogether. But it’s clear that the huge boost in military spending globally is also lifting the sale of Chinese technology, said Gerald Mako, an expert on artificial intelligence and autonomous systems governance and a research affiliate at Cambridge University. The implications extend beyond the capabilities of individual weapons systems to technological dependence and the military balance across the Indo-Pacific, he told me.Since the beginning of President Donald Trump’s second term, Washington has shifted its priorities toward the Middle East through its war in Iran, and is now more interested in showy meetings with China and Russia than maintaining a stable presence in Southeast Asia. It’s overstating it to say that US military supremacy in Asia is over, however the gap with China is now narrower than ever. The Lowy Institute’s 2026 Asia Power Index found that the US-Iran conflict, combined with Washington’s pressure on countries to spend more on their own defense, had contributed to a record decline in US diplomatic influence in Asia.Nations in this part of the world are used to a US that’s distracted by priorities and conflicts elsewhere. But the collateral damage is glaringly visible this time. Iran’s move to restrict shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and disrupt fuel supplies should not be underestimated. The Philippines remains under a national energy emergency eight months after it was declared, while every Southeast Asian government has been forced to introduce emergency measures to cushion the impact of the war .China itself has important weaknesses. Its impressive pace of shipbuilding masks a key question about just how conflict-ready Beijing is. It hasn’t fought a major war since invading Vietnam in 1979 — unlike the US, which starts wars with depressing regularity. It’s too early to say whether more nations are planning to adopt China’s military systems. The impact of winder adoption would certainly be profound and long-lasting. To counter this, the US, South Korea and other exporters should push to develop more affordable systems. They must be able to integrate easily with Asia’s armed forces while ensuring sensitive data is shared securely. The US could also ease its export regulations and expand sales among nations that have struggled to access its drone technology. There are always options. But with US focus elsewhere, Southeast Asian nations may be left with only one — China — to help them modernize their militaries. headline: SAD-BJP tie-up sparks tussle among ticket aspirants in Amritsar
content: Days after the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) revived their alliance in Punjab, both parties face the challenge of managing multiple ticket aspirants in several Assembly segments, with fears that disgruntled leaders may choose the rebel path.The border district comprises 11 Assembly constituencies. Traditionally, the BJP has contested four seats, while the remaining seven have been allotted to the SAD. However, unconfirmed reports suggest that the BJP may seek a larger share of seats in the forthcoming Assembly elections.Before the two parties parted ways, the BJP fielded candidates from Amritsar North, East, West and Central constituencies. In Amritsar North, the party will have to accommodate several ticket aspirants. Sitting MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, who won the seat on an AAP ticket and later joined the BJP, is among the contenders. Former BJP Punjab president Shwait Malik, Sukhwinder Singh Pintu, who unsuccessfully contested the last election, and Akshay Sharma, who has been active in the constituency over the past few years, are also seeking the party ticket.A similar situation exists in the East constituency. Former IAS officer Jagmohan Singh Raju, who contested unsuccessfully on a BJP ticket in the last Assembly election, is seeking another chance. Rajesh Honey, a former BJP candidate from the seat, and Rajbir Sharma are also in the race.The Amritsar Central Assembly constituency, traditionally considered a BJP stronghold and represented several times by veteran leader Laxmi Kanta Chawla, currently has only one prominent aspirant, Ram Chawla. However, ever since Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh joined the BJP, speculation has been rife that he may be fielded from the constituency, which has witnessed demographic changes due to migration from Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal, alongside the movement of local Punjabi residents to newer city colonies.The alliance partners have traditionally allotted the Amritsar West (SC) Assembly constituency to the BJP. Kumar Amit, who contested unsuccessfully in the last election, along with Rakesh Gill and Balwinder Kaur, are among the ticket aspirants.Election statistics reveal that the BJP has traditionally struggled in the constituency. In the 2017 Assembly election, BJP candidate Rakesh Gill secured 24,424 votes, while Congress candidate Raj Kumar Verka won with 52,271 votes. The impact of the SAD-BJP split was evident in the last election, with SAD candidate Dalbir Singh Verka polling 10,370 votes and BJP nominee Amit Kumar securing just 8,999 votes. As a result, there is a growing demand within some quarters to allot the seat to the SAD, given its sizeable Sikh and Scheduled Caste voter base.For the BJP ticket from the Amritsar South constituency, Harjinder Singh Thekedar and Gurpartap Singh Tikka are staking claim, having both contested from the seat earlier. The constituency has traditionally been an Akali stronghold and was won by members of the Bolaria family in four successive elections between 2007 and 2017. Following the SAD-BJP split, Inderbir Singh Bolaria contested as a Congress candidate, while the SAD fielded Talbir Singh Gill in the last Assembly poll.The SAD has appointed a relatively lesser-known leader as its halqa in-charge for the South segment, overlooking several senior leaders. Among them is Avtar Singh Truckawala, a four-time councillor from different wards of the constituency and a well-known political figure in the area.Jandiala (SC) Assembly constituency remains a traditional SAD seat. The youngest son of former Akali MLA Malkiat Singh AR, who won the constituency in 2007, is among the aspirants for the party ticket.Bikram Singh Majithia is widely seen as the natural choice for the SAD ticket from the Majitha Assembly constituency, currently represented by his wife.In Baba Bakala (SC), Baljit Singh Jalal Usma is considered the main SAD ticket contender, while Gulzar Singh Ranike is likely to be fielded from the Attari (SC) constituency. Following SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal’s announcement that a Dalit leader would be appointed Deputy Chief Minister if the alliance comes to power, Ranike is being viewed as a strong contender for the post.In Raja Sansi, former Akali MLA Vir Singh Lopoke and Akali leader Rajwinder Singh Raja Ladeh are among the ticket aspirants. Jodh Singh Samra is seeking the party ticket from the Ajnala Assembly constituency.Shwait Malik, a member of the BJP Punjab Election Committee, said the final decision on seat-sharing and constituency allocation would be taken at a joint meeting of the parliamentary boards of the BJP and SAD.

headline: Pension, insurance for 15 lakh gig workers likely by year-end
content: NEW DELHI: Government is likely to announce a pension scheme along with health insurance, maternity benefits and life and disability covers for the nearly 15 lakh gig and platform-based workers enrolled on the e-Shram portal by Dec-end, TOI has learnt.“Workers who have been enrolled by platforms on the portal will be the primary beneficiaries. All leading platforms have already shared data,” an official said.The move will affect lakhs working with platforms like Swiggy, Zomato, Uber, Ola, Rapido, Pronto, Snabbit and Urban Company.The measures are set to be discussed in the maiden meeting of the National Social Security Board next month. It is expected to deliberate on contributory models, including a turnover-based model, where platforms or aggregators will contribute 2% of their turnover to the social security fund. headline: Hyd needs footpaths, not more flyovers, to fix mobility crisis
content: Hyderabad: The fundamental right of pedestrians to access safe, unobstructed and continuous footpaths goes beyond just urban mobility. Experts have called for stricter enforcement against those occupying pedestrian spaces, including commercial establishments and vehicle owners, with clearly defined penalties for repeat violations.Experts said that Hyderabad can take a cue from cities such as Singapore, where pedestrian infrastructure is an integral part of urban planning. Despite its hot and humid tropical climate, Singapore has developed extensive networks of continuous walkways, making walking a convenient and accessible option. In Hyderabad, however, reaching a bus stop or Metro station is not just about the distance commuters have to cover but also the risks they face while navigating footpaths and crossing roads.A perception survey presented at the Cyberabad Moves event has underscored these concerns, with 41% of respondents saying they feel unsafe at junctions, highlighting the need for safer pedestrian crossings and better-designed, continuous footpaths. The survey, conducted among 200 people at Biodiversity Junction and Gachibowli, found that only 20.5% felt safe at pedestrian crossings.“Hyderabad does not necessarily need more highways or subways to solve its mobility crisis; it needs better footpaths,” said former mayor of Bogotá, Enrique Peñalosa. headline: No content from Pakistan to be shown in India, government reminds Netflix
content: NEW DELHI: Netflix’s first original Pakistani series has run into a diplomatic and regulatory hurdle in India even before its global premiere. The ministry of information and broadcasting on Thursday asked the streaming giant to ensure that no content originating in Pakistan is made available to Indian subscribers, following complaints over the possible release of its star-studded romantic drama, Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo.Scheduled for release on December 4, the series features Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan, Sanam Saeed and Hania Aamir, actors familiar to Indian audiences. Netflix has not clarified whether India is among the markets where the series will be streamed.Government advisory on Pak content issued during Operation SindoorThe ministry’s intervention comes 18 months after government, amid Operation Sindoor, issued an advisory on May 8, 2025, asking digital platforms to discontinue Pakistani-origin films, series, songs, podcasts and other content on national security grounds.Officials said Netflix had informed the ministry in June 2025 that no Pakistani-origin film or series was available to its Indian subscribers. The ministry has now asked it to honour that commitment.When TOI reached out to Netflix, the platform said it had no comment.The controversy escalated after All Indian Cine Workers Association and Federation of Western India Cine Employees approached PM Narendra Modi. All Indian Cine Workers Association has also sought a permanent legal framework prohibiting Pakistani entertainment content in India, while Federation of Western India Cine Employees, an umbrella body of 32 associations representing five lakh workers, threatened to “ensure the shoot of all Netflix projects comes to a halt” if the series is released.Pakistan’s planning and development minister, Ahsan Iqbal, accused India of weaponising art and culture.Directed and produced by Momina Duraid, the series is based on Farhat Ishtiaq’s bestselling 2013 Urdu novel.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spoken for
content: Nandini (name changed), 16, who lives in Rajasthan’s Sikar, had mapped out her future: finish school, go to college, and get a job to be financially independent. Her family, however, had other plans. Last month, they fixed her wedding without her consent. But the Class 12 student refused to surrender her dreams. She picked up her father’s mobile phone and called the 24x7 child helpline, 1098. Over the next few days, Nandini called the helpline more than six times, using whatever phone she could lay her hands on. Sometimes, she pretended she wanted to speak to her prospective groom; at other times, she sought to contact her friends. But each call carried an urgent message: wedding preparations were under way, guests were being invited, and the date was drawing closer. Help! Each time, the call was connecting to the District Child Protection Office. “She had asked us not to contact her. She said she would call whenever she got a chance. Her first call came just three days before the wedding,” recalls Gargi Sharma, District Child Protection Officer. With barely 72 hours to act, the team secured an injunction order from the court and stopped the wedding. The family was taken by surprise when officials arrived, suspecting that a neighbour had tipped them off. They never imagined that the quiet schoolgirl in their midst had been orchestrating her own rescue. Her identity as the whistleblower remained a secret. The Sikar administration prevented 29 child marriages in 2024 and 10 in 2025. “In 2026, we have received information about 21 cases so far,” Sharma says. But there are many Nandinis, especially in India’s villages, who do not have the education or the agency to say no to child marriage.

headline: Supreme Court sets timer for FSSAI, companies to implement warning labels
content: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has set a timeline to implement the front-of-package labelling for each nutrient of concern on packaged food.The top court granted four months’ time to food regulator FSSAI to frame rules, and one year’s time to make it compulsory for companies. The labels indicating high sugar, saturated fat and salt will be placed inside red, hexagonal shapes.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran pushed the regulator to fall in line and discharge its duty to protect the interest of consumers, noting that FSSAI showed “reluctance” on labelling followed in many countries to make consumers aware of the harmful contents.Supreme Court said India is facing a major public health crisis, driven in part by the consumption of foods high in saturated fat, sugar and/or salt. “The population’s exposure to harmful substances must be controlled, their consumption must be discouraged, and consumers must be protected from practices detrimental to health used by the food businesses. Preventive measures, that are most effective, must therefore be undertaken in an effort to respect, protect and guarantee the right to health,” the bench said, adding that it cannot remain a “mute spectator” in such a situation.Supreme Court: Every day’s delay allows unlabelled food to be soldSupreme Court bound the regulator to the time frame suggested by it, which was four months to follow the process under the 2006 Act and regulations. It agreed that food business operators be granted a year’s time from the date of notification to implement the labelling regime. The intervening 365 days will be a “voluntary implementation” period.“Every day of delay means that packaged foods continue to be sold without such labels, to the detriment of the rights to health, food and informed choice, respectively... FSSAI should anticipate potential impediments and take active measures to ensure that they are resolved or adequately addressed,” the bench said.“The right to health has expanded from being limited to healthcare to addressing the broader determinants of health and conditions congenial to good health; the right to food now requires access to food which is sufficient in terms of both quantity and quality; and the right to informed choice has expanded its focus towards confronting the broader informational and social order that people live in,” Supreme Court said.It rejected FSSAI’s plea that there be only one hexagon within which levels of ‘high sugar’, ‘high saturated fat’ and ‘high salt’ would be placed, directing there be a separate hexagon for each nutrient of concern. “The font size... must be such that it remains clear, prominent and readily legible alongside pictograms,” Supreme Court added.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
