headline: Govt’s retirement-day police promotions policy sparks backlash
content: Panaji: Questions are being raised about BJP govt’s policy of promoting police personnel on the eve of retirement, with critics arguing that it violates established promotion norms and administrative processes.Chief minister Pramod Sawant said on Wednesday that police personnel would retire one rank higher than their existing rank. By way of example, he said a head constable would retire as a police sub-inspector (PSI) on the final day of service.Former Goa Government Employees Association (GGEA) president John Nazareth criticised the announcement, saying Sawant—who is also the home minister and holds the additional charge of personnel — should know that promotions require a no-objection certificate (NOC) from the department of personnel, in consultation with the department of administrative reforms. He said govt employees are already mocking the announcement.Retired superintendent of survey and land records, Ajit Talaulikar, supported the criticism, saying govt cannot apply two different yardsticks to employees under the same administration.Kashinath Shetye, an executive engineer with the electricity department and a vocal critic of govt, said he would challenge the policy in the Bombay high court once it is notified. “It will be quashed as not as (sic) per Article 14 and 16 of Constitution of India. Give to all govt servants. Why step motherly treatment to others govt servants?” Shetye said.Nazareth urged Sawant to reconsider the policy and withdraw it immediately, warning it would set a bad precedent for the entire country. He also questioned why such a benefit should be limited to Goa police personnel. “If such promotions are granted to the police personnel working in Goa, why not for those working in CBI and NIA? Why no special promotion for those working as doctors and saving the lives of people? Why not for the teachers or all other govt servants?” Nazareth said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Goa | Silver Rate in Goa | Bank Holidays in Goa | Public Holidays in Goa | Petrol Price in GoaStay updated with the latest Goa news. headline: Commemorative coin to mark Sobha Singh’s legacy
content: Legendary artist Sobha Singh, whose iconic portraits helped shape India's cultural and spiritual imagination, is set to become the first Indian painter to be honoured with a commemorative coin. The Government of India has notified the issuance of a ₹125 commemorative coin to mark his 125th birth anniversary, with its release expected early next year.The announcement is a moment of pride for admirers of the artist, whose life and work forged a lasting cultural bridge between Punjab and Himachal Pradesh. Born on November 29, 1901, at Sri Hargobindpur in Punjab, the artist made Andretta in Himachal Pradesh's Kangra district his home after the Partition.The commemorative coin will form part of year-long celebrations of his 125th birth anniversary, to be observed from November 2026 under the theme "Janambhoomi Se Karmabhoomi Tak". The theme reflects Sobha Singh's journey from his birthplace in Punjab to Andretta, where some of his most celebrated works were created.Welcoming the Centre’s decision, KG Butail, president of the Sobha Singh Memorial Art Society, Andretta, said the notification was the culmination of sustained efforts to secure national recognition for the painter.Calling it a proud moment for Himachal Pradesh and Punjab, he said Sobha Singh’s contribution to Indian art and his humanistic philosophy deserved the highest national recognition. He expressed confidence that the coin would introduce the artist's work and philosophy to younger generations.Butail also acknowledged the support of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in taking forward the proposal for the commemorative coin. He expressed gratitude to former Union ministers Anurag Thakur and Vijay Sampla, former Himachal Chief Minister Shanta Kumar and former Rajya Sabha MP Tarlochan Singh for their efforts in pursuing the demand.For the artist’s family, the announcement carries a deep emotional significance. Dr Hirday Paul Singh, secretary general of the society and grandson of Sobha Singh, described the honour as a fitting tribute to an artist whose paintings conveyed a universal message of humanity and compassion. He said the recognition would take his grandfather's life, philosophy and artistic legacy to a much wider national and international audience.Sobha Singh’s artistic contribution remains etched in India's cultural consciousness. His portraits of Sikh Gurus, historical personalities and spiritual figures are admired for their depth, sensitivity and spiritual expression. For Andretta, the Himalayan village that became his creative home, and for Punjab, where his journey began, the honour is a tribute to a legacy that continues to inspire generations.

headline: Sirsa’s ‘Ashubh Vivah’ campaign targets child marriage
content: Invitation cards carrying the message ‘Ashubh Vivah’ instead of the traditional ‘Shubh Vivah’ are being circulated in Sirsa as part of a campaign to raise awareness against child marriage. The cards feature names of girls married at an early age and appeal to people to oppose the practice.The initiative is part of the Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat Abhiyan, run jointly by Selfie with Daughter Foundation and Just Rights for Children. According to the campaign organisers, the cards refer to UNICEF data highlighting that 22.30 crore women in India were married before the age of 18. A national-level programme marking the second anniversary of the campaign will be held at Chaudhary Devi Lal University on November 27. More than 6,000 participants, including students, women, teachers, panchayat representatives and social workers, are expected to attend. Sunil Jaglan, director of Selfie with Daughter Foundation, said the programme would feature tableaux depicting different roles in child marriage, including those who arranged such marriages, participated in them, remained silent or failed to prevent them.Cash prizes of Rs 21,000, Rs 11,000 and Rs 5,100 will be awarded to the best tableaux.

headline: Constitutional values take centre stage at Himachal law varsity
content: Himachal Pradesh National Law University (HPNLU), Shimla, celebrated Constitution Day on Thursday in the presence of Prof (Dr) Priti Saxena, Vice-Chancellor, along with faculty members, students and other members of the university fraternity.On the occasion, Prof (Dr) SS Jaswal, Dean, Academic Affairs, HPNLU, read out the Preamble to the Constitution of India, reaffirming the university's commitment to the constitutional values of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity. Faculty members, students and other participants joined in the observance, reflecting on the principles enshrined in the Constitution.The celebration was organised in accordance with the directions issued by the University Grants Commission (UGC) and the Government of Himachal Pradesh as part of the nationwide observance of Constitution Day. The occasion provided an opportunity to reflect on the significance of the Constitution and the values that highlight India's democratic and constitutional framework.

headline: Chief Minister to release book on Cochin royal family
content: KOCHI The Making of Cochin, a book on the erstwhile Cochin royal family, co-authored by Kocha Rama Varma, Usha Chettur Varma, and Rajith B. Nair, will be released by Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on December 5 at Kalikotta Palace, Thripunithura at 4 p.m. It will be followed by a discussion on the book.

headline: Young minds explore the spirit of Constitution at Chamba’s Holi school
content: The District Legal Services Authority (DLSA), Chamba, organised a legal awareness camp and an essay-writing competition at Eklavya Model Residential School, Holi, in the Bharmour subdivision of Chamba district on Thursday to mark National Law Day.The initiative aimed to promote legal and constitutional awareness among young people and encourage them to become informed, responsible and law-abiding citizens. It also provided students with an opportunity to engage with constitutional principles beyond the classroom through writing and collective participation.The programme began with DLSA Chamba Secretary and Senior Civil Judge Ekansh Kapil, students and teachers collectively reading the Preamble to the Constitution of India.The participants reaffirmed their commitment to constitutional values and ideals while sensitising students to the importance of the Constitution in ensuring justice, equality and individual freedoms.An essay-writing competition on the theme ‘Constitutional Duties and Values’ was organised for students of classes X, XI and XII. As many as 83 students participated in the competition, expressing their understanding of constitutional principles, civic responsibilities and the role of citizens in strengthening democracy.The programme witnessed the participation of 210 students and 15 members of the school staff, including the Principal and teachers.

headline: Kullu DCC chief submits reply, ball now in HPCC’s court
content: The Himachal Pradesh Congress Committee (HPCC) has received the written reply submitted by Kullu District Congress Committee president Ses Ram Azad to the show-cause notice issued to him, with the party set to take a decision after examining his response.HPCC organisational secretary Vinod Zinta confirmed the development on Thursday, saying the party would decide its next course of action after going through the reply.The show-cause notice was issued after the Kullu DCC endorsed a resolution passed by the Kullu Block Congress Committee seeking the induction of Kullu MLA Sunder Thakur into the state Cabinet. Azad had also been directed to appear before AICC in-charge for Himachal Pradesh Rajni Patil and state Congress president Vinay Kumar within 10 days to explain his position.Azad said he had a brief meeting with Patil during the party's Samvidhan Raksha March in Shimla on Thursday, describing it as a courtesy call. He said he would meet the state Congress president on Friday to clarify the matter.Maintaining that the Kullu DCC had not acted against the party's directions, Azad said the district unit was following all instructions issued by the party high command and the HPCC. He also pointed out that more than 150 Congress leaders and workers from Kullu had participated in Thursday's march, asserting that the district unit remained committed to the party.Azad said a few Kullu leaders, including MLA Sunder Thakur, could not attend the march as it coincided with the hearing in a case registered against them during the previous government over their participation in a protest.Meanwhile, in a separate organisational development, the HPCC on Wednesday removed state vice-presidents Rajneesh Khmita and Mohinder Chauhan from their posts, citing their prolonged absence from party programmes.

headline: Constitution Day: Yamunanagar-Jagadhri civic body holds rally against single-use plastic
content: he Municipal Corporation, Yamunanagar-Jagadhri (MCYJ), organised an awareness rally against single-use plastic at DAV Senior Secondary School, Model Town, on the occasion of Constitution Day on Wednesday.Around 150 students from the school participated in the rally, organised with the support of Heer Enviro Services Private Limited, an authorised agency of the Municipal Corporation. Through the rally, students sensitised citizens and shopkeepers about the harmful effects of single-use plastic and the need to protect the environment.During the programme, students were informed about the fundamental duties enshrined in the Indian Constitution. They were told that Article 51A makes it the duty of every citizen to protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and to show compassion towards all living creatures.The rally was organised to highlight this constitutional responsibility and spread the message of environmental protection. It started from the DAV School campus and covered a distance of around 2 km, passing through Chhoti Line Road, Santpura Gurudwara, Nehru Park and Madhu Hotel.Passing through various market areas, the rally returned to the school campus. A presentation featuring the Plastic Monster, along with drumbeats, attracted public attention and highlighted the need to protect the environment.

headline: Haryana Human Rights Commission chief visits old-age home in Narnaul
content: Justice Lalit Batra, the Chairperson of the Haryana Human Rights Commission (HHRC), inspected SEWA Senior Citizens’ Home located at Nasibpur in Narnaul on Wednesday.During the inspection, Justice Batra interacted with the men and women inmates of the old-age home. He enquired about their daily routine, living conditions, food, healthcare facilities and arrangements for their care. “Ensuring due respect and a dignified life for senior citizens is among the key priorities of the Human Rights Commission,” he stated, adding that such visits maintain the accountability of the institutions and reassure elderly residents that their needs and rights are being duly addressed.The HHRC chairperson said the functioning and arrangements at the old-age home are also monitored by the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA).“The Secretary of the Authority regularly visits the home and provides all possible assistance to senior citizens in matters concerning their legal rights,” he said.To address the medical concerns of the elderly residents, Justice Batra called up the Civil Surgeon, who assured him that necessary medical assistance would be provided to the senior citizens requiring healthcare support.District Social Welfare Officer Amit Sharma said the elderly residents were being provided benefits under various welfare schemes of the Haryana Government.Justice Batra felicitated the elderly residents by presenting them with bouquets as a gesture of respect and appreciation.

headline: Farmers march to Tikri border on 6th anniversary of Delhi stir
content: Farmers and various farm outfits under the banner of Samyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM), Haryana, staged a demonstration at the Tikri-Bahadurgarh border and took out march on Thursday, marking six years of the historic Delhi farmers’ agitation and demanding land for a memorial honouring farmers who died during the movement.They also submitted two memorandums addressed to the President and the Haryana Chief Minister through the district authorities, highlighting pending demands. Police personnel in good numbers were deployed and barricades were installed en route of march.The protesters first held a meeting at Sector 9 in Bahadurgarh town before taking out a march towards the Tikri Border. On reaching the Tikri Border, the farmers observed a two-minute silence in memory of the deceased farmers.Sumit Dalal, district general secretary of the All India Kisan Sabha, said the Delhi agitation against three farm laws began on this day six years ago and continued for 13 months, forcing the government to repeal the laws. However, he accused the Centre of betraying the farmers by failing to honour its written assurances on other demands.“Besides demanding memorial sites at the Tikri and Singhu borders, the protesters called for a legal guarantee of MSP at C2+50 per cent with assured procurement of all crops, complete farm loan waivers and withdrawal of the proposed India-US free trade agreement. They also demanded repeal of the Electricity Amendment Bill 2025 and Seeds Bill 2025, an end to forced installation of prepaid smart meters and land acquisition, and withdrawal of the four labour codes. Other demands included restoration of MGNREGA with 200 days of work and a daily wage of Rs 700,” said Dalal.The protesters also accused the Haryana Government of pursuing anti-farmer policies and misleading the farmers over MSP guarantees. They announced a gherao of the Chief Minister’s office on December 2 over the failure to increase sugarcane prices.Earlier, Vikas Sisar, a farm leader, while addressing a gathering during Shaheed Samman Yatra, said the government had promised to provide land for a memorial honouring farmers who died during the agitation when the protest was called off, but no concrete steps had been taken so far.He demanded around 12 acres in the Bahadurgarh area for the memorial, saying the land, which had been discussed earlier, should be allotted for the purpose.During the march, the farmers peacefully reached the designated site near Pillar No. 750 at the Tikri Border, crossing barricades along the route. Sisar warned that failure to address their demands could force the farmers to launch another prolonged agitation, holding the government and administration responsible.

headline: Panchayat funds in Haryana hit by multi-crore cyber fraud
content: The cyber theft of development funds belonging to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) in Haryana has assumed alarming proportions, with suspected fraudulent withdrawals running into several crores of rupees across multiple districts. Authorities at the state headquarters and district levels are scrutinising bank transactions to establish the total amount siphoned off.Preliminary findings suggest that cybercriminals breached the state-level mother account maintained by the Development and Panchayats Department after the State Finance Commission (SFC) released grants for Zila Parishads, Panchayat Samitis and gram panchayats.In Hisar district, officials have identified suspicious transactions involving approximately Rs 7.30 crore linked to 43 gram panchayats, nine Panchayat Samitis and the Zila Parishad. Records from Narnaund and Agroha blocks are still awaited. A three-member team has been examining bank accounts and transactions for the past six months to ascertain the extent of the suspected fraud.Sources said the hackers allegedly exploited the payment mechanism of the Haryana Government's SNA-SPARSH portal, a unified digital platform for processing government scheme funds.According to preliminary information, the cybercriminals targeted the mother account at the headquarters instead of individual linked accounts of panchayats and other rural bodies.The SFC grants are routed through a Punjab National Bank account in Chandigarh, with linked accounts at the district level. Under the established procedure, digital payments require authentication and approval through dongles issued to authorised district officials.Officials probing the matter in Hisar said the suspected withdrawals appeared to have bypassed the usual approval mechanism, raising serious questions about the security of the payment system.Similar reports of suspected cyber theft have emerged from Kaithal, Sirsa, Fatehabad, Panipat, Jind, Ambala and other districts.The SFC released the grants on November 7, while the suspected fraudulent transactions reportedly took place between November 11 and 15.Bhagwan Das, president of the Sarpanch Association, Hisar, said his village panchayat had received a grant of Rs 43 lakh, which was allegedly withdrawn by cybercriminals within five days.The total loss across Haryana is yet to be established as district authorities continue to verify the accounts and transactions.

headline: Haryana Congress remembers freedom fighter Chaudhary Ranbir
content: Haryana Congress in-charge Sanjay Dutt, state Congress president Rao Narender Singh and MP Deepender Hooda on Thursday paid floral tributes to freedom fighter and member of the Constituent Assembly of India, which framed the Indian Constitution, Ch Ranbir Singh on his birth anniversary at his memorial in Kheri Sadh village. They recalled his contribution to the freedom struggle, nation-building and farmers’ welfare on the occasion, which coincided with Constitution Day.Dutt said Ch Ranbir Singh dedicated his life to the Freedom Movement, nation-building and public service. After enduring imprisonment during the freedom struggle, he contributed to the framing of the Constitution as a member of the Constituent Assembly. He also raised the demand for minimum support price (MSP) for farmers as early as 1948.“Ch Ranbir Singh had served in seven different constitutional houses, including the Constituent Assembly, Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha and the legislatures of undivided Punjab and Haryana. His contributions as a minister and founding general secretary of the Bharat Krishak Samaj remained significant,” he added.Rao Narender called on people to pledge themselves to upholding constitutional values of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity. He also launched a scathing attack on the state government over the law and order situation, alleging that criminals were operating fearlessly even near police establishments while the government had failed to rein them in, creating a sense of insecurity among people across the state.Deepender, grandson of Ch Ranbir Singh, said the ideals for which the freedom fighters had sacrificed their lives were enshrined in the Constitution. He alleged that the Constitution was facing attacks and asserted that the Congress would not allow its values to be compromised. He described his grandfather’s Gandhian principles as a lasting source of moral guidance.Recalling Ch Ranbir Singh’s contribution to the Bhakra-Nangal project, Deepender said he played an important role in its development to ensure irrigation water and electricity for the farmers and other sections of society.“Ch Ranbir Singh, who never bowed before the atrocities of British rule, spent several crucial years of his life in eight different jails, four of which are now in India and four in Pakistan. He was the only person to have served as a member of seven different legislative and constitutional bodies. This remarkable achievement has been duly recognised in the Limca Book of Records,” the MP pointed out.A prayer meeting was also organised, where local dignitaries paid tributes to the freedom fighter.

headline: Illegal structure linked to drug offender razed in Amritsar
content: The Amritsar Municipal Corporation, with assistance from the city police, on Thursday demolished an allegedly illegal property belonging to a habitual drug offender in Anngarh, taking the number of such demolition drives in the city to 30.The property belonged to Sukhdev Singh, alias Akash (28), a resident of Fakir Singh Colony in Anngarh, who is allegedly involved in drug-related activities.Deputy Commissioner of Police Ravinderpal Singh Sandhu said the Commissionerate Police assisted the civic body and made elaborate security arrangements to maintain law and order during the demolition drive.He said Sukhdev had six FIRs registered against him, including five under the NDPS Act, besides facing three preventive actions. The cases were registered between 2020 and 2026, with the latest NDPS case dating back to February 27 this year. He was released from jail on April 8.Meanwhile, the DCP said that under the state government’s anti-drug campaign, ‘Yudh Nashian Virudh’, the city police registered 1,813 NDPS cases and arrested 2,844 persons in Amritsar district between January 1 and November 25.The police also seized 170.102 kg of heroin, 12.466 kg of methamphetamine (ICE), drug money worth Rs 98.23 lakh and 62 vehicles during the period.

headline: HP puts a price on its water
content: The Himachal Pradesh Government has approved a uniform pricing policy for supplying surplus raw water to neighbouring states and various government agencies, aiming to ensure transparent valuation of the state’s water resources while safeguarding its long-term financial interests.Under the policy, a benchmark rate of Rs 100 per 1,000 cubic feet of raw water has been fixed. The rate will be revised periodically in accordance with the wholesale price index (WPI) to ensure that the economic value of water keeps pace with prevailing price levels. However, the policy will not apply to water used for domestic purposes within the state.Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said water was among Himachal Pradesh’s most valuable natural assets and its economic worth must be duly recognised in any arrangement involving the supply of surplus water to other states or agencies.He said the policy would establish a transparent and uniform mechanism for determining water rates and their periodic revision, ensuring that the state received appropriate economic returns from its resources. The government was committed to protecting Himachal’s natural wealth and securing its financial interests, he added.The policy will cover all existing and future projects in Himachal Pradesh from which surplus raw water is supplied to other states or eligible agencies. It also provides a standard pricing framework for inter-state multipurpose and water-storage projects, including the proposed Kishau Multipurpose Project and Renuka Dam Project.Sukhu said the availability of surplus water would be assessed only after safeguarding the state’s own requirements. Drinking water, irrigation, agriculture, environmental protection and developmental needs would remain the government’s foremost priorities before any surplus was made available to other states.The policy assumes significance in the context of the Kishau Multipurpose Project, under which Himachal Pradesh has been allocated 3.154 per cent of the dam’s live storage, equivalent to approximately 42 million cubic metres (MCM).The state also has an allocated share of Yamuna waters under the memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed among the Upper Yamuna Basin states. The agreement envisages the development of the Lakhwar, Kishau and Renuka projects for optimum utilisation of the basin’s water resources.The new pricing framework is expected to provide a uniform basis for valuing surplus water and ensure that Himachal Pradesh’s interests are protected in future inter-state water-sharing arrangements.

headline: Social reform: Rs 11,000 ‘shagun’ for a wedding without liquor
content: An initiative to promote alcohol-free wedding celebrations and discourage the growing culture of alcohol consumption at social functions is beginning to gain traction in the Jogindernagar subdivision of the Mandi district, with Block Development Committee (BDC) member Dalip Singh presenting the first Rs 11,000 incentive to a family that hosted a wedding without serving alcohol.The initiative took a significant step forward on November 25, when a wedding ceremony in Khajur village was celebrated without alcohol. Encouraged by the family’s decision to keep the occasion alcohol-free, Dalip Singh honoured his commitment by handing over Rs 11,000 to the family as a token of appreciation and encouragement.Dalip Singh said the initiative was aimed at encouraging families, particularly those from economically weaker and middle-income backgrounds, to organise weddings without alcohol and resist the social pressure to serve liquor during celebrations.He also revealed that another family in the area had recently organised an alcohol-free wedding. However, the family politely declined the incentive, saying that they were happy to support the initiative and did not require the monetary reward. Their decision, he said, was equally encouraging and reflected a growing willingness among families to embrace a healthier and more socially responsible approach to wedding celebrations.Dalip Singh had announced the initiative in August during a gram sabha meeting held at Main Bharola gram panchayat. Under his pledge, he promised to provide Rs 11,000 from his Army pension as a ‘shagun’ to poor and middle-income families in his area that organise weddings without serving alcohol.The Tribune had carried a story titled: ‘Cash reward for liquor free wedding in Mandi’ on August 6, which became viral on social media, and the message of Dalip Singh reached the grassroots level.Dalip believes that serving liquor at wedding ceremonies has increasingly become a social trend, often adding to unnecessary expenditure and encouraging the consumption of intoxicating substances. In many cases, families feel compelled to serve alcohol due to social expectations, even when it places an additional financial burden on them.According to Dalip Singh, promoting alcohol-free weddings could help discourage substance abuse, encourage responsible celebrations and allow families to organise ceremonies in accordance with their financial capacity, without being influenced by social pressure.A former Indian Army personnel, Dalip Singh, was elected BDC member from Ward No. 9 Tikru in the Jogindernagar subdivision. His ward comprises Ropri Klehdu, Main Bharola and Tikru gram panchayats.Associated with Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh activities since childhood, he is also an active member of Seva Bharati. After being elected a BDC member, he pledged to dedicate the honorarium received during his five-year tenure to serving needy people through Seva Bharati.The initiative is now drawing attention as a grassroots effort to promote social responsibility, discourage alcohol consumption and encourage families to celebrate weddings in a simpler, healthier and more financially prudent manner. The first reward has given the campaign a practical start, with hopes that more families in the area will come forward to organise alcohol-free wedding ceremonies.

headline: Dharamsala to host NZC meet on Dec 20
content: Dharamsala is set to emerge as the centre of inter-state deliberations on December 20, when it hosts the 33rd meeting of the Northern Zonal Council, bringing together representatives of eight states and Union Territories to discuss issues of common concern and strengthen coordination with the Centre.Union Home Minister Amit Shah will chair the meeting, which will be attended by representatives of Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh and Chandigarh. Kangra Deputy Commissioner Hemraj Bairwa said preparations for the high-level meeting were underway in Dharamsala.Organised through the Inter-State Council Secretariat under the Union Ministry of Home Affairs, the Northern Zonal Council serves as an advisory platform for the Centre and member states to deliberate on issues involving two or more states and Union Territories and explore coordinated solutions.While the Union Home Minister is its chairperson, the chief minister of one of the member states serves as vice-chairperson on a rotational basis. The meeting is expected to take up a wide range of issues, including narcotics trafficking, cybercrime, inter-state boundary disputes, power-related matters and coordination among law enforcement agencies. Other subjects likely to figure in the discussions include cases under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, emergency response services, the E-Zero FIR initiative, food safety and access to banking services.Himachal Pradesh is expected to have a significant stake in the deliberations, particularly on matters requiring cooperation with neighbouring states.The meeting will also provide an opportunity for participating states and UTs to flag pending issues with the Centre and seek time-bound, coordinated solutions to challenges that cut across administrative and geographical boundaries.

headline: Haryana CM Saini takes charge of Civil Aviation portfolio
content: Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini has taken charge of the Department of Civil Aviation, with Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Vipul Goel relieved of the portfolio, according to a notification issued by the Haryana Government.The notification says the Governor made the change on the advice of the Chief Minister. The allocation takes effect immediately.Goel will continue to hold the portfolios of Revenue and Disaster Management, and Urban Local Bodies.The notification was signed by Vijay Kumar Bhavikatti, Secretary to the Governor, and Chief Secretary Anurag Rastogi.The notification does not give a reason for the re-allocation. Haryana has been pushing to expand its air connectivity, and the Civil Aviation Department oversees airport and aviation-related development in the state.During the special session of the Haryana Legislative Assembly on Thursday, Goel was seen talking to Saini. Thereafter, he left the House.

headline: Amritsar’s Khalsa College confers 1,497 degrees at 120th convocation
content: At the 120th annual convocation of historic Khalsa College on Thursday, 1,497 degrees were awarded to the graduate and post-graduate students. The chief guest Satyajit Singh Majithia, Chancellor of Khalsa University (KU) and president of Khalsa College Governing Council (KCGC), in his convocational address, coaxed the students to adopt new technologies like Artificial Intelligence (AI) but make sure their own thinking and creativity remains intact.Majithia while congratulating the students on earning degrees, said AI is affecting various aspects of life including education and making working considerably easier. “The AI is a highly useful technology and its proper utilisation can help save time and acquire new knowledge. However, we must be cautious of becoming entirely dependent on AI,” he said.Accompanied by KU pro-chancellor Rajinder Mohan Singh Chhina, VC Mehal Singh and Principal Atam Randhawa, he also awarded gold medals and honours to the meritorious students. He also emphasised that AI can assist us, but it cannot replace our own ideas, experiences and decision-making abilities.“Excessive and unnecessary dependence on AI may adversely affect our capacity to think and learn independently,” he stated.Chhina, meanwhile, said education does not stop by getting the degree and we must continue to imbibe knowledge, enhance skills and intellectual abilities throughout life. He also said Khalsa College, since its inception, has consistently promoted education, moral values, culture and social responsibility.Mehal Singh said that in today’s competitive era, the purpose of education is not merely to obtain a degree but also to develop knowledge, skills, confidence and a sense of responsibility among students. Atam Singh Randhawa presented the annual report, highlighting the college’s achievements in academics, sports, cultural activities, research and other fields.

headline: Himachal Pradesh Police take Constitution Day pledge in Shimla
content: Himachal Pradesh Police observed Constitution Day with a solemn ceremony at the State Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (SV&ACB) Headquarters in Shimla. Police officers and personnel representing various ranks from the Police Headquarters (PHQ), State Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau Headquarters and Criminal Investigation Department (CID) Headquarters participated in the ceremony.Director General of Police Ashok Tewari administered the Constitution Day pledge to the assembled officers and personnel through a collective reading of the Preamble to the Constitution of India. On the occasion, police personnel reaffirmed their commitment to the fundamental constitutional principles of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity. They also pledged to uphold the dignity of every citizen and discharge their official responsibilities with honesty, integrity, impartiality and professionalism.The observance highlighted the significance of the Constitution as the supreme guiding framework for governance, democratic institutions and law enforcement agencies. It also served as a reminder of the police force's responsibility to protect citizens' constitutional rights, uphold the rule of law and ensure that public service remains guided by constitutional morality.

headline: Amended Delimitation Bill likely to be tabled in special Parliament sitting from November 30
content: The government has called for a special sitting of Parliament beginning Monday (November 30, 2026), where it is likely to table an amended Delimitation Bill. The two Houses will meet on separate dates, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced on Thursday (November 26, 2026), which is the 104th day since the Monsoon Session adjourned indefinitely on August 13. Lok Sabha sittings will begin on November 30 and Rajya Sabha sittings on December 2. Both Houses will conclude on December 3. The last record of a session of Parliament continuing unprorogued was in 2008, when it went on for 87 days. Parliament’s monsoon session remains unprorogued for record 88 days storyline 1 The Union Cabinet will meet on Friday (November 27, 2026) to clear the amended legislation. According to sources, three crucial changes are being introduced: a uniform 50% increase in the share of Lok Sabha seats; extending the freeze for 25 years on using the 1971 Census as the basis to determine the proportional strength of each State in the Lok Sabha; and third, using the 2011 Census for redrawing constituencies within each State. This replicates the formula brought by the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government in the Constitution (Eighty-fourth Amendment) Act, 2001. Reacting to the announcement, Congress general secretary (communication) Jairam Ramesh said the Narendra Modi government announced the session “after 105 days of operation lotus” in the hope of getting a “super-tainted” two-thirds majority to get the Bill passed. “Can there be a great insult to and assault on the Constitution,” he asked in a post on X, noting that the announcement came on Constitution Day. Congress general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal took to X to describe the attempt to pass the Delimitation Bill as “sansad chori”. “To orchestrate this murder of the Constitution on Constitution Day shows how badly they want to mock our precious democratic system. We will not allow this to pass,” Mr. Venugopal said. Changed numbers Since April, when the legislative package, including the Delimitation Bill, was defeated by a united Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the seat arithmetic in the House has changed. Twenty TMC MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA. TMC challenged the split, which is currently under Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla’s review. The NCPI faction, on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), 84 days after TMC’s challenge, submitted replies to Mr. Birla, defending its decision and asserting that the move did not violate any parliamentary or constitutional provisions. Six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena. Following the recent alliance between the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), the lone SAD MP is also expected to vote with the government. It is also learnt that the YSR Congress, which has four MPs in the Lok Sabha, will extend support to the government on the Bill. Parliament’s monsoon session remains unprorogued for record 88 days Parliament’s monsoon session remains unprorogued for record 88 days As of November 9, 2026 morning, neither the Lok Sabha nor the Rajya Sabha had been formally prorogued, keeping open the possibility of convening an extended sitting of the existing session Parliament’s monsoon session remains unprorogued for record 88 days storyline 1 ‘For the nation’s good’ In this evolving situation, all eyes are on the DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), with eight. Senior NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule, on Thursday (November 26, 2026), told reporters that pre-emptively opposing the law before its draft was made public was not a good move. “First let the bill come. Let the entire bill come into our hands. When the bill is in our hands, then we will all talk about it, and if the bill is good for the nation, we might support it,” she said. She further added that there have been instances in the past when the Opposition has supported the government on matters of national importance and key reforms. DMK’s dilemma The DMK, meanwhile, has not made any public remarks on the issue. Though, as per sources, the government has reached out to the party informally. A dominant section of the DMK is leaning towards the argument that not supporting the present constitutional amendment could mean further reduced representation for Tamil Nadu. “The freeze under Articles 81 and 82, which prevents the readjustment of seats allotted to each State in the Lok Sabha, has an inbuilt sunset clause. It provides that the freeze shall cease to operate once the relevant figures of the first Census undertaken after 2026 are published. If a constitutional amendment is not brought, the freeze will automatically lapse,” Swapnil Tripathi, who leads Charkha, Centre for Constitutional Law at the Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy, explained. If the post-2026 Census figures are taken into consideration, a top DMK leader argued, the State could end up losing as many as 12 seats in the Lok Sabha. “We are for a fair delimitation,” a top DMK leader said. Political arithmetic A senior NDA leader said the government is confident of the support of at least 358 MPs, just two short of the required strength if all 540 MPs are present and voting. In April, during the Bill’s previous outing, 528 members were present and voted, with 298 voting in favour and 230 against. In the Rajya Sabha, the NDA has 152 MPs and is within striking distance of the two-thirds majority, which stands at 164 if the entire house is present and voting.

headline: Register live-in relationship or face jail, recommends Haryana law commission
content: Mandatory registration of live-in relationships, prohibition of multiple marriages and uniform provisions governing divorce, maintenance and succession are among the key recommendations of the Haryana State Law Commission in its report on the proposed Uniform Civil Code (UCC).The report, submitted at the Haryana Government's request, proposes that partners in a live-in relationship must submit a declaration to the Registrar or Sub-Registrar having jurisdiction over their place of residence. Following a summary inquiry, the declaration will be entered in a prescribed register and a certificate issued. A copy will also be sent to the local police station. If either partner is below 21 years of age, their parents or guardians will be informed.Commission chairperson Justice HS Bhalla confirmed that the report had been submitted. Chief Secretary Anurag Rastogi said on Thursday that the government would seek the opinions of the Advocate General and the Legal Remembrancer before proceeding further.Under the recommendations, registration of a live-in relationship will be refused if either partner is already married, is in another live-in relationship or is a minor. Relationships involving consent obtained through force, coercion, fraud, misrepresentation or undue influence will also be ineligible for registration.Either or both partners can terminate the relationship by submitting a prescribed declaration. Staying in a live-in relationship for more than a month without submitting the mandatory statement could attract imprisonment of up to three months, a fine of up to Rs 10,000, or both. Obtaining consent through force or fraud could invite imprisonment of up to five years and a fine.The report also provides for a woman to seek maintenance from a competent court if deserted by her live-in partner.Marriage and divorceThe proposed code prohibits polygamy by allowing marriage only when neither partner has a living spouse. It also makes marriage registration mandatory and prohibits marriages between first cousins on both maternal and paternal sides. Exceptions to other prohibited relationships may be allowed where recognised customs permit them, subject to public policy and morality.A marriage may be annulled on grounds including non-consummation, forced or fraudulent consent, and misrepresentation of identity. Divorce may be granted on grounds of adultery, cruelty, desertion for at least two years and conversion to another religion. Existing polygamous marriages solemnised before the UCC comes into force have also been addressed in the proposed provisions.The report proposes permanent alimony and maintenance based on the financial circumstances of both parties or their mutual agreement. 'Mahr, dower, streedhan' and other property given to the wife would be additional to her maintenance claim.It also allows divorced spouses to remarry each other without any condition requiring either to marry a third person first.The proposed code would override conflicting personal laws, customs and traditions, with violations of its divorce provisions attracting imprisonment of up to three years and a fine. Scheduled Tribes have been exempted.Uttarakhand and Goa already have a Uniform Civil Code in force, while Gujarat, Assam and Madhya Pradesh have taken steps towards similar legislation. Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on Thursday that all BJP-ruled states would implement the UCC. The state government’s next step will be to examine the Law Commission's recommendations and obtain legal opinion. The proposals are recommendations and have not yet become law.

headline: Governor releases two books on Himachal’s heritage
content: Governor Kavinder Gupta released two recently published books authored by KR Bharti, a retired IAS officer and noted author from Himachal Pradesh, at Lok Bhavan here today.Speaking on the occasion, the Governor appreciated KR Bharti's efforts to document Himachal Pradesh's cultural heritage and promote literary appreciation of regional writing. He observed that such works play an important role in preserving the state's rich traditions, literary legacy and cultural identity. He said the books would be useful for researchers, students preparing for competitive examinations, cultural enthusiasts and general readers.The first book, Fairs and Festivals of Himachal Pradesh, is an extensively researched account of the state's traditional fairs and festivals. It explores their historical origins, folklore, rituals, religious significance and vibrant community traditions, offering readers an insight into the rich and diverse cultural heritage of Himachal Pradesh.The second book presents a critical review and literary analysis of Hindi short stories written by authors associated with Himachal Pradesh. It pays tribute to the literary contributions of eminent writers such as Chandradhar Sharma Guleri and Yashpal, whose works have left an enduring imprint on Hindi literature. Bridging the literary past with the present, the book also critically examines the works of 19 prominent contemporary Himachali short-story writers.KR Bharti is a noted Himachali author who has authored 11 books in Hindi and English so far.

headline: Haryana Governor Ghosh leads Constitution Day pledge at Lok Bhavan
content: Constitution Day was observed at Haryana Lok Bhavan on Thursday, with Governor Ashim Kumar Ghosh administering a pledge to officers and staff to uphold the ideals and values enshrined in the Constitution of India.On the occasion, officers and staff of Lok Bhavan assembled in the hall for a collective reading of the Preamble to the Constitution. The Governor led the reading, with all those present joining in.Addressing the gathering, Ghosh said the Constitution guaranteed every citizen the principles of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.He said public servants must imbibe these constitutional values and perform their duties in accordance with established rules and procedures, ensuring fairness and justice for all.Secretary to the Governor Vijaykumar Bhavikatti, ADCs to the Governor Mohit Handa and Sqn Ldr P Bharat, and other officers and staff of Lok Bhavan were present on the occasion.

headline: Sports University of Haryana celebrates Constitution Day
content: The Sports University of Haryana (SUOH), Rai, celebrated the 77th Constitution Day on Thursday with a programme centred on the theme ‘Nagrik Kartavya evam Bhartiya Samvidhan’ (Citizen Duties and the Indian Constitution).Professor (Dr) Devendra Singh, Vice-Chancellor of Dr BR Ambedkar National Law University (DBRANLU), attended the event as the chief guest. Students, teaching faculty, coaches and administrative staff of SUOH and Motilal Nehru School of Sports (MNSS) participated in the programme.The event began with the ceremonial lighting of the lamp. Jasvinder Singh, Registrar of SUOH, delivered the inaugural address and highlighted the importance of constitutional values and civic responsibilities. He also spoke about the proposed Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between DBRANLU and SUOH to promote academic collaboration and research in the emerging field of sports law.Professor Devendra Singh emphasised the importance of civic duties. He said every citizen’s conscious effort to contribute to the nation’s progress represented one of the highest forms of civic responsibility.Reflecting on the making of the Indian Constitution, he said the Constituent Assembly had initially favoured a Constitution that focused primarily on citizens’ rights rather than explicitly listing their duties. However, changing circumstances made it increasingly necessary to define and emphasise citizens’ responsibilities.Referring to the 1962 Indo-China War, he said the circumstances of that period reinforced the need to give greater recognition to citizens’ responsibilities towards the nation.Dr Singh said the Constitution was not merely a document guaranteeing rights but also a guiding framework for fulfilling one’s responsibilities towards the country. He stressed that a nation’s progress and strength depended not only on citizens being aware of their rights but also on their sincere commitment to performing their duties.Professor Yogesh Chander, Dean, Academic Affairs; Professor Ashok Sharma, Dean, Physical Education and Sports; Dr Jitender Kumar; Professor RP Garg; Dr Santosh Kumar Dubey, Controller of Examinations; and Dinesh Kumari, Principal of MNSS, were among those present. Teaching, coaching and administrative staff members and students of both institutions also attended the programme.

headline: Himachal High Court takes pledge to honour Constitution
content: Constitution Day was celebrated at the Himachal Pradesh High Court on Thursday to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution of India and honour the contributions of its founding fathers. Registrar General Vikas Bhardwaj read out the Preamble to the Constitution of India in the presence of officers and officials of the High Court.Other Registrars, including Nitin Kumar, Registrar (Rules, IT and Recruitment); Harish Sharma, Registrar (Judicial); Avinash Chander, Registrar (Administration); Nishant Verma, Central Project Coordinator; Rajesh Sharma, Registrar (Accounts); and Poonam Mahajan, Registrar (Establishment), along with other officers and officials of the High Court Registry, were present on the occasion.

headline: Student assaulted in Navodaya hostel, video goes viral
content: A case of assault on a student by fellow students in the hostel of Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, Reckong Peo, in Kinnaur district, has come to light after a video of the incident went viral on social media today. In the video, a couple of students are seen threatening and assaulting a fellow student, who appears helpless as he takes the beating.The Kinnaur police have taken note of the video. SP Susheel Sharma said the school had constituted a committee to inquire into the incident. Asked about the police action, the SP said the police would await the committee’s findings, as the students involved are juveniles.It has been learnt that the assault allegedly took place a couple of months ago. The incident came to light only after the video surfaced on social media. The incident has also triggered questions on social media over the safety of students and the monitoring arrangements at the school.

headline: Haryana: Youth key to nation-building, says Arjun Ram Meghwal
content: Union Law and Justice Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal on Thursday described the youth as the country's greatest strength, urging them to utilise their knowledge, talent and energy constructively for nation-building and India's progress.He made the remarks while addressing a Constitution Day programme organised by the Centre for Constitutional Law and Transformative Studies at Dr BR Ambedkar National Law University virtually.The programme was held on the theme “The Constitution of India: From the Vision of Its Founding to Future Aspirations”.The event was held under the chairmanship of Vice-Chancellor Devinder Singh. Rekha Sharma, Member of Parliament and former chairperson of the National Commission for Women, attended the event.Rekha Sharma highlighted the historical background of the Constitution, the vision of its framers and the significance of constitutional values in strengthening democratic institutions. She observed that the Constitution was not merely a legal document but a guiding framework for building a strong, inclusive and progressive nation founded on the principles of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.

headline: Gannaur BDPO suspended over alleged irregularities
content: The Development and Panchayat Department has suspended Rajesh Tiwana, Block Development and Panchayat Officer (BDPO), Gannaur, with immediate effect amid allegations of financial irregularities, delay in departmental proceedings and non-payment of salaries to 12 water employees for five years.The suspension order, issued on Wednesday, does not specify the reasons for the action. During the suspension period, Tiwana's headquarters will be the Deputy Commissioner's office in Sonepat.According to sources, one of the complaints against the officer relates to a complaint filed by water employee Ashok Sharma on the CM Window in 2023. He had alleged that 12 employees had not received their salaries for five years and their names were not registered on the REMS portal. He also alleged that salaries were being paid to some employees without their names being uploaded on the portal.Following the complaint, a four-member committee headed by Uttam Dhaliya, Deputy Director (Panchayat), was constituted to investigate the matter. The panel submitted its report covering 14 points.Another issue reportedly concerned delays in forwarding chargesheets against four employees, including a retired employee, despite repeated reminders. The department had issued a reminder on November 18, directing the officer to submit the report within two days.As per the suspension order, Tiwana will receive subsistence allowance under Rule 83 of the Haryana Civil Services (General) Rules, 2016. He will also have to certify that he is not engaged in any other employment or business and cannot leave his headquarters without prior permission of the Director-General, Development and Panchayat Department.

headline: SJIM initiative brings smart boards, desks and water filters to Haveri government schools
content: Bengaluru: St Joseph’s Institute of Management (SJIM), Bengaluru, said it had been working to develop government schools in Hangal taluk, Haveri district, in collaboration with Loyola Vikas Kendra (LVK)..The initiative focuses on identifying school-specific requirements and supporting improvements that can directly enhance the teaching and learning environment..The interventions include classroom improvements, painting of school buildings, provision of drinking water filters, desks and benches, printers and smart boards, among other facilities..Bengaluru govt schools under scanner for jump in dropout rate.Government schools at Dasarathakoppa and Hottasahalli received support for painting work, while a drinking water filter was provided to Shiragodu Government School. .Balehalli Government School received 20 benches and 20 desks, while a printer was provided to Sringeri Government School. Smart boards have also been provided to support technology-enabled classroom learning in selected schools..“Through these efforts, we hope children in rural communities will have access to better educational facilities and opportunities,” said Rev Fr Roshan Pereira, director of St Joseph’s Institute of Management, according to a press release.

headline: Sthaneeka Bhattars make contradictory statements on the lighting of deepam
content: Madurai The Sthaneeka Bhattars of the Subramaniya Swamy Temple at Thirupparankundram gave some tense moments to the Madurai district administration by making contradictory statements on their “consent” for lighting the ceremonial lamp at the traditional spot — Deepa Mandapam — on Karthigai Deepam day. Editorial | Indefensible defiance: On Tamil Nadu and Court’s Thirupparankundram order https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/editorial/indefensible-defiance-on-tamil-nadu-and-courts-thirupparankundram-order/article71747044.ece The administration had submitted at the Supreme Court that despite its readiness to light the lamp at the deepathoon, it could not comply with the court directive as the temple’s Board of Trustees insisted on lighting the lamp only at the Deepa Mandapam, following age-old practices, customs and rituals, and agama rules. ‘Mental agony’ A statement made on November 24 by the temple’s Executive Officer, G. Selvi, had said the reasoning for lighting the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam was backed by the Bhattars. However, the next day, a letter purportedly written by the Bhattars, stating that they had not given any letter of consent on lighting the lamp on November 24, went viral on social media. They said they had given consent for lighting the lamp at the usual spot near Uchipillaiyar Temple “last year” (2025). The recent statement by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department referring to their consent, made “without consulting” them, had caused mental agony, they said. Thirupparankundram deepam row: what Sthaneeka Bhattars testified 30 years ago Thirupparankundram deepam row: what Sthaneeka Bhattars testified 30 years ago When a row broke out over lighting of Karthigai Deepam at the hill in Madurai, four Sthaneeka Bhattars of the Subramaniaswami Temple testified that the lamp had been lit at the Uchipillaiyar Temple since “time immemorial” Thirupparankundram deepam row: what Sthaneeka Bhattars testified 30 years ago storyline 1 Meanwhile, there was commotion outside the house of Swaminatha Bhattar late in the evening on Wednesday, as functionaries of the BJP and Hindu outfits arrived at the priest’s house. Temple officials too were present at the house. The BJP functionaries said the Bhattars were being “forced” to give a new letter of consent to help the officials substantiate their stand before the Supreme Court. The demonstrators were detained by the police. New letter An official of the Department said the Bhattars gave the new letter on Wednesday to the Board of Trustees. “The lighting of Karthigai Deepam has been done at the Uchipillaiyar Temple since 1996 with the cooperation of the temple authorities,” said the letter, signed by four Bhattars. However, they underlined that they were only replying to a letter written by the temple administration, seeking their opinion on this issue. They reasoned that the Utchipillaiyar Temple, the Rajagopuram, and the venue for burning chokkapanai near the 16-Pillar Mandapam lie on a straight line, and the Utchipillaiyar Temple was located right above the sanctum sanctorum. They also confirmed that they had given the same opinion “in writing” on November 7, 2013 and December 4, 2025. “The deepam is lit at the deepamandapam after getting oral or written opinion from us every year. This is in line with the agama rules and age-old Saiva customs,” they clarified.

headline: Eye on Punjab elections, AAP bats on social welfare pitch, woos women, farmers
content: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) sounded the poll bugle for the 2027 Assembly elections today, becoming the first party in Punjab to formally launch its campaign with a massive rally in Moga. Having already announced candidates for 71 of the 117 constituencies, the party is seeking an early advantage over its political rivals.Going by the swelling crowds at the Khushhaal Punjab rally, the party managed to make a strong beginning. The gathering was used to project the government’s five-year report card and set the narrative for the coming election. The party clearly put welfare delivery at the centre of its campaign, while reaching out to women and farmers.AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal and Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann made a strong case for how AAP had delivered on its electoral promises, unlike its predecessors. Free electricity, 77,000 government jobs, canal water for agriculture, the Rs 10-lakh health cover scheme and welfare assistance for women featured prominently in their speeches.Kejriwal sought to turn the election into a choice between continuity of welfare schemes and their possible withdrawal under a different government. Warning voters against the Congress, BJP and the SAD, he claimed these parties would discontinue the existing benefits if voted to power. He also alleged that in Delhi several pro-people schemes started by his government had been withdrawn after the BJP government was formed there, while cautioning voters against the BJP.Women, who constitute 48.4 per cent of Punjab’s electorate, were a particular focus. Kejriwal urged them to persuade the men in their families to vote for AAP. Beneficiaries of the Mawan-Dheeyan Satkar Yojana shared their experiences at the rally, while Mann launched the Smart Ration Card Scheme for 10 lakh beneficiaries and distributed Meri Rasoi ration kits containing essential food items along with free wheat.Farmers were another important target group. Mann reminded them of the SAD’s initial support for the three farm laws in 2020 and its subsequent withdrawal by the NDA following the farmers’ agitation. He accused the Akali Dal of betraying farmers and highlighted his government's claim that over 78 per cent of available canal water was now being used for irrigation, up from 22 per cent earlier.Mann also targeted the newly announced SAD-BJP alliance, questioning how two parties that had remained opposed to each other for six years had come together again. He described the alliance as politically motivated and predicted that it would not yield significant electoral gains. He also accused the Congress and the SAD-BJP of having failed Punjab during their combined 25 years in power.The early candidate announcements and campaign launch indicate that AAP wants to move beyond election-time mobilisation and give its candidates time to consolidate their constituencies. However, converting the rally’s crowds into votes will depend on the government’s ability to defend its record on employment, law and order, drugs, agriculture and finances -- the issues that are being raised by their political opponents.

headline: Haryana’s Gorakhpur village honours martyr on 49th birth anniversary
content: Villagers, family members and students paid tribute to Army martyr Rajesh Kumar on his 49th birth anniversary at Gorakhpur village on Thursday. Village sarpanch Mandeep Yogi attended the programme as the chief guest.The event began with floral tributes at the martyr's statue near Shaheed Rajesh Kumar Government Senior Secondary School. His parents, Balwan Singh and Kailasho Devi, also paid their respects. A havan was organised later, followed by prayers for the peace of his soul.Addressing the gathering, Mandeep Yogi said the sacrifices of martyrs should always be remembered. He added that passing on their values and ideals to future generations was the best tribute to them.Students presented patriotic songs in memory of the soldier. The programme was conducted by his brother, Sub-Inspector Rajbir Singh.According to Mandeep Yogi, Rajesh Kumar was born on November 25, 1978. After completing his education in the village, he joined the Indian Army. On July 30, 1998, he received a President's award for excellence in shooting.On October 4, 2001, he was killed while fighting infiltrators along the India-Pakistan border in the Uri sector of Jammu and Kashmir. He was just 23 years old at the time.Soldiers and students who participated in the programme were honoured by the martyr's family. School Principal Prahlad Singh, former sarpanch Joginder Singh Siwach, ex-servicemen and several villagers also attended the event.

headline: Post alliance with Akalis, BJP seeks 6 of 10 seats in Gurdaspur & Pathankot
content: As seat-sharing talks between the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) gather pace ahead of the Assembly elections, the BJP is pushing hard for six of the 10 Assembly segments spread across the twin districts of Gurdaspur and Pathankot.Pathankot, carved out of Gurdaspur as a separate district in 2011, comprises the Assembly constituencies of Sujanpur, Bhoa and Pathankot city, while the larger Gurdaspur belt includes Dinanagar, Gurdaspur, Batala, Qadian, Sri Hargobindpur, Fatehgarh Churian and Dera Baba Nanak seats.The BJP is considered the stronger partner in all three seats of Hindu-dominated Pathankot district -- Bhoa, Pathankot city and Sujanpur. The party also has a strong influence in the Dinanagar seat which falls in Gurdaspur district.Hectic lobbying is on by senior BJP leaders to ensure the Gurdaspur and Batala Assembly seats fall in the party’s kitty. Previously, when the parties were in an alliance, these two seats were contested by the Akalis.BJP leaders are asking for the Gurdaspur Assembly seat because in the 2024 parliamentary polls, Dinesh Babbu of the BJP, despite losing to Congressman Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa, bagged more than 10,000 votes than the SAD candidate from the seat. Both the parties had contested the polls separately.BJP leaders said the party had put a policy in place in which it would be given those seats in which its candidate had polled more votes than the SAD nominee during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Likewise, in the 2024 elections, from the Batala seat, the BJP candidate had polled more votes than the Akali candidate. “That is why we are demanding these two seats apart from the Bhoa, Sujanpur, Pathankot city and Dinanagar seats,” said a senior BJP leader.The Batala seat was with the BJP in 2007 till it was swapped with the Ludhiana (West) seat during the 2012 and 2017 assembly elections. Subsequently, the SAD had fielded its candidates. In 2022, the two parties had contested separately. Whatever the final decision may be, the BJP has already started its grass root campaigning in these two seats.

headline: Himachal: Police, NHAI flag safety gaps on Kangra highway
content: To improve road safety and prevent accidents, the Kangra police, in coordination with National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) officials and local representatives, conducted a joint inspection of the four-lane highway stretch from Gaggal to Kachhari on Wednesday evening. The stretch covers Rajol, Ladwara, Shahpur, 39 Mile, Mataur and Gurkhadi in Kangra district.The inspection was led by Kangra SP Kulbhushan Verma and attended by the Additional SP and local police officials, NHAI engineers and officials and representatives of the Shahpur Nagar Panchayat and the Shahpur Vyapar Mandal.Several road safety deficiencies were identified. NHAI officials were directed to install adequate traffic signboards and indicators, reflective tapes at U-turns and vulnerable spots and W-beam crash barriers on sensitive stretches. The poor condition of service lanes in Shahpur was flagged for immediate improvement.The team found several unauthorised openings and cuts along the highway that allow motorists to enter or exit from the wrong direction and recommended closing them to prevent accidents. Directions were also issued to repair damaged blinkers and warning lights and to install rumble strips near junctions, intersections and U-turns to alert motorists and regulate speed.To strengthen traffic surveillance in Shahpur town, the installation of 360-degree CCTV cameras at two strategic locations was proposed. The NHAI was also asked to start steps to install automatic speed-detection sensors and digital speed display boards to monitor speeds and ensure compliance with speed limits. The team stressed the need to widen the road at Mataur and remove encroachments obstructing traffic. The police were directed to check unauthorised roadside parking and step up challaning of traffic violators.At Kachhari Chowk, the team recommended a traffic police post or kiosk and sturdy sliding barriers to regulate vehicle movement.The SP told The Tribune that a systematic two-minute traffic-holding arrangement had been discussed to ease congestion at Kachhari Junction. “Under the proposed system, vehicles moving from the four-lane highway towards Palampur and those coming from Hamirpur towards Mataur will be released in a regulated manner through the existing two-lane stretch. The movement will be managed in phases, allowing traffic pressure on the Kachhari-Mataur road to ease before the next batch of vehicles is released,” he said.The SP apprised the NHAI and district administration officials of the deficiencies and the corrective measures proposed, and the departments concerned were directed to coordinate and ensure prompt action. He said the implementation of the proposed measures would be reviewed after 15 days.

headline: Cong marches to ‘save the Constitution’
content: The Himachal Pradesh Congress on Thursday took its campaign for the protection of the Constitution to the streets of Shimla, accusing the BJP of undermining constitutional values and attempting to weaken democratic institutions. Party leaders and workers participated in a Samvidhan Raksha March, walking from the statue of Dr BR Ambedkar at Chaura Maidan to Mahatma Gandhi’s statue at the Ridge, raising slogans against the BJP and displaying posters.The march culminated with state Congress president Vinay Kumar and AICC in-charge for Himachal Pradesh Rajni Patil administering an oath to party leaders and workers to uphold and protect the Constitution. Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu could not attend the programme as he had been unwell for the past few days, while some ministers also stayed away due to prior commitments.Addressing the gathering, Patil accused the BJP of attempting to bring democratic institutions under its control, alleging that the Election Commission of India was its latest target. She accused the BJP of stealing votes, elected legislators and governments, and said Congress leader Rahul Gandhi was leading the fight to safeguard the Constitution.“We need to strengthen his hands and fight fearlessly until the supremacy of the Constitution is restored,” she said.Raising the issue of examination paper leaks, Patil said such incidents had shattered the hopes of poor families who believed education could provide their children with a better future. She also alleged that irregularities involving donations collected for the construction of the Ram Temple had hurt the religious sentiments of devotees, questioning the BJP leadership’s silence on the matter.Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri accused the BJP of attempting to destabilise the elected Congress government in Himachal Pradesh through Operation Lotus. He said Congress workers had resisted the alleged attempts and called for a united fight to protect constitutional institutions and democratic values.

headline: Health minister Khader flays ASHA workers for striking work, says cannot abuse govt and work for it at th
content: Bengaluru: Govt is in a quandary over the demand for a pay hike by ASHA workers, whose strike in Bengaluru entered its 10th day Thursday, as any concession could have a cascading effect and trigger similar demands from employees across other departments.Chief minister DK Shivakumar Thursday said employees from 17 govt departments were seeking similar pay hikes and that a decision on hiking pay of ASHA workers could have wider financial implications for the state.Sources say a hike in ASHA workers’ remuneration could bring their earnings on a par with those of anganwadi workers, who are also seeking a similar increase.“ASHA workers’ roles are not the same as that of anganwadi workers and cannot be compared. If a decision is taken to increase their pay, it will open a Pandora’s box,” officials said.Health minister UT Khader told TOI govt was not adamant, but that workers cannot hold the state to ransom through their protest.“Our stand — that we will discuss the issue with the finance department and come back to them — is clear,” Khader said. “We are only asking for time. Is it not their duty to go back to work after the CM has assured a resolution? ASHA workers cannot abuse the govt and then continue to work for the govt. It is not fair.”On financial implications of a possible hike, Khader said the health department, in consultation with the CM and finance department, would take a decision. The opposition has pegged the additional expenditure at Rs 480 crore.Khader also questioned the significance of ASHA workers’ roles, pointing to Tamil Nadu, where there is no equivalent system of ASHA workers.“But the neighbouring state fares better on health indicators such as infant mortality rate and maternal mortality rate,” he said. “ASHA workers have not been working for the past 15 days in Karnataka, but the state’s health index has not deteriorated.”Indicating that govt could consider a revision in incentives, Khader suggested that workers could have sought an increase in performance-linked incentives instead of a hike in honorarium.“The minimum an ASHA worker receives is Rs 8,000 and those who have worked for incentives receive anywhere between Rs 12,000 to Rs 20,000. They can always seek double their incentive,” he said, adding that the final decision rested with the CM.Asked whether the health department would initiate punitive action against the striking workers, Khader said the responsibility would lie with union leaders leading the protest.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. headline: Himachal: Faith, folk traditions come alive at Rudra Maharaj fair
content: Education Minister Rohit Thakur attended the three-day district-level Rudra Maharaj Ekadashi Mela at Devthi Majhgaon in the Pachhad constituency of Sirmaur district on Thursday. He offered prayers at the Rudra Maharaj Temple before participating in the inaugural celebrations.The minister said fairs and festivals were an integral part of Himachal Pradesh’s rich cultural heritage and traditions. He said the Rudra Maharaj fair was not only an important centre of faith but also helped strengthen communal harmony and preserve age-old customs.Highlighting the importance of sports, Thakur said drug abuse had emerged as a major social challenge and that sports could play a significant role in keeping youth away from addiction. He appreciated the sports competitions organised during the fair, saying they helped develop discipline, confidence, leadership and team spirit among young people.He said four new sports hostels had been opened at Shillai, Chaupal, Ghumarwin and Mandi over the past four years, taking the total number of sports hostels in the state to 12.Speaking about education, he said 143 schools had been identified for the CBSE curriculum, while another 100 would be brought under the system in the second phase. He also highlighted Himachal Pradesh’s fifth position in the National Achievement Survey 2025 and stated that the state’s literacy rate had reached 99.5 per cent.Earlier, the minister performed the bhoomi pujan for a school playground to be constructed at a cost of Rs 53 lakh and directed officials to expedite the work. He also listened to public grievances and assured residents that their issues would be addressed in a phased manner. He announced financial assistance of Rs 50,000 from his discretionary fund for the mela organising committee and Rs 15,000 for schoolchildren participating in cultural programmes.

headline: Rally by Samyukt Kisan Morcha marks 6th anniversary of farmers’ protest
content: The Samyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM) held a rally, marking the sixth anniversary of the historic farmers’ movement here on Thursday. Thousands of farmers and workers participated in it, raising slogans against the Centre and the Punjab Government.On the nationwide call of the Samyukt Kisan Morcha, a massive rally was held in the Majha zone in front of the Deputy Commissioner’s office here. Thousands of farmers and workers from various organisations from the border districts of Amritsar, Tarn Taran, Gurdaspur and Pathankot participated in this rally.The rally began with a two-minute silence to pay tribute to the 735 farmers who passed away during the stir.Addressing the farmers and workers gathered on this occasion, various farmer leaders, including Dr Satnam Singh Ajnala, Mahavir Singh Gill, Satbir Singh Sultani, Major Singh Bhikhiwind, Master Surinder Singh, Harvinder Singh Khaira, Gurdev Singh Varpal, Pargat Singh, Rattan Singh Dhand and Gurcharan Singh Gill demanded from the Central Government to implement the demands accepted in writing during the farmers’ agitation.They demanded to enact a law to guarantee the purchase of crops above the MSP, to provide justice to the farmers killed in Lakhimpur Kheri and to withdraw the Electricity Bill. The speakers also demanded to keep the agriculture sector out of the India-US trade agreement.They also criticised the Punjab Government. Farmer leaders Rattan Singh Randhawa, Lakhbir Singh Nizampur, Jatinder Singh Chhina, Amrik Singh Sangatpura, Palwinder Singh Mathola, Dalbir Singh Bedadpur, Sucha Singh Ajnala and Jagjit Singh said that during the Kisan Morcha held in Chandigarh on September 7, the Punjab Government had made many written promises to the farmer organisations, but the government is refusing to implement them.They said on the ownership rights over the river waters of Punjab, it was promised to pass a bill in the Vidhan Sabha to repeal Articles 78, 79 and 80 of the Constitution, to get the electricity and seed laws restored. Apart from this, it was also assured of a lump sum settlement of the loans of agricultural cooperative societies and land mortgage banks. But the Punjab Government is reneging on these promises and breaking promises with the farmers’ organisations.All the speakers called upon the BJP government at the Centre and its allies as well as the Aam Aadmi Party government in Punjab to teach them a lesson in the upcoming Assembly elections.During the gathering, a demand was made from the Central Government to open the Attari-Wagah border for cross-border trade. Similarly, a demand was made from the Punjab Government to operationalise the Sheron Sugar Mill in Tarn Taran district as per its promise.

headline: Governor inspects Renuka tunnels
content: Governor Kavinder Gupta visited the Renuka Dam project site in Sirmaur district yesterday and reviewed the progress of construction work on the three diversion tunnels being developed as part of the project.The Governor interacted with project officials and reviewed different aspects of the construction work, emphasising the importance of infrastructure projects of national significance and their contribution to regional development and public welfare. He stressed the need for coordinated efforts, effective execution and sustained monitoring.General Manager of the Renuka Dam project, Anoop Sharma, briefed the Governor on the current status of the project, ongoing construction activities, achievements made so far and the future action plan.
