He also apprised him of the progress against prescribed targets and various stages of construction.The Renuka Dam project is a 40 MW multipurpose project of national importance being constructed on the Giri river in the Sirmaur district of Himachal Pradesh. Its primary objective is to provide 23 cusecs of drinking water to the National Capital Region of Delhi. The project envisages construction of a 148m-high rock-fill dam and a 40 MW powerhouse.

headline: Haryana Police to get Rs 62.40-cr tech upgrade in three months
content: The Haryana Police are set for a major technological upgrade, with the state government approving proposals worth Rs 62.40 crore for the procurement of advanced software, cyber tools and modern hardware. The procurement process is expected to be completed within three months.Next-gen policingAI team for crime analysis, suspect trackingBlockchain and dark web investigation unitsCyber commandos for emerging threatsSpecial training for cops and cyber staffStatewide database of active criminalsStronger monitoring of social media platformsDaily mapping of cybercrime hotspotsATM alert network in remote areasThe proposals were cleared at a meeting of the High-Level Purchase Committee chaired by Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini. The initiative aims to strengthen the police force's operational efficiency, improve crime detection and enhance its ability to tackle emerging cybercrime threats.Following the approval, DGP Ajay Singhal chaired a review meeting at Police Headquarters in Panchkula, where officers from various units discussed technological requirements, modernisation and capacity building.Singhal said procurement alone would not deliver the desired results unless police personnel were adequately trained to use the new resources. Specialised training programmes will, therefore, be organised at the Haryana Police Academy, Madhuban, for investigating officers, SHOs, Cyber Cell in-charges and other technical personnel.The DGP said an AI Task Force had already been constituted with three specialised modules. The first will focus on using artificial intelligence for crime prevention, identification of criminals and data analysis. The second will develop expertise in blockchain technology and dark web investigations, while the third will train personnel as cyber commandos to tackle emerging digital threats.Singhal also directed police units and districts to integrate their cyber tools and technological resources on a common platform and share best practices.The meeting stressed the need to strengthen surveillance and monitoring of social media and Meta platforms. The State Crime Branch has been assigned the task of developing a centralised database of active criminals across Haryana.Officials informed the meeting that cybercrime hotspots were being identified daily through mobile location plotting. A daily alert system has also been developed by connecting ATMs in remote areas with a technological monitoring mechanism.Superintendents of Police from Hisar and Rohtak shared details of technology being used in their districts. The meeting also reviewed the 'Achook' platform developed by Rohtak Police.

headline: Seat-sharing poses first test for reunited SAD-BJP alliance in Punjab
content: The renewed alliance between the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) might have brought back into focus the Hindu-Sikh political bonhomie in Punjab, but the narrative of reconciliation has left unresolved fault lines that led to the separation.Beneath the bonhomie, there are not only several uncomfortable questions that neither party can afford to ignore, which includes the release of Bandi Singhs, or Sikh political prisoners.In fact the past has caught up with the present. “The biggest challenge is likely to be seat-sharing. Despite being projected as the ‘Bada Bhai’ (senior partner), the SAD may have to make substantial concessions to its former junior partner, particularly in urban constituencies. Since the split, the BJP has invested in expanding its organisational base beyond its traditional strongholds in Doaba and Hindu dominated Majha region. It now has an eye on urban constituencies in Ludhiana, Patiala and Bathinda,” Prof PS Bhogal, psephologist and former professor of political science told The Tribune.The BJP has also built a cadre in several urban Assembly segments of Ludhiana, including North, East, Central, West and South, besides Sahnewal, Patiala city and Kharar. The induction of former SAD leader and two-time Kharar candidate Ranjit Singh Gill into the BJP is indicative of its efforts to strengthen its position in constituencies where the Akalis once enjoyed considerable influence.For the BJP, therefore, the alliance is not necessarily a return to the old arrangement in which it contested a limited number (23/117 seats in 2017) of seats as the junior partner. The party would expect a significantly larger share (over 50), particularly dominating the urban areas, and is unlikely to surrender constituencies where it has spent years building its organisation.However, keeping the seat-sharing formula under wraps also reflects the apprehensions within both parties. An early announcement could demoralise leaders and workers who have spent years nurturing constituencies and aspiring to contest elections on their respective party tickets.If a constituency is allotted to the alliance partner, the sidelined aspirants could either revolt, switch parties or work against the official candidate. BJP has experienced this in the recent past when former minister Tikshan Sud had criticised the leadership for making “abrupt” organisational changes.Both parties are conscious that such disgruntlement could provide an opportunity to the opposition, particularly the Congress and the AAP.The much-used criterion of ‘winnability’ is likely to become the justification for difficult decisions. Leaders from both sides have reportedly conducted internal assessments to identify candidates with the best electoral prospects.But the exercise will not be without resistance from local leaders who have invested years in building their political constituencies.There has also been public resentment from BJP leaders against Akalis. Former Union Minister of State Ravneet Singh Bittu, who is keen on contesting from Ludhiana on a BJP ticket, has earlier been a vocal critic of the SAD leadership.In February this year, Sud had accused the Akalis of failing to act against drugs, gangster culture and sacrilege incidents, alleging that certain leaders had pursued electoral gains at the cost of religious sentiments.Similarly, Amritsar MLA and former IPS officer Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, who has repeatedly accused the previous SAD government of failing to act against those responsible for sacrilege incidents, will have to share the political platform with leaders he has targeted in the past.For SAD, the alliance is equally consequential. From ruling Punjab for two consecutive terms between 2007 and 2017, the party has been reduced to the margins of state politics. Its tally fell from 15 seats in 2017 to just three in 2022.Its legislative presence has since dwindled further, with Manpreet Singh Ayali joining the Akali Dal Waris Punjab De and Dr Sukhwinder Kumar Sukhi moving to AAP. Ganieve Kaur Majithia effectively remains its lone representative in the Assembly.The party has also suffered organisational setbacks following the emergence of SAD (Punar Surjit), led by prominent Akali leaders such as Gurpartap Singh Wadala, Parminder Singh Dhindsa and Adesh Partap Singh Kairon. Several other leaders, including Surjit Singh Rakhra, Manpreet Singh Ayali, Charanjit Singh Brar and Iqbal Singh Jhundan, have also drifted away from the Akali fold.The emergence of the Akali Dal Waris Punjab De has fragmented what was once a relatively consolidated Panthic political space.

headline: Rs 2.95 crore lost as fire razes Sanghni market
content: A devastating fire swept through Sanghni market in the Salooni subdivision of Chamba district late Wednesday night, reducing six houses and seven shops to ashes and leaving 14 families homeless and without their sources of livelihood. The Revenue Department’s preliminary assessment has estimated the losses at Rs 2.95 crore.The blaze broke out around 10 pm and quickly engulfed the wooden multi-storey buildings lining the market, leaving residents and shopkeepers with little time to salvage their belongings. A grocery depot, a medical store, a makeshift shop and two vans were also destroyed in the inferno.Panic gripped the area after a gas cylinder exploded amid the raging flames, further intensifying the blaze. Local residents, assisted by personnel from the Sanghni police post, made desperate efforts to contain the fire. However, residents alleged that the Fire Department reached the spot nearly two-and-a-half hours after being alerted. By then, the flames had already consumed a substantial part of the market. It took nearly five hours to bring the fire under control. A short circuit at a fast-food shop is suspected to have triggered the blaze, though the exact cause is yet to be ascertained.The preliminary assessment by the Revenue Department indicates that all 14 affected families have suffered complete losses. Besides residential properties, the fire destroyed shops and goods belonging to tenants and small traders, dealing a severe blow to the local trading community.Officiating Salooni SDM Anil Bhardwaj said an administrative team led by the Tehsildar was dispatched immediately after the incident was reported and a preliminary assessment of the damage had been completed.He said the 14 affected families had suffered losses estimated at Rs 2.95 crore. Relief cases were being prepared, and the administration would provide immediate relief and financial assistance to the affected families as per the prescribed rules.

headline: Himachal: Ultrasound facility starts at Shillai hospital
content: Residents of the remote Shillai Assembly constituency in Sirmaur district will no longer have to travel to Paonta Sahib, Nahan, Solan, Shimla or Dehradun for ultrasound examinations, as Industries, Parliamentary Affairs, Labour and Employment Minister Harshwardhan Chauhan on Thursday inaugurated an ultrasound facility at the Civil Hospital, Shillai.The facility meets a decades-old demand of the people of the region and is expected to provide considerable relief, particularly to pregnant women and patients who earlier had to travel long distances and spend thousands of rupees for the test.The service became operational on Thursday. Until a regular sonologist is appointed at the hospital, Dr Shashi Kant, sonologist at the Civil Hospital, Paonta Sahib, will visit Shillai on deputation every Monday and Tuesday to conduct ultrasound examinations free of cost.“Providing accessible and quality healthcare to people living in remote and geographically challenging areas remains a priority of the government. The commencement of ultrasound services at Shillai Civil Hospital will save patients considerable time, travel and expenditure, particularly benefiting pregnant women. We are committed to strengthening healthcare infrastructure and ensuring that people receive essential medical facilities closer to their homes,” Chauhan said.The minister also inspected the under-construction hospital building and reviewed the quality of the ongoing work. He directed the Public Works Department (PWD) officials to expedite construction and complete the project within the stipulated time so that residents could benefit at the earliest.He took note of the hospital management’s requirements and assured support, including equipment for eye care, two monitors and a defibrillator for the emergency ward, a diesel generator and a vehicle for vaccination drives.The Civil Hospital, Shillai, currently has specialists in gynaecology, orthopaedics, ophthalmology, general medicine, general surgery and anaesthesiology, besides five medical officers (MBBS). The government has also issued posting orders for a paediatrician, who is expected to join the hospital shortly.

headline: NGT flags organic pollution at 2 Ashwani khud locations
content: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) has flagged elevated organic pollution at two locations on Ashwani khud and its tributaries in Shimla, directing the Himachal Pradesh State Pollution Control Board (HPSPCB) to intensify its investigation and identify the sources of contamination.The directions were issued by a Bench headed by Justice Prakash Shrivastava, Chairperson, and Dr Afroz Ahmad, Expert Member, while hearing a matter concerning pollution in Ashwani khud following a news report. The tribunal took note of a comprehensive report submitted by the HPSPCB on November 16, which identified potential pollution sources, sewage and wastewater discharge pathways and 25 water-quality monitoring locations across the catchment.The board had collected water samples from 25 locations on September 29, 30 and October 1, which were analysed at its NABL-accredited State Board Laboratory in Shimla. The monitoring covered Ashwani khud and several tributaries, including Jagroti nullah, Bhattakufer nullah, Churath nullah, Lift nullah, Kasumpti nullah and Koti nullah.The report revealed significantly elevated biological oxygen demand (BOD) levels at two locations on Lift nullah near Combermere, where readings stood at 16 mg/L and 22.4 mg/L against the prescribed limit of 3 mg/L. The tribunal observed that the high readings indicated increased organic pollution loads and warranted further investigation into possible wastewater discharges. At the remaining 23 monitoring locations, BOD levels were within the prescribed limit.The sample collected from the Municipal Corporation slaughterhouse at Krishna Nagar also recorded a pH value of 9.80, exceeding the permissible range of 5.5 to 9.0. The establishment is stated to be connected to the Lalpani sewage treatment plant.The HPSPCB report also recorded faecal coliform concentrations of 920 MPN/100 ml in Lift Nullah before its confluence with Ashwani khud and 540 MPN/100 ml in Ashwani khud downstream of the confluence. Although the board reported these readings to be within applicable limits, the tribunal called for continued scrutiny of the pollution sources.The NGT directed the pollution control board to continue its source-identification exercise, particularly at locations showing elevated BOD and faecal coliform levels. It ordered that appropriate remedial and regulatory action be initiated wherever violations or unauthorised discharges are established.The tribunal also granted two weeks to the Jal Shakti Department and Shimla Jal Prabandhan Nigam Limited (SJPNL) to submit a progress report on the construction and laying of the sewage network.During the hearing, SJPNL’s law officer sought permission to withdraw a statement made before the tribunal on September 1, 2026, explaining that it had been submitted inadvertently without complete information and tendering an apology. The Tribunal allowed the request. The matter has been listed for the next hearing on March 5, 2027.

headline: Click, not queue: Travel agents seek online permits for foreign tourists
content: The Himachal Pradesh Travel Agents’ Association (HPTAA) has urged the state government to simplify the Protected Area Permit (PAP) process for foreign tourists visiting remote Himalayan destinations, particularly Lahaul-Spiti and Kinnaur, by introducing an online permit facility and decentralising the powers to issue permits.In a representation submitted to Himachal Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation (HPTDC) Chairman RS Bali, the association has proposed that the SDM office at Manali and other designated authorities be empowered to issue PAPs through an online system, eliminating the need for foreign tourists to visit government offices in person.HPTAA president Hira Lal Rana said the existing system, under which foreign nationals have to approach SDM offices at Kaza, Reckong Peo and Rampur to obtain permits, often causes inconvenience. The problem becomes particularly acute during weekends and government holidays, when tourists travelling through remote mountain regions may find it difficult to access the designated offices, disrupting their travel schedules and itineraries.Rana said extending permit-issuing powers to Manali and introducing online processing would reduce administrative hurdles, improve accessibility and make travel to restricted and remote areas more convenient for international visitors.He said Himachal Pradesh had immense potential to attract foreign tourists with its spectacular high-altitude landscapes, Buddhist monasteries, heritage villages, indigenous cultures and distinctive Himalayan experiences. However, cumbersome administrative procedures could affect the overall visitor experience and the state’s competitiveness as an international tourism destination.Lahaul-Spiti and Kinnaur, in particular, attract travellers seeking remote mountain experiences, Buddhist heritage and indigenous cultural traditions. Simplifying travel formalities would make these destinations more accessible while strengthening the state’s tourism potential.The PAP-related demand is part of a broader set of recommendations submitted by the association to promote spiritual, cultural, heritage and sustainable tourism in Himachal Pradesh.Other proposals include developing integrated tourism circuits, installing multilingual QR-code-based information systems at heritage sites, regulating commercial solicitation on Manali Mall Road, taking action against unauthorised travel operators and preserving the state’s cultural identity.The association has urged the government to consider its recommendations and strengthen tourism infrastructure, administrative coordination and visitor-friendly services across the state.

headline: Tamil Nadu Government staff to get 15-day paternity leave: CM Vijay
content: Tamil Nadu CM Joseph Vijay on Thursday announced a 15-day paternity leave for married government employees.Following the announcement, the Tamil Nadu Government issued a formal order outlining the details. Eligible employees may avail of this leave either 15 days prior to the expected due date or within six months from the child's birth, enabling them to be with their spouses during childbirth, according to a press release.Currently, female government employees are entitled to 365 days of maternity leave, a policy reflecting the high priority accorded to motherhood and child welfare. Citing this existing entitlement, male staff members had submitted requests seeking a similar provision for fathers, as per the release.The period surrounding delivery is an extremely important phase for both mother and child. During this critical time, a father's presence is essential not only to provide physical and emotional support to his wife, but also to assist in looking after the newborn, said the release.According to the government, extending this facility would help couples share family responsibilities more equitably, ensure active paternal involvement in early childcare and ease the transition for working families across the state.

headline: Meritorious candidates wrongly declared unfit deserve review: Punjab and Haryana HC
content: Meritorious candidates denied appointment on the basis of an inconclusive or erroneous medical assessment should be given another opportunity to undergo medical examination at a reputed institution, the Punjab and Haryana High Court has observed.The Bench made it clear that that a candidate's hard-earned success in a competitive examination should not be undone by one medical examination.Justice Sudeepti Sharma observed that medical examination was the last stage of the selection process and the doctors and institutions examining selected candidates needed to be highly competent, as the issuance of appointment letters depended on medical clearance."Such meritorious candidates should not suffer because of lack of knowledge/ability of the medical boards constituted by the medical institutions, where the candidates are sent for medical examination," Justice Sharma observed.The court further observed that candidates medically declared unfit for appointment should be given one opportunity to get themselves medically examined by another reputed institution so that they did not suffer because of the lack of ability or knowledge of medical institutions or boards constituted by recruiting agencies and departments.The observations came while dealing with a petition filed by Harmanpreet Sodhi, who had secured All India Rank 385 among 958 candidates recommended for appointment in the Civil Services Examination, 2025. He had also secured the sixth rank in the PwBD category.Sodhi had appeared in the examination under the low-vision category and cleared the preliminary examination, mains and personality test, securing an aggregate of 967 marks. However, his appointment was withheld after the Standing Medical Board's Benchmark Disability Expert Panel at AIIMS, New Delhi, issued a report dated July 27, declaring him unfit under the PwBD category and unfit for all services.Justice Sharma took note of the fact that the same institution had assessed Sodhi as having 60 per cent permanent disability on account of low vision during the Civil Services Examination, 2023. The subsequent assessment, however, could not determine the percentage of his visual disability.Finding major discrepancies in the medical examination reports issued by the same hospital, Justice Sharma had, through an order dated August 21, directed the Director of PGIMER, Chandigarh, to constitute a board of doctors specialising in ophthalmology to medically examine Sodhi in accordance with UPSC norms.The court had also directed that one post to which the petitioner would be entitled according to his rank be kept reserved till the decision of the writ petition.The PGIMER board subsequently examined Sodhi and, in its report dated November 18, assessed his ocular disability at 60 per cent and permanent.Justice Sharma observed that the PGIMER report falsified the reason for rejecting the candidate's claim for appointment. The court noted that the petitioner was a meritorious candidate who had cleared the written examination with a very good rank despite his disability.Justice Sharma emphasised that recruiting agencies and medical boards constituted by institutions to examine selected candidates needed to be very careful while preparing their reports. The court pointed out that while a meritorious candidate waited for a decision, his age did not await him, potentially rendering him ineligible to apply for further opportunities.In view of the facts and circumstances, the court directed the respondents to appoint Sodhi forthwith in accordance with the rank obtained by him. It, however, clarified that his appointment would remain subject to the final outcome of the writ petition.

headline: From Guru Ram Das to Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar’s story unfolds on stage
content: Amritsar’s 450-year journey is not merely a chronicle of its founding and growth, but a story of faith, sacrifice, resilience and cultural coexistence. This layered identity found an evocative theatrical expression in ‘Dastaan-e-Amritsar’, a light and sound production presented at Guru Nanak Dev University as part of the celebrations marking the 450th anniversary of Amritsar.Conceived as a part of Prof Karamjeet Singh’s initiative of Global Conclave and developed by eminent playwright and director Kewal Dhaliwal, the nearly one-hour-and-45-minute production emerged as the highlight of the two-day celebrations.Presented by Manch-Rangmanch at the university’s Dasmesh Auditorium, the play traces the city’s evolution from its foundation to the present, bringing together episodes that have shaped its spiritual, political, literary and social landscape.The narrative draws upon the contributions of Sri Guru Ram Das, Sri Guru Arjan Dev and Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib, alongside the presence of Sai Mian Mir and the martyrdom of Baba Deep Singh. Stories associated with Bibi Rajni, Bhai Mani Singh, Sukha Singh and Mehtab Singh added to the historical tapestry, while the freedom struggle and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre underline the city’s enduring association with resistance and sacrifice. It also portrayed historical episodes associated with Bhai Mani Singh, Sukha Singh and Mehtab Singh, Bibi Rajni, and the role of Amritsar’s martyrs in the freedom struggle.The sacrifices of Madan Lal Dhingra, Mewa Singh Lopoke, Baba Gurdit Singh, Sohan Singh Bhakna and Shaheed Udham Singh were also highlighted, along with the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.Yet, the production moves beyond monumental history. “It’s portrayal of the traditional markets within Amritsar’s 12 gates, old newspapers, educational institutions, temples, mosques and churches brings out the city’s everyday character. I researched and worked on the naunces to include correct history, one that shaped generations and gave a distinct character to Amritsar,” said Dhaliwal, who has previously worked on theatrical sagas of Jallianwala Bagh and Saragarhi.The literary legacy of Bhai Vir Singh, Dhani Ram Chatrik, Nanak Singh and Saadat Hasan Manto, alongside Bhagat Puran Singh’s work at Pingalwara, were included to reflect Amritsar’s contribution to intellectual and social life.Its cultural canvas extends to Punjab Naatshala, Virsa Vihar, traditional cuisine, festivals and kite-flying at Gol Bagh.“Through theatre, music, visuals and performance, ‘Dastaan-e-Amritsar’ transforms history from a collection of dates into a living narrative. By placing sacred landmarks alongside neighbourhoods, writers and ordinary cultural traditions, it offers a compelling reminder that Amritsar’s heritage resides as much in its people and lived experiences as in its monuments,” said Prof Karamjeet Singh.

headline: Sant Nagar in Sirsa hits streets against drugs after 23-year-old’s death
content: The death of 23-year-old Sagar, allegedly due to a drug overdose, has triggered a wave of protests in Sant Nagar, with residents taking to the streets on Thursday to demand action against drug trafficking and measures to make the village drug-free.Men, women, elderly residents and youths participated in the protest, highlighting the worsening drug problem in Ward No. 10 and accusing the authorities of failing to curb the menace despite repeated complaints. The protesters also demanded the establishment of a police chowki in the village to strengthen policing and prevent drug sales.Sant Nagar, once known for producing hockey players who brought laurels to the country, including at the Olympic level, is now grappling with a growing substance abuse crisis. Residents expressed concern over an increasing number of young people falling prey to addiction, saying several families urgently need access to medical treatment, counselling and rehabilitation services.Women taking part in the rally alleged that drugs were being sold openly in residential areas and that those raising their voices against the trade were being threatened. Several mothers voiced fears about their sons falling into addiction and appealed to the state government to take immediate action.Paramjeet Singh, district secretary of Naujawan Bharat Sabha and a Sant Nagar resident, alleged that he had received death threats for highlighting the drug problem before the police. He further claimed that his elderly mother was assaulted while she was on her way to visit a doctor in the village. According to him, a complaint had been submitted to the police, but no action had been taken so far.Ranjit Singh, cousin of deceased Sagar, said the family had not witnessed any significant intervention by the administration following the young man's death. He claimed that hundreds of youths in the village needed medical treatment and counselling to break free from addiction.He also demanded a police chowki in Sant Nagar, pointing out that the nearest police post was in Jiwan Nagar and that police personnel generally visited the village only after receiving complaints.Sagar's death had brought the extent of the problem into focus. A kabaddi player who earned his livelihood as a mason, he had reportedly battled drug addiction for the past two to three years. Residents said many other families were facing similar struggles, including repeated relapses, financial distress and the adverse impact of addiction on children.The protesters have called for a crackdown on alleged drug traffickers, a police post in the village, an impartial inquiry into complaints of threats and assault, and easily accessible treatment and rehabilitation facilities for those battling addiction. They said the administration must act before more young lives are lost to drugs.

headline: Couple killed, 1 hurt as pickup plunges into Lahaul stream
content: Two persons were killed and another sustained injuries after a pickup vehicle plunged into a stream near a petrol pump on the Tandi-Peukar link road in Lahaul and Spiti district on Thursday afternoon.According to the District Emergency Operations Centre (DEOC), Lahaul and Spiti, the accident occurred around 4 pm when the pickup (HP-42-3830), travelling from Gozang village towards Tandi, reportedly lost control while crossing a waterlogged stretch of the road. The vehicle skidded off the road and plunged into the stream below.Three persons, including two men and a woman, were travelling in the vehicle at the time of the accident. The two occupants, identified as Ajay, son of Diwan Chand, and his wife Anjali, both residents of Katrain in Manali tehsil of Kullu district, died on the spot.The third occupant, Saksham, son of Jawahar Lal and a resident of Lapshak village in Lahaul, sustained injuries and was rushed to Regional Hospital, Keylong. The police initiated necessary proceedings and verification in connection with the incident.

headline: Himachal teachers’ body seeks governor’s intervention against State Universities Amendment Bill
content: The Himachal Pradesh University Teachers’ Welfare Association (HPUTWA) on Thursday met Himachal Pradesh governor Kavinder Gupta and raised concerns over the university’s autonomy, academic freedom, and institutional structure, seeking protection of its established governance framework in the wake of the Himachal Pradesh State Universities (Amendment) Bill, 2026.The association has been protesting for the last 85 days outside the vice-chancellor’s office at Himachal Pradesh University (HPU).The delegation urged the governor to ensure that future decisions concerning the university preserve its historic institutional structure and autonomy. The governor heard the delegation’s concerns and assured them that the issues raised would be considered.They said HPU must retain the freedom to make its own academic and research-related decisions to effectively fulfil its role in higher education and research.President of HPUTWA, Nitin Vyas, said, “The autonomy of the university is not an issue concerning any one section alone. It is an important question linked to the future of the entire university community, including teachers, non-teaching staff, research scholars and students. Any adverse impact on autonomy could directly affect academic freedom, the quality of research, innovation and the university’s institutional decision-making process.”The Himachal Pradesh assembly passed the Bill during the monsoon session by voice vote despite opposition from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The bill is yet to get the governor’s assent.The legislation fundamentally alters the recruitment landscape for state universities. Under the new system, universities retain the authority to appoint professors and associate professors. However, recruitment for all other posts will be handled by the Himachal Pradesh Public Service Commission (HPPSC) and the State Selection Commission.

headline: Himachal: Tanda hospital cuts stent prices by up to 57%
content: In a major relief to patients undergoing cardiac treatment, Dr Rajendra Prasad Government Medical College and Hospital, Tanda, has substantially reduced stent prices following a competitive tender process. The cost of different brands of stents, earlier priced at Rs 41,000, has been reduced to Rs 21,500 and Rs 17,500, depending on the brand.The revised rates are expected to ease the financial burden on patients requiring stent implantation and other cardiac interventions. The reduction follows a competitive tendering process in which several vendors participated.Principal of Tanda Medical College, Dr Milap Sharma, told The Tribune that the revised prices had been finalised after completion of the tender process. He said vendors, including Hari Om Traders, Atulya Surgical, Niccos and Ramdial, among others, had participated in the process.Dr Sharma clarified that the revised rates would apply uniformly to all patients, irrespective of their mode of payment. Patients availing themselves of treatment under the Himcare and Ayushman Bharat health insurance schemes, as well as those paying in cash, would benefit from the reduced prices.The decision is particularly significant for economically weaker patients, for whom the cost of cardiac treatment can be a major financial burden. The reduction in stent prices is expected to make treatment more affordable and improve access to essential cardiac procedures.The hospital administration has appealed to patients and their attendants to remain informed about the revised rates and avail themselves of the facility.The move is being viewed as a step towards reducing out-of-pocket healthcare expenditure at one of Himachal Pradesh’s major government tertiary-care institutions. By introducing lower rates through a competitive tender process, the medical college administration aims to make essential cardiac treatment more affordable.Tanda Medical College had earlier come under scrutiny after stents were found stored illegally in a cupboard in its Cardiology Department, raising concerns over alleged irregularities in the department.Dr Sharma said an inquiry into allegations of overcharging for stents in the past was underway. He said the Chief Minister had taken the matter seriously and senior officials of the state Health Department were investigating it.Cardiac scrutinyStents were found stored illegally in a cupboard in the Cardiology Department at Tanda Medical College, triggering scrutiny over alleged irregularitiesPatients had allegedly been overcharged for stents in the past, prompting an inquiry into the matterThe Chief Minister has taken the allegations seriously, with senior Health Department officials investigating the caseThe inquiry into the alleged overcharging is still underway

headline: DMK To Join Hands With BJP? TVK's Big Claim Amid Delimitation Buzz
content: The DMK is preparing to join hands with the BJP in Tamil Nadu, Chief Minister Vijay's TVK party has claimed, in the backdrop of the delimitation issue that appears set to headline next week's Parliament session. The MK Stalin-led party has rejected the allegation, though sources suggest that DMK leaders would meet soon to discuss the delimitation issue. The delimitation bill was defeated in April due to the lack of a two-thirds majority. It is expected to make a comeback when Lok Sabha reconvenes on Monday, and Rajya Sabha on Wednesday. READ | Parliament Reconvenes From November 30 For Centre's Big Delimitation Move The DMK also defended Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin's meeting with Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, which the TVK had cited as an indicator of an alleged political shift.

headline: Centre authorises states, UTs to exercise powers under UAPA against Zakir Naik’s IRF
content: New Delhi, The Centre has authorised states and Union territories to exercise powers related to funds and premises under the stringent Unlawful Activities Act, 1967, in relation to fugitive preacher Zakir Naik's Islamic Research Foundation , which was declared an unlawful association earlier this month.In a gazette notification issued on Thursday, the Ministry of Home Affairs invoked powers under Section 42 of the anti-terror law to issue the directive to state governments and Union territory administrators.The ministry had extended the ban on the IRF as an unlawful association through a notification dated November 13 under sections 3 and 3 of the Act."The Central government declared the Islamic Research Foundation an unlawful association vide notification number S.O. 6182 dated November 13, 2026, published in the Gazette of India; in exercise of the powers conferred by Section 42 of the Unlawful Activities Act, 1967, the Central government hereby directs that all powers exercisable by it under sections 7 and 8 of the said Act shall also be exercised by the state governments and the Union territory administrations in relation to the above said unlawful association," the notification said.Section 7 of the UA pertains to the powers of the government to prohibit the use or transfer of funds, securities and other financial assets suspected of being used or intended for the purposes of an unlawful association.It also allows authorised officers to investigate such financial dealings, whereas Section 8 empowers the government to notify premises, including houses and buildings, suspected of being used for the activities of an unlawful association.Following the notification, the authorities can regulate access to a premises and restrict the use of movable properties found there.On November 13, the Centre extended the ban on fugitive preacher Zakir Naik's IRF for another five years under the stringent UA. The ban was to expire on November 14.Naik, a resident of Maharashtra, was on a trip abroad when the government banned his organisation in 2016. Since then, he has been living in Malaysia. In 2017, his passport was also revoked at the request of the National Investigation Agency , which registered a case against him.India has been pursuing legal and diplomatic measures against Naik since November 17, 2016, when the Central government declared his organisation an unlawful association citing allegations of promoting enmity and hatred between religious communities.In May 2017, India approached INTERPOL for a Red Corner Notice against Naik, providing subsequent clarifications in August and October.However, during its 102nd session in late December 2017, the Interpol Commission deemed the request premature because a charge-sheet had not been filed at the time of the initial application.Based on a fresh court warrant issued on November 24, 2017, the Indian agencies submitted a renewed RCN request to INTERPOL on January 3, 2018, a response to which remains awaited.India had also formally transmitted a provisional arrest and extradition request to Malaysia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs on January 19, 2018, after it was confirmed that Naik had been granted permanent residency status.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: 3-day National Dairy Mela & Agri-Expo begins at ICAR-NDRI
content: With the objective of connecting the dairy sector with modern technologies, increasing farmers’ income and promoting milk production, a three-day National Dairy Fair and Agri Expo began at the ICAR-National Dairy Research Institute (NDRI), on Thursday to mark National Milk Day.Farmers, livestock owners, dairy entrepreneurs, scientists, experts and milk producers from across the region are participating in the event, which showcases improved dairy breeds, modern dairy technologies, milk-processing machinery and innovations in agriculture. Scientists showcased their technologies and research related to dairy sectors, while farmers brought their livestocks for beauty and milking competitions.For the first time, goat farmers have also been specially invited to participate in the fair, reflecting the growing interest in goat farming as an alternative source of livelihood.Chief guest, Prof Suresh Kumar Malhotra, Vice-Chancellor, Maharana Pratap Horticultural University, Karnal, said the holistic development of agriculture was possible only when equal attention was given to allied sectors such as dairy, horticulture, animal husbandry, fisheries and other related areas.He said the future belonged to innovation, technology and knowledge-based agriculture, in which institutions such as ICAR–NDRI were playing a significant role.Prof Malhotra appreciated the latest technologies developed by ICAR–NDRI, stating that these innovations enabled faster and more reliable detection of adulteration in milk and dairy products. Dr Dheer Singh, Director, ICAR–NDRI, said more than 50,000 farmers, livestock owners and animal lovers from various states, including Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttarakhand, are expected to participate in the three-day National Dairy Mela.Dr Singh emphasised that the mela was not merely an exhibition of products, but also an important platform for knowledge sharing, technology transfer and market linkage. “This year the institute has introduced a new initiative by showcasing technologies that have been developed and are ready for commercialisation. Young entrepreneurs can explore these technologies and adopt them to establish their own start-ups,” he added.At the inaugural ceremony, Sunil Kaushik, General Manager, NABARD, apprised the farmers and livestock rearers present about NABARD’s activities.On this occasion, the institute honoured several farmers for their outstanding contributions to the dairy and agriculture sectors.

headline: Samrasta Yatra gets grand welcome in Karnal, Haryana
content: The nationwide Samrasta Sankalp Yatra, being organised to mark the 650th birth anniversary year of Sant Ravidas, received a grand welcome on its arrival in Karnal on Thursday. BJP office-bearers, party workers and representatives of various social and religious organisations welcomed the yatra near Atal Park Chowk on NH-44. The yatra was welcomed in Gharaunda also.BJP state general secretary and yatra’s state coordinator, Satya Prakash Jarawata said the yatra was being organised to take forward the ideals of equality, self-respect and social justice propagated by Sadguru Ravidas centuries ago. He said the teachings of the saint were not limited to any particular community but provided a new direction to humanity as a whole. His life and philosophy inspire people to rise above caste-based discrimination and move forward with mutual respect, equality and brotherhood.Jarawata said ensuring dignity and self-respect for the Ravidassia community, along with the welfare of every section of society, remained a commitment of the BJP. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the principles of 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas and Sabka Prayas' were being promoted to strengthen social harmony.Giving details of the journey, Jarawata said it began on November 18 from Dera Sachkhand Ballan in Jalandhar, Punjab, and would cover around 2,402 km before concluding on December 3 at Seer Goverdhanpur in Varanasi, the birthplace of Sant Ravidas. From Karnal, it would proceed towards Uttar Pradesh via Panipat and Sonepat, he added.BJP district president Parveen Lather said Haryana had always been known for the mutual love, trust and brotherhood among its 36 communities. The Samrasta Sankalp Yatra was strengthening this proud social tradition and spreading the message of unity.

headline: Six years after Delhi march, Punjab farmers’ movement grapples with divisions, fading momentum
content: Six years after thousands of farmers marched towards Delhi to oppose the three contentious farm laws, the farmers’ movement in Punjab is facing a crisis of unity, political differences and dwindling mobilisation.Several of the key demands that sustained the year-long agitation remain unaddressed. The historic march, which began on November 26, 2020, brought together farmers from across the country to protest against the Farmers’ Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2020; the Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act, 2020; and the Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2020.The farmers had argued that the laws would weaken the regulated mandi system, undermine the minimum support price (MSP) regime, expose them to corporate exploitation and dilute safeguards against hoarding of essential commodities. Following a year-long agitation at Delhi’s borders, the Centre repealed the three laws in November 2021.However, six years on, farmers’ organisations say there has been little progress on their other major demands, including a legal guarantee for MSP for all crops, a farm loan waiver covering farmers and agricultural labourers, and a comprehensive crop insurance scheme.The movement, which brought several farmer unions together under a common umbrella, has since fragmented. The Samyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM), which spearheaded the Delhi agitation, has split into the SKM and the SKM (Non-Political). Differences over political engagement and the electoral choices of constituent unions in the run-up to the 2022 Punjab Vidhan Sabha elections further complicated efforts to maintain a united platform.The movement has also struggled to sustain its momentum. A rare instance of wider mobilisation, albeit much smaller in scale and intensity than the Delhi agitation, was witnessed recently when the Punjab Government announced its land pooling policy.The political landscape has also changed. The pressure generated by the farmers’ agitation had contributed to the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) walking out of the BJP-led NDA in 2020. The two parties have now reunited, even as sections of the farmers’ movement continue to oppose the BJP.The divisions within the SKM have come into sharper focus, with some constituent unions making independent political choices. Harinder Singh Lakhowal of the BKU (Lakhowal), who recently extended support to the SAD, said the SKM’s rules had been amended to allow constituent unions to make independent electoral choices, provided they did not contest elections themselves.“In six years, the momentum built in 2020-21 is getting lost. There is no word on an MSP guarantee for all crops, farm loan waiver for farmers and farm labourers, or crop insurance. We have supported the SAD, not the BJP. Our support is to a regional party so that it can take our demands to the Centre,” he told The Tribune.He said the SAD had assured the union that it would take up two important issues concerning Punjab with the Centre — the release of Bandi Singhs and a legal guarantee for MSP.“We have not even been heard in the five years since the protest ended in 2021,” he said, while criticising both the AAP and the Congress over their handling of farmers’ issues.However, other farmer organisations have strongly opposed any political alignment with parties they consider responsible for implementing policies detrimental to farmers. Kirti Kisan Union general secretary Rajinder Singh Deepsinghwala said his organisation would oppose any political alliance involving the BJP.“The farmers’ movement has slowed down. When the protest was called off, nearly 70 per cent of farmers in the country did not know about MSP. It was decided that unions from all states would return and build a movement for a legal guarantee for MSP. In most states, this did not happen,” he said, adding that the lack of political engagement on farmers’ demands had also contributed to the absence of progress.Meanwhile, the state committee of the Bharatiya Kisan Union (Ekta Dakaunda) has condemned what it described as indirect support extended to the BJP by certain farmer organisations. State president Manjit Singh Dhaner said that while all political parties were responsible for implementing policies favouring corporate interests, the BJP, being in power at the Centre, was the principal adversary of farmers and labourers.He maintained that farmers’ and labourers’ issues could not be resolved by aligning with political parties implementing such policies. The union said the collective strength of people had been instrumental in the success of the Delhi agitation and expressed concern that some farmer organisations were moving away from that approach.

headline: "From Farm Laws to Chitta": Bhagwant Mann Questions SAD-BJP U-Turns
content: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann launched a sharp attack on the newly forged Shiromani Akali Dal-BJP alliance on Thursday, accusing the parties of misleading Punjabis for 25 years through political rivalry, shifting alliances and contradictory positions on key issues, including drugs and the farmers' agitation. Addressing the AAP rally in Moga, Mann took particular aim at the coming together of leaders who, according to him, had spent years attacking each other but were now sharing political platforms for electoral gains. He pointed towards the December 8 rally, where Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to share the stage with senior BJP and Akali Dal leaders, and questioned the political consistency of the alliance partners. "Imagine who will be sitting on the stage on December 8. Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, Bikram Singh Majithia, Sukhbir Badal, Captain Amarinder Singh, Sunil Jakhar, Ravneet Bittu, Kewal Singh Dhillon, Ashwani Kumar and Tarun Chugh will all be together. The same people, the same faces and the same leaders," Mann said. Taking a dig at leaders frequently switching political positions and parties, he remarked that they changed parties faster than they changed clothes.

headline: Opposition slams AAP govt for ‘misusing’ public funds for Moga rally
content: The Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the BJP on Thursday launched a sharp attack on the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), accusing it of misusing public funds and government machinery to organise its “Khushhaal Punjab” rally in Moga.Bathinda MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal alleged that more than half of the Pepsu Road Transport Corporation (PRTC) bus fleet had been diverted from regular routes to ferry people to the rally venue, inconveniencing daily commuters.Claiming that 680 buses out of a fleet of around 1,350 had been deployed for the event, she questioned the use of public transport and government funds for a political rally. She accused the government of projecting the rally as an official state function, with the Chief Secretary being deployed to defend the decision.Former Punjab BJP president Sunil Jakhar also targeted AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal, alleging that the Moga rally was being organised using public money.Taking a dig at Kejriwal, Jakhar asked whether he would again stay at the house of a Khalistan Commando Force activist during his Punjab visit, as he had allegedly done in 2017.Jakhar also accused the AAP of inducting gangsters and anti-social elements into the party under what he described as its policy of “persuasion, punishment, division, fighting and quarrelling”. He questioned whether the party would also consider giving election tickets to separatists.BJP general secretary Anil Sarin accused CM Bhagwant Mann and Kejriwal of turning the rally into a spectacle of political rhetoric without making any concrete announcements for Punjab.

headline: Madras High Court commends Tamil Nadu police for tracing 2,510 missing persons within a fortnight
content: CHENNAI The Madras High Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) commended the Tamil Nadu police for conducting a two-week-long special drive to trace missing persons and succeeding in tracing 1,469 women, 629 men, 289 girls and 128 boys between October 30, 2026 and November 13, 2026. Justices A.D. Jagadish Chandira and B. Karthikeyan recorded appreciation to the police department for having traced as many as 2,510 missing persons during the special drive and asked Additional Public Prosecutor M. Mohamed Riyaz to ensure that the momentum sustains. It was while hearing a habeas corpus petition filed by T. Bhuvaneshwari of Keezhaiyur in Kallakurichi district, whose husband P. Sankararaj was missing since 2021, that the judges had called for data related to missing persons from the office of the Director General of Police/Head of Police Force. In response, A. Pradeep, Assistant Inspector General of Police (Law and Order) and staff officer to the DGP/HoPF, filed a report before the court on Thursday stating that 2,41,927 cases were booked in Tamil Nadu in connection with the missing of 2,63,894 missing persons between January 1, 2016 and November 16, 2026. Of them, 2,48,364 missing persons had been traced and reunited with their family members and the rest of 15,530 remain untraceable. The court was also told that as on November 16, 2026 15,134 cases related to missing persons were under investigation and of them, 1,064 cases were more than seven years old. The court was also told that 1,174 cases were between seven and five years old; 2,121 cases were between five and three years old; 4,402 cases were between three and one year old; and 2,861 cases were three months old. The district-wise data regarding the status of missing person cases was also submitted before the court. On the court’s query as to whether latest technologies such as Artificial Intelligence were being utilised for tracing the missing persons, the office of the DGP/HoPF said, the Tamil Nadu citizen portal www.police.tn.gov.in provides a facility for searching and comparing missing-person particulars with the available database of unidentified dead bodies. If the users enter basic details of missing individuals such as gender, age group, date range of disappearance, identifiable marks and physical parameters, the system returns a list of unidentified deceased persons that match the entered criteria. Photographs and physical descriptions are also displayed to enable manual comparison by families or police officials, the AIG said. He told the court that a facial recognition system was utlised for comparison of available photographs with the existing database to identify possible matches. Further, the DGP/HoPF’s office had circualted a Standard Operating Procedure on August 10, 2026 for utilisation of CCTV footage, call detail records, internet protocol detail records, social-media information, banking transactions, cybercrime-related information, missing-person portals, NATGRID and other relevant digital evidence, wherever necessary and permissible under law, for tracing missing children, Mr. Pradeep added.

headline: Tamil Nadu govt. has acquired only 24% of land required for railway projects: Ashwini Vaishnav
content: Chennai Stating that the Tamil Nadu government will have to do its duty of acquiring land if all sanctioned railway projects are to be implemented in the State, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the total land acquired so far stood at only 24% of the land required. Speaking at a Constitution Day event organised by the State BJP unit in the city on Thursday, Mr. Vaishnav said, that out of a total requirment of 4,800 hectares of land, the State has managed to acquire only 1,253 hectares. “My request to the TVK is, please take this as a challenge. Acquire the land [and] we will [carry out] each and every project without any hassle...don’t shy away from your responsibilities,” he emphasised. Projects sanctioned for development of railways in Tamil Nadu amounted to Rs. 48,000 crore, he added. Taking a dig at the State government over the Thiruparankundram deepam issue, Mr. Vaishnav said, “You can stop one deepam to be lighted, but you cannot stop the Tamil people from progress. Stopping one deepam, you have disturbed the emotions of millions of people.” Listing out some of the projects undertaken, the minister said that 77 railway stations in Tamil Nadu are being reconstructed. Construction was underway in stations like Chennai Egmore, Madurai, and Katpadi, while construction work has been completed in Chinna Salem, Morappur, Manapparai, Pollachi, Thiruvarur, Coonoor, and Udhagamandalam. Nine Vande Bharat services are being operated in Tamil Nadu, he maintained. Bullet trains, once introduced, will cut the journey from Chennai to Bengaluru to merely 73 minutes. Also, the Hyderabad-Amaravati-Chennai distance will take three hours to complete, the minister added. He added that in Gummidipoondi, the Ramkrishna Titagarh Rail Wheels Ltd’s forged wheel factory was ready and would soon roll out high strength railway wheels which will be exported to Europe as well. Earlier, BJP State President Nainar Nagendran put forth a series of requests, including installing a statue of former chief minister M.G. Ramachandran at the Chennai Central Railway Station, reopening of Kallur station near Tirunelveli, introducing sleeper coaches in Vande Bharat trains, and a stop at Thalaiyuthu station for trains running between Coimbatore and Tirunelveli. The minister immediately got on his phone passing the demands on to railway officials and setting a timeline for the same, which drew applause from the crowd. Tamilisai Soundararajan, senior BJP leader, requested the minister to install a statue of freedom fighter Vanchinathan at the Vanchi Maniyachchi Junction in Thoothukudi district.

headline: No compromise on teacher recruitment: Himachal minister Dharmani
content: “A student-centric approach is essential for improving the education system,” said Technical Education Minister Rajesh Dharmani while addressing students at the annual function of the District Institute of Education and Training (DIET) at Jukhala in Bilaspur district today.He also inaugurated the APJ Abdul Kalam Science Bhawan at the institute. The building, constructed at a cost of nearly Rs 1.22 crore, is equipped with facilities to meet various academic and institutional requirements.Dharmani said the building would play an important role in meeting the institute’s academic and training needs. He stressed that students should remain at the centre of every decision and action in the education system to ensure that these measures positively shaped their future. Prioritising personal interests or convenience over students’ well-being, he said, undermined the very purpose of education.He also stressed that there should be no compromise on teacher recruitment, as the availability of qualified teachers directly affected students’ education and future.The minister described institutions such as DIETs as the backbone of the education system. He said trainees receiving instruction there would go on to educate future generations and, therefore, must be provided high-quality training, subject expertise and a conducive academic environment.He added that the role of DIETs extended beyond training prospective teachers to include the skill development of in-service teachers and improvement in academic standards.Referring to Constitution Day, Dharmani said the Constitution guaranteed every citizen equal rights, justice, opportunities and freedom of expression. Its core spirit, he stressed, should not remain confined to words but must be translated into practice.Earlier, he honoured students for their achievements in academics, sports and other activities.Former MLA Tilak Raj Sharma, HIMUDA Director Jitender Chandel, State Congress Committee General Secretary Vikas Thakur and Deputy Director of Higher Education (Schools) Naresh Chandel were also present on the occasion.

headline: AAP kicks off poll drive with Moga rally, highlights welfare schemes
content: The ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Thursday sounded a poll bugle for the upcoming Assembly elections with the 'Khushhaal Punjab Rally' at Matwani village on the Moga-Ludhiana highway. The event was officially organised by the state government as a Smart Ration Card Distribution Function, during which Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann launched the scheme and distributed smart cards and ration kits to beneficiaries.The rally drew a massive turnout, with AAP leaders attacking political opponents, particularly the newly revived SAD-BJP alliance, while projecting the Mann government’s welfare schemes as the party's principal electoral plank. The party has announced 71 of the 117 candidates, much ahead of other parties.AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal, who addressed a gathering in Punjab after five months, appealed to women voters and assured them that all existing welfare schemes would continue if the party returned to power. He accused the BJP-led Centre of attempting to stop the monthly financial assistance of Rs 1,000 and Rs 1,500 to women under the Mawan Dhiyan Satkar Yojana.Referring to Mann as his "younger brother", Kejriwal claimed that over two lakh people attended the rally. Invoking the significance of November 26, he said it was the day Dr BR Ambedkar’s Constitution was adopted and AAP was formed in 2012. “The Constitution is being crushed today. It is an indication from God that this responsibility has been given to AAP,” he said.Recalling the 2022 Assembly elections, Kejriwal said he had sought votes by giving guarantees rather than making false promises and credited Mann with fulfilling those commitments. Blaming the Modi government for inflation, he said the state's monthly assistance scheme was providing women financial independence and helping meet household expenses.Two women beneficiaries were invited to the stage and shared how the financial assistance had helped them meet household and medical expenses.Kejriwal alleged that the Congress intended to discontinue the scheme, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi had described welfare benefits as "free revadis". Referring to the AAP government's initiatives in Delhi, he alleged that the BJP had stopped schemes such as free pilgrimage facilities and mohalla clinics after coming to power there.Assuring women that all welfare schemes would continue if AAP returned to power, he urged them to vote for the party and persuade men in their families to support it. He cited free electricity, improved canal water supply, daytime power for agriculture, free treatment and more than 70,000 merit-based government jobs as achievements of the Mann government.Later, Mann launched a scathing attack on the SAD-BJP alliance, accusing the two parties of betraying Punjab’s interests and joining hands again for political gains. He claimed the Akalis formed the alliance just to secure a Cabinet berth in the Centre for Harsimrat and to pass the three farm laws.He also targeted Congress leaders over their alleged infighting.Referring to the agitation against the three farm laws, Mann accused the Badal family of initially supporting the legislation and changing their stand only after protests intensified. He also questioned the SAD leadership’s alleged silence on Chandigarh, river waters, Bandi Singhs and the Anandpur Sahib resolution after renewing its alliance with the BJP.Targeting SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal, Mann recalled the party's earlier allegations that the BJP interfered in Sikh religious institutions and questioned its decision to renew the alliance.He also took a dig at the BJP's anti-drug campaign and made remarks about Sukhbir's late mother, his wife Bathinda MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal and brother-in-law Bikram Singh Majithia.Without making any fresh announcement, Mann highlighted the government's flagship initiatives, including free electricity, financial assistance to women and government recruitment drives.AAP Punjab affairs in-charge Manish Sisodia and state unit president Aman Arora also addressed the gathering. No AAP leader targeted the Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De) in their speeches.The venue was packed and the public cheered during Mann’s speech. Moga MLA Dr Amandeep Kaur Arora and Dharamkot MLA Devinderjeet Singh Laddi Dhose, who had been summoned by the Enforcement Directorate on November 26 and 27, respectively, were also present.A worker manning the coffee machine at the press gallery allegedly died after it exploded before the start of the rally. However, neither the district administration nor the police officially confirmed the death. AAP chief spokesperson Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal said one person had been injured, but some eyewitnesses claimed that the worker had died on the spot due to a severe head injury. None of the speakers on the stage mentioned him in their speeches.Agriculture Minister Gurmeet Singh Khudian, who has not been fielded from Lambi this time, was sitting in the front row on the stage. AAP’s Bathinda Mayor Padamjeet Singh Mehta had put up hoardings along the route to the rally venue, located about 80 km from Bathinda. The rally led to a huge traffic jam lasting over two hours on the Moga-Ludhiana highway.Famous Punjabi singer Kulwinder Billa enthralled the audience.Smart Ration Card SchemeMann said the Smart Ration Card Scheme would cover 10 lakh additional beneficiaries. The government received 19.25 lakh applications during a special campaign launched in July, following which door-to-door verification was conducted to identify eligible families.

headline: Experts examine key aspects, challenges of conducting Census
content: Photo: Johan Sathyadas J CHENNAI An engaging conversation between retired IAS officer C. Chandramouli and Vinay Sitapati, Associate Dean and Professor of Law and Politics at Shiv Nadar University, over the former’s book, Counting a Nation – The Story of the Indian Census, here on Thursday evening, brought out the various aspects of conducting Census in the country. Among the issues discussed were the need for a law to govern enumeration for caste census, the challenges faced while ensuring accuracy, training of enumerators for a standardised enumeration process, differences in the motive for carrying out the Census before and after the country’s independence, and the implication of Census for delimitation. Book launch During the book launch organised by Chennai International Centre (CIC) at the NFDC Tagore auditorium, Mr. Chandramouli, who had also served as the Registrar General and the Census Commissioner of India, recalled the challenges faced by enumerators while collecting data, specifically while enumerating the Sentinelese. Mr. Chandramouli, also the CIC Managing Director, explained why his book was not a memoir, noting that carrying out the Census was a team work of greater proportion. Mr. Sitapati said Mr. Chandramouli’s book was a current affairs work, but it looked at current issues through the lens of history. The discussion also highlighted the curiosity over the results of Census 2027. When a curious Mr. Sitapati asked what the newspapers’ headlines would be, especially that of The Hindu, the day after Census 2027 results, Mr. Chandramouli said the headlines would differ across regions depending on the results for each State. Technology adoption As for adopting technology for conducting Census, Mr. Chandramouli said that even in the most sophisticated of Censuses, “ground truthing of the whole exercise by visiting the field and checking the information is key to the success of an operation like this.” With modern technology, the exercise could be more efficient and quicker, he added.

headline: Over 4 kg ICE, drone seized from field near Attari border
content: The Amritsar police recovered 4.950 kg of methamphetamine, popularly known as crystalline meth or ICE, along with a drone, from agricultural fields near Attari here on Wednesday.The recovery was made after a specific intelligence input alerted the police to a suspicious packet lying in the fields near the border village. A drug detection kit confirmed the presence of ICE.The seizure of sophisticated firearms, including an MP5 submachine gun in a recent operation, and the continued smuggling of weapons and narcotics through the porous international border with Pakistan have raised concerns among security agencies, particularly in view of the upcoming Punjab Assembly elections.Apart from drugs and weapons, the police also recovered two drones used for smuggling the consignments.In another recovery near the Attari railway station, the police seized a .30-bore Ghaffar rifle (MP 5 Sub-machine gun), two empty magazines and 50 live cartridges. The weapon was found in a packet weighing heavily, which had reportedly been detected during a search operation by the Border Security Force. They also confiscated a drone from the scene. The police have registered a case under the Arms Act and the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam.In two separate cases registered at the Gharinda police station, the police recovered a pistol magazine with ammunition and a 7.62-mm Zastava pistol manufactured in Serbia. Both consignments were handed over to the police by BSF personnel.The recoveries point towards the continued attempts to push sophisticated weapons, ammunition and narcotics into Punjab from across the border, often through drone-assisted consignments.Security agencies are particularly concerned over the increasing availability of foreign-made firearms and assault weapons, which could potentially be diverted to criminal and anti-national networks in the state.The recent seizure of an MP5 submachine gun has further heightened these concerns. Investigating agencies are examining the supply routes and possible links of handlers operating from across the border, besides trying to establish the intended recipients of such consignments.

headline: Haryana Agri Dept calls for Vigilance probe into Karnal mandi accounts
content: The Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Department has recommended a Vigilance inquiry into alleged financial irregularities and discrepancies in the income and expenditure records of the Karnal Market Committee. The move follows a report submitted by the District Marketing Enforcement Officer (DMEO), Kaithal, highlighting suspected lapses in the maintenance and verification of financial records.The department has sought an action-taken report within a month and directed the Chief Administrator of the Haryana State Agricultural Marketing Board (HSAMB), Panchkula, to examine the allegations thoroughly and submit an investigation report for further action. The report flags questions over bank deposits, fixed deposits (FDRs), cash book entries and the maintenance of mandatory financial registers.An audit team was constituted in July 2024 to examine the Market Committee’s financial records. However, the committee allegedly failed to provide the requisite documents for the period from 2014-15 to 2024-25. The inquiry reportedly made little progress following the transfer of the then DMEO in December 2024.The matter was revived following fresh directions from the authorities. In June 2026, the Market Committee Secretary was asked to produce the permanent Register of Deposits, an essential document for verifying bank accounts, fixed deposits and other financial transactions. However, the report states that the register and supporting documents were not furnished despite repeated reminders.The DMEO report also points to discrepancies involving substantial bank deposits during 2014-15 and 2015-16. It refers to 13 fixed deposits identified during the audit exercise, with transactions involving amounts such as Rs 1.76 crore, Rs 1.61 crore and Rs 75 lakh in two banks.Another issue concerns Rs 2 crore received from the Thanesar Market Committee in January 2014. The report questions how the receipt and subsequent repayment were recorded, alleging discrepancies between cash book entries and the actual financial position. It also refers to special audit reports covering 2012-15, which had flagged financial discrepancies. The DMEO has recommended a fresh, independent audit of the period from 2012 to March 2015, particularly the period covered by the 2015-16 special audit.HSAMB Chief Administrator Dharmendra Singh said the board would comply with the government’s directions.

headline: Haryana in grip of gangsters, alleges Congress after Rohtak killings
content: The Congress on Thursday condemned the killing of four people by unidentified assailants at Milan Dhaba near Kharawar village, alleging that Haryana was in the grip of gangsters while the government remained absent.Reacting to Wednesday night’s incident, Rohtak Congress MP Deepender Singh Hooda alleged that the law and order situation in Haryana had “completely collapsed”, with Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini having “no time for the state”.Describing the killings as horrific, he said such incidents had become routine in the state.“Haryana is now in the grip of extortion, gun violence and gangster rule. People are living in fear while criminals continue to roam freely without fear,” Deepender told mediapersons in Rohtak.Congress Rajya Sabha MP Randeep Singh Surjewala also slammed the state’s BJP government.“Today, Haryana is under criminal rule. Gangs are running Haryana, while the government is missing,” he said in a social media post.“Ransom, indiscriminate gunfire, kidnappings — this is now everyday life in Haryana. The latest evidence is the shooting at Milan Dhaba, just 50 steps from the Kharawar police post in Rohtak…” he added.“Chief Minister Nayab Saini, if you can spare a moment from your jokes and trips to Punjab, spare a little concern for the lives of Haryanvis too,” he said.Three of the four deceased — Rinku (28), Vineet (22) and Yash (22) — belonged to Dighal village in neighbouring Jhajjar district.An uneasy calm prevailed in the village after news of the murders reached residents, as it has already witnessed two killings stemming from personal enmity this year.Some residents, particularly those engaged in the financing business, have also received extortion threats from gangsters operating from abroad.In view of the prevailing security concerns, police checkpoints have already been set up in the village.Meanwhile, Jhajjar Commissioner of Police Simardeep Singh said the preliminary investigation suggested that the killings at Milan Dhaba were a case of inter-gang rivalry.“The investigation is ongoing, and we expect to track down those responsible soon. A significant number of rounds were fired. We are verifying a post that appeared on social media and are also examining the angle of inter-gang rivalry. At least four to five shooters appear to have been involved in the crime,” he said.
