headline: "Dhakosla Patra": UP BJP Chief On Samajwadi Party's Poll Manifesto
content: New Delhi:Political temperatures rose on Thursday following the release of the Samajwadi Party's manifesto, "PDA Ka Prannpatra," with Uttar Pradesh BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary dismissing it as a "dhakosla patra" and saying voters in the state will not fall into the party's "electoral trap." Speaking to ANI, Chaudhary accused the SP of filling its "own coffers" while in power and plunging the state into "the fire of riots and corruption." He also mocked the manifesto's promise of zero tolerance for crime. He claimed SP members themselves know they will neither win the election nor form the government, which is why they brought out the document. "Even if the Samajwadi Party brings out a White Paper instead of a 'Pran Patra', the people of Uttar Pradesh are not going to fall into their electoral trap. Samajwadi Party members themselves know that they are neither going to win the election nor form the government; that is why they have brought out an unrealistic sham document ('dhakosla patra') today. Upon coming to power, they only filled their own coffers and plunged the entire state into the fire of riots and corruption...Those who implemented a 'One District, One Mafia' policy during their regime are today talking about zero tolerance toward crime and criminals; what could be more laughable than this?," Chaudhary said. In an X post, Choudhary also attacked the manifesto, saying even lies would die of shame, seeing "so many false promises", questioning SP's pledge to strengthen law and order in the state. "They're guaranteeing they'll end thuggery in the state? I want to ask: will you send your party workers out of the state?? Because their workers are already threatening to teach people a lesson," he said, accusing the previous Samajwadi government of backing "terrorists, thugs and even strongmen".

headline: Judicial member must for ED attachment cases: Supreme Court
content: The Supreme Court on Thursday ruled that the adjudicating authority (AA) under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) must include a judicial member while deciding whether to confirm the Enforcement Directorate’s (ED) provisional attachment of properties, holding that such consequential decisions cannot be left to a member without a legal background.A bench, comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, clarified that while a single-member bench can undertake adjudication under the law, it must necessarily comprise the judicial member of the AA. The requirement, the court said, flows from the need to ensure legal objectivity when determining whether properties are involved in money laundering, a finding that can have serious consequences for the rights of individuals.The ruling settles an important legal question that had divided high courts, with the Delhi, Calcutta and Telangana high courts having declined to insist on the presence of a judicial member in every bench of the AA. The Supreme Court has now drawn a clear distinction between the authority’s administrative and adjudicatory functions, holding that the former can be performed without a judicial member but the latter cannot.“The AA is, however, plainly more than a custodian of records. As its very name indicates, its principal task is ‘adjudication’ under Section 8 of the PMLA,” noted the bench, distinguishing between the authority acting as the “keeper of the sealed cover” and when “it holds the scales”.The court explained that when the ED provisionally attaches a property, it forwards the order, along with the material relied upon, to the AA, which preserves these records. This custodial function does not involve substantive decision-making or the appreciation of competing submissions and can, therefore, be discharged without a judicial member.However, the position changes when the AA hears the affected person and the ED, examines the evidence and determines whether the property is involved in money laundering. Such an exercise requires the application of legal principles, interpretation of statutory provisions and appreciation of evidence, it said.“The application of an independent judicial mind is...adequately ensured by the presence of a Judicial Member in the Bench undertaking adjudication under Sections 8(2) and 8(3) of PMLA,” it held.The bench also rejected the Centre’s argument that the availability of an appeal before the appellate tribunal and subsequently the high court was sufficient safeguard against any erroneous decision by the AA.“An appellate forum may correct the errors in a decision; it cannot supply what the original forum lacked,” said the court, adding that a defect in proceedings before the AA on account of the absence of a judicial member cannot be cured merely because an appeal lies to a judicial forum.It further clarified that a judicial member need not necessarily be appointed as the chairperson of the AA. The chairperson’s role, it said, was essentially administrative, involving the constitution of benches and allocation of cases, and did not require the same application of legal mind as the adjudicatory process.It accordingly directed the chairperson to issue the necessary administrative circular to ensure that every bench passing an order under Section 8(3) of the PMLA includes a judicial member. The court also extended the requirement to certain consequential determinations under other provisions of the PMLA, which are intrinsically linked to the adjudication of attachment, freezing or retention of property and records.Notably, the judgment did not invalidate the issuance of show-cause notices under Section 8(1) by a bench without a judicial member, nor did it mandate that every adjudication must be conducted by a bench of two or more members. A single-member bench remains permissible, provided the member is drawn from the field of law.The bench also clarified that its ruling would not automatically reopen orders already passed by a single, non-judicial member before Thursday. Persons aggrieved by such orders would, however, remain free to challenge them on their merits through the statutory appellate remedy.SC flags need for multiple adjudicating authoritiesSeparately, the bench nudged the Centre to reconsider the 2009 amendment to the PMLA that restricted the number of adjudicating authorities to one, recommending that the government examine the desirability of restoring the original framework of multiple AAs, including regional authorities.Pointing to the steep rise in provisional attachment orders (PAOs), the court said the existing arrangement was placing enormous pressure on the authority, particularly when it was required to complete adjudication within the statutory period of 180 days.According to figures furnished by the ED, a total of 3,639 PAOs had been issued since July 2005. While 321 such orders were issued in 2023-24, the number rose to 461 in 2024-25 and further jumped to 712 in 2025-26. Another 138 PAOs were issued up to August 31, 2026.The bench noted that the expansion of offences under the PMLA schedule and the consequent widening of proceedings under the law would only add to the workload, including applications for retention of seized properties and records.“This juxtaposition of the increasing cases and the time-bound nature of adjudication, to our mind, puts an enormous pressure on the Members of the AA, especially those involved in the process of adjudication,” it said.The court observed that the 2009 amendment, which replaced the original provision allowing the Centre to appoint one or more adjudicating authorities with a framework providing for only one, appeared to have created “an undesirable, if not unsolvable, lock-jam of cases at the level of the AA”. It cautioned that such circumstances could induce hurried and hasty decisions, adversely affecting stakeholders’ ability to access justice.The bench said it would ordinarily have exercised its powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to direct the Centre to notify additional adjudicating authorities, which would also enable the creation of regional AAs. However, since the 2009 amendment itself was not under challenge, it refrained from issuing such a direction.Instead, it recommended that the Union government “appropriately consider the suitability and desirability of repealing the 2009 Amendment and reverting to the original framework of multiple Adjudicating Authorities and take necessary steps for the same”.In its concluding observations, the bench described the PMLA as a law of “exceptional rigour”, stressing that its stringent provisions must be accompanied by safeguards at the stage when an affected person gets the opportunity to contest the attachment of property.“Independence of position is, however, only one half of that assurance. Where the authority is called upon to weigh evidence, apply statutory presumptions and construe the law, the assurance is fully honoured only when the person who decides is trained in the discipline of the law,” it said.

headline: Sheshnag Lake row: Karan Singh questions need for wider road, PDP steps up heat
content: SRINAGAR: The controversy over the presence of heavy machinery near the ecologically fragile Sheshnag Lake along the Amarnath Yatra route shows no signs of dying down, with former Sadr-i-Riyasat (head of state) of Jammu & Kashmir, Karan Singh, saying every pilgrimage route need not be turned into a multi-lane road for the convenience of tourists. Mehbooba Mufti-led PDP has also stepped up its campaign, demanding that govt allow a joint team of politicians and environmentalists to visit the lake and make the site accessible for an independent assessment.Joining the voices opposing the move, Karan Singh, in a social media post, said: “We do not have to make every pilgrim route into a motorable road just for the convenience of tourists. Genuine pilgrims will not mind walking or riding towards this great shrine.”Mehbooba demanded transparency in the matter, saying if no work was taking place near the lake, as assured by forest minister Altaf Kaloo, there was no reason to prevent people from visiting the site.“How did JCBs reach Sheshnag? Who authorised their movement, and what action has been taken against those responsible?” she asked at a press conference.Mehbooba said chief minister Omar Abdullah had signed a memorandum of understanding with the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) in Jan, assigning it the work of constructing a track in the area. She demanded that the agreement be made public and asked why people were not being allowed to travel from Pahalgam to Chandanwari and beyond.J&K government on Wednesday dismissed allegations of construction near the high-altitude lake, with Kaloo saying the JCB machinery was operating 200-300 feet away and at a higher elevation.As an online petition demanding an immediate halt to excavation and road-widening work near the lake crossed over 16,000 signatures Thursday, environmental activist Raja Muzaffar Bhat said he received a “distressing SOS” last night from a young nature lover, Zarqua Banday, who was allegedly being harassed for starting the petition. Bhat said cyber police had called her family.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Weakening democratic values: BJP, Congress target each other
content: The Himachal Pradesh Congress Committee organised a ‘Samvidhan Raksha March’, and the BJP leaders participated in ‘Samvidhan Gaurav Diwas’, to mark Constitution Day in Shimla, Thursday, while accusing each other of undermining and weakening democratic values. Following a call by the All India Congress Committee (AICC), state Congress president Vinay Kumar led the march, which witnessed the participation of thousands of party workers from across the state. Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu didn’t attend the event due to a short illness. The march began at Chaura Maidan, where Congress leaders paid floral tributes to Dr B R Ambedkar, the architect of the Indian Constitution. It culminated at the Ridge after the party leaders and workers took a pledge to protect the Constitution before Mahatma Gandhi’s statue. The AICC state in-charge, Rajni Patil, Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri, several Cabinet ministers, former MP Pratibha Singh, Congress MLAs and former legislators, besides party office-bearers and representatives of various frontal organisations, participated in the march. Patil, while addressing the gathering, accused the BJP-led central government of weakening democratic and constitutional institutions, and alleged irregularities in electoral processes and donations collected for the Ram temple. She urged people to strengthen Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi’s campaign to safeguard the Constitution. On the other hand, Agnihotri termed the march a mass movement against the vote theft, while Vinay Kumar asserted that the Congress remained united and strong in Himachal Pradesh. AICC secretary and co-in-charge Kamal Kant Sharma also called for protecting democracy and constitutional values. Meanwhile, several senior BJP leaders also accused the current Congress leaders of befooling the country’s people in the name of ‘Samvidhan Bachao Yatra’, ‘Samvidhan Raksha March’, and through other events. The leaders also termed the Congress a political party that always guarded its interests through the pious constitution. Former state BJP president and former minister Suresh Bhardwaj attended the event as the chief guest, which was chaired by legal cell co-convenor Ajay Vaidya. Addressing the gathering, Bhardwaj said, “Since independence, the Congress has been undermining the constitutional values… the same Congress is now preaching about protecting the Constitution.” He said former prime minister Indira Gandhi imposed the Emergency on June 25, 1975, curtailing fundamental rights, imprisoning opposition leaders, and restricting press freedom to retain power. BJP state media in-charge Karan Nanda criticised Rahul Gandhi for carrying a copy of the Constitution during political campaigns. Nanda said that the Congress leaders should first study their party’s own constitutional record. He pointed out that the 42nd Constitutional Amendment, enacted in 1976 during the Emergency, introduced changes to the Preamble, including the addition of the words ‘Socialist’, ‘Secular’, and ‘Integrity’. The BJP also highlighted the history and salient features of the Constitution, noting that it was adopted on November 26, 1949, and came into force on January 26, 1950.

headline: Bridging India’s critical border infrastructure gap
content: China and India have never agreed where their border lies. Without a boundary, both countries have treated border infrastructure as the practical means of defending territorial claims. Beijing has pursued this strategy systematically for decades, extending the logic to border settlements and dams in recent years. New Delhi has caught up since the 2017 Doklam standoff and the 2020 border clashes. The question then is what that gap consists of and how India could bridge it. China’s border infrastructure is not just larger; it is built for permanence. In contrast, India’s response is often triggered by crisis rather than standing policy, and is annual and project-based. The result has been slower mobilisation, limited operational reach and weaker forward logistics at the Line of Actual Control (LAC). The 2020 Ladakh crisis showed the gap in India’s capacity to move, sustain and rotate forces in high-altitude and extreme weather conditions.

headline: India-Germany submarine partnership can act as a catalyst for Indo-Pacific security: German envoy
content: With the India-Germany Project-75 India (P-75I) conventional submarine deal in CCS for final approval, Germany has reiterated its commitment to delivering comprehensive technology transfer under the long-term industrial partnership with India. German ambassador to India Jasper Wieck told TOI in an interview mutual trust regarding protection of sensitive technologies will be key to this partnership.Pegged at $ 8-9 billion, the proposed P-75I deal involving Germany’s TKMS and India’s Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL) to build 6 submarines equipped with the vital Air-Independent Propulsion (AIP) technology—which allows vessels to remain submerged for weeks without surfacing—will be one of the largest-ever defence contracts signed by India.Wieck said the project will see extensive transfer of technology in the underwater domain, not just limited to the submarines, as he highlighted overarching policy frameworks established by Berlin to guarantee reliability."Germany has committed to becoming a reliable defence-industrial partner of India. The bilateral defense industrial cooperation roadmap, which was signed in April this year, explicitly includes defense technology transfer," said Wieck.Asked about compartmentalisation and protection of sensitive submarine technology transferred to India, Wieck said technologies related to P-75I will only be shared with related Indian companies and government bodies. "Now, ultimately sharing technology with partners is always a question of trust and reliability, but here I can confirm India and Germany are definitely trusted partners in both directions," Wieck said.Speaking alongside Wieck about the technical execution of the project, TKMS global CEO Oliver Burkhard said P-75I is built around the transfer of the design of the submarine which will belong to the Indian Navy."You can't run a submarine if you haven't understood it. A few core technologies are protected in every partnership but India will get full access to that what they need to run, maintain, sustain those boats over the next 40 years," said Burkhard.Addressing India's concerns regarding TKMS' historical submarine contracts with Turkey, Burkhard clarified that each international program is strictly isolated and governed by German sovereign oversight."India does not have to worry because every program is ring-fenced. The technology, data, and intellectual property stay in that country and is protected by agreements between the two governments. The design India will receive is a highly advanced, unique-to-India boat and that has nothing to do with Turkey anymore," Burkhard said.Ambassador Wieck highlighted how the submarine agreement fits into Germany’s broader Indo-Pacific strategy, considering particularly regional security challenges and efforts to maintain rules-based maritime order."India plays a central role in the Indo-Pacific and India and Germany have a shared interest in upholding and defending the rules-based international order. And in the Indo-Pacific, that means the freedom of navigation and the security of lifelines of communication across the oceans. P75I is a long-term engagement with the potential of becoming a catalyst for deepening security and safety in the Indian Ocean," noted Wieck.Asked if India's ties with Russia might limit Germany's willingness to transfer sensitive naval technology, Wieck stressed mutual respect for sovereign choices."Each and every country around the world has its own network of partners and friends across the globe...instead of dwelling on India's partnerships with other countries, I'd rather focus on broadening and deepening the Indo-German partnership. Mutual trust, also regarding the protection of sensitive defense technology, is of course the key to that partnership," said Wieck.According to Burkhard, the submarine partnership might offer an opportunity for turning India a hub for Southeast Asian nations or others who want to join the submarine programme. "Submarines of the future can be built for other nations with, for example, a German design on one side, and on the other Indian competencies when it comes to assembly and manufacturing. A number of countries are approaching us. We are the global leaders in conventional submarines...so, if you can offer, for example, a country which is interested and it goes along with the political interests of India and Germany also to be part of a submarine building programme...it can be steered from a new hub in Asia, which will then be India for us," he said.On the need to adhere to strict delivery schedules, Burkhard emphasised TKMS’ delivery track record - citing four submarines and one frigate delivered this year - and noted that execution is a shared responsibility with MDL, with indigenous content reaching 70% on the final boat. While acknowledging past delays, he stressed confidence in meeting timelines, stating, "we are also in a delivery mode which shows hopefully some confidence that, of course, we will meet the timelines".Addressing concerns over integrating the AIP system into a new design for India’s P75I submarines, Burkhard called AIP a proven technology operated by the German Navy for over 20 years and across more than 50 submarines in service or under contract. He noted that India will own the design for P75I, making future modifications easier without having to depend on the foreign original equipment manufacturer.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Vizag youth advocate pitches ‘Blue Steps’ beach walk at Doha wellness forum
content: VISAKHAPATNAM Young people from eight countries met in Doha from November 8 to 11 for the fourth edition of the Youth at Hostel, International Forum, which looked at how youth hostels and tourism can promote physical and mental well-being. India was represented by Haritha Nagaveni Naganaboina of Visakhapatnam and Mithil Manoj Joshi of Goa. Ms. Haritha spoke on the country’s experience of youth health and well-being. Organised by Qatar Youth Hostels in partnership with UNICEF, the forum focused on United Nations Sustainable Development Goal, SDG-3: Good Health and Well-being. The theme was chosen by participants through a vote at the end of the previous edition. The forum aims to develop youth-led recommendations and programmes that link health and well-being with sustainable tourism, in line with the Qatar National Youth Policy. The participating countries were Qatar, the host, Bahrain, Libya, Lebanon, Slovenia, India, Pakistan and Spain. Ms. Haritha, 28, said the two of them were the only participants from India. Mr. Joshi is 25. The programme combined interactive sessions and workshops meant to build partnerships among youth hostel representatives. UNICEF and Qatari ministry representatives opened the ceremony, and addressed the delegates, she said. Participants attended eight workshops over two days. In one, groups were asked how tourism and wellness could be combined in Qatar. Ms. Haritha led her group in pitching “Blue Steps”, a beach walk proposal that the session host liked. Each country also made a presentation, and hers was on India’s experience. Extreme heat keeps most people in Qatar indoors, Ms. Haritha said, with residents travelling largely by car or metro. She was told that parks and cycling facilities were being developed there, and felt the idea could work in Visakhapatnam, which has a coastal setting and is not as hot. Delegates from other countries, she found, shared similar concerns, among them the need for a digital detox, and drew on their own geography for activities such as mountaineering and kayaking. Ms. Haritha, who holds an LL.M. from Middlesex University, London, and an LL.B. from Andhra University, is a former junior advocate. She has been associated with the Youth Hostels Association of India for about 13 years. The Andhra Pradesh branch recommended her to the national office, and she credits its chairman, Ch. Ravi Paul, for urging her to apply. Back home, she hopes to organise a five-day trek through forest to the Katiki waterfalls in Araku, and will propose it to the State branch.

headline: Party discipline, appointments figure in Revanth-Sandeep talks

headline: It will be a consensus candidate for Hiriyur bypoll, say BJP and JD(S) after meeting
content: BENGALURU Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel and Janata Dal (Secular) leader H.D. Kumaraswamy announced that his party, with the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) partner Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), will field a consensus candidate in the Hiriyur Assembly bypoll, while asserting that their priority to ensure the NDA’s victory. Leaders of both parties held a coordination meeting at a private hotel in Bengaluru to discuss the candidate selection and plans for the Winter Session of the legislature in Belagavi. Leader of Opposition in the Assembly R. Ashok and Leader of the Opposition in the Council Chalavadi Narayanaswamy, along with other leaders, attended the meeting. While both outfits were pushing for their party candidates for the Hiriyur seat, the meeting on Thursday sought to arrive at an amicable resolution. Mr. Ashok said the BJP and the JD(S) would continue their alliance in forthcoming local body elections and would soon announce State and district-level coordination committees to strengthen joint electoral efforts. “The Central leaders will soon take the final decision on who will contest in which constituency. There is no confusion or tug-of-war. There is complete clarity,” Mr. Ashok said. In the session Speaking about their joint strategy in the legislature session at Belagavi, Mr. Ashok said price rise and corruption in the State had crossed all limits, and these would be raised. Along with these issues, the BJP and the JD(S) will strongly raise the problems of farmers, the poor, ASHAs, and anganwadi workers in the session, he added. He said that because the two parties fought unitedly in the previous Assembly session, a situation was created in which Minister B. Nagendra had to resign in the alleged Valmiki corporation scam. “We have won all four seats in the recent Legislative Council elections, and the people of the State have extended support to our unity. It has been decided in the meeting to continue the same united fight in this session as well,” he said.

headline: Rishivandhiyam DMK MLA booked in harassment case
content: CHENNAI / KALLAKURICHI The Thiyagadurgam police have booked a case against Rishivandhiyam MLA Vasantham Karthikeyan of the DMK under four sections, including the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act, for allegedly threatening the Project Officer of the Tamil Nadu State Rural Livelihood Mission in Kallakurichi over phone. Acting on a complaint lodged by Lalitha, Project Officer of the Tamil Nadu State Rural Livelihoods Mission, Kallakurichi, that the MLA had threatened her, the police booked him on charges of resorting to criminal force deterring a public servant from discharging duties, act intended to insult the modesty of a woman and criminal intimidation. In a petition sent to the Chief Minister, the officer alleged that the MLA called her on the night of October 18, 2026, and accused her of preventing a Scheduled Caste woman from joining duty as a cook in the Perunthalaivar Kamaraj breakfast scheme. Even as she denied the allegation, Vasantham Karthikeyan said that appointments were being made unilaterally without his knowledge and threatened to get her transferred out. The complainant alleged that the MLA had intimidated her for acts that she never committed, and his actions deterred her from discharging her official duties. She said a factually incorrect news item was circulated on WhatsApp and Facebook to malign her reputation. Claiming she had no affiliation with any political party or community, she said the news that was being spread on social media coupled with political pressure and criminal intimidation, had restrained her from doing her lawful duties. Lalitha petitioned the District Collector and then approached the district cybercrime police. She then petitioned the Chief Minister’s Special Cell, and the Thiyagadurgam police registered the case on that petition. Lalitha has since been transferred to Ramanathapuram. Sources said the Kallakurichi Collector reportedly relieved her from her duties on November 23.

headline: 'Dham' Tag To Be Removed From Digha Jagannath Temple: Suvendu Adhikari
content: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Tuesday announced the state government will remove the insignia 'Dham' from the state-funded Lord Jagannath Temple and cultural activity premises in Digha, which was inaugurated by former CM Mamata Banerjee in April last year. The premises will now be called 'Sri Sri Jagannath Cultural Centre' and the deities of Lord Jagannath, Lord Balabhadra and Goddess Subhadra, at the temple within the premises, will be worshipped in accordance with prescribed norms and rituals, Adhikari said. The decision was taken in the wake of a formal request for removal of the tag made by the Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, Adhikari said. Responding to the development that took place a month after the BJP came to power in West Bengal, Majhi expressed his gratitude to Adhikari for the "prompt and tradition-loving step". The official request from him was delivered to Adhikari by Sambit Patra, BJP's MP in Lok Sabha from Puri, who acted as an emissary of the Odisha CM.

headline: ‘Massive, purposeful error’: Trump seeks probe into alleged ‘FAKE’ US GDP figures after growth revised to 4.3%
content: US President Donald Trump has accused his administration of deliberately under-reporting economic growth, demanding an investigation into what he described as a "purposeful" error in earlier gross domestic product (GDP) estimates.Trump's accusation followed a Commerce Department revision that put US economic growth at an annualised 4.3% in the third quarter, up from the earlier estimate of 3.4%. The president seized on the difference to allege that economic figures released before the election had been deliberately understated, but offered no evidence to support the claim.In a post on social media on Thursday, Trump called the earlier figures "FAKE" and described the revision as a "massive, and purposeful, error"."I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation. This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error," he wrote in a post from his golf course in West Palm Beach, Florida, on Thanksgiving morning.Why Trump is questioning US economic dataTrump's latest allegations centre on the difference between the initial GDP estimate and the revised figures released by the Commerce Department on Wednesday.However, the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), which publishes US GDP data, routinely releases estimates in stages. These figures are revised as additional economic information becomes available, meaning changes between initial and subsequent estimates are not unusual. Trump has repeatedly questioned the credibility of federal economic data when the figures have been unfavourable to his administration, without providing evidence of political interference. Trump previously fired US labour statistics chief The latest dispute follows Trump's decision in August 2025 to dismiss the head of the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) after a weak jobs report. The report showed that the US economy added just 73,000 jobs in July 2025. It also revised employment figures for May and June, showing that 258,000 fewer jobs had been created than previously estimated. Trump described the report as "phony" and "rigged" at the time.His latest demand for an investigation into GDP estimates marks another instance of the president challenging the credibility of federal statistical agencies over economic figures.GDP growth improves, but inflation remains a concernWhile Trump highlighted the upward revision in economic growth, the same Commerce Department release also reported an acceleration in inflation.A key inflation gauge, the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, rose at an annual rate of 3.8% in October, according to the data cited in the report. The inflation figure presents a more complicated picture of the US economy than the growth numbers highlighted by Trump.The president has repeatedly claimed credit for stronger economic performance, but voter assessments of economic conditions have remained less favourable.According to the AP Voter Poll, 76% of voters described the economy as either "not so good" or "poor" during the midterm elections.Around two-thirds also said Trump's policies had contributed to inflation.Trump has previously offered competing explanations for electoral setbacks, including blaming his absence from the ballot for his party's performance in the midterms.

headline: Saurav Das passport issue: MEA explains why CJP co-convenor was stopped from flying to London; details here
content: The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Wednesday said Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Saurav Das had received a show-cause notice over inconsistencies in the place of birth mentioned in his passport. The notice was issued following inputs from the relevant authorities, according to PTI.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the Regional Passport Office (RPO) in Chennai served the notice on Saurav Das on Monday, asking him to submit his explanation within seven days.The clarification came after Das alleged that immigration authorities had stopped him from travelling to the United Kingdom, where he was scheduled to attend an Oxford University event and speak on the "cockroach movement".Meanwhile, Das moved the Delhi High Court on Wednesday, challenging the authorities' decision to prevent him from travelling overseas.Jaiswal emphasised that applicants are required to provide accurate details while applying for passports. "Let me say that the passport application provides for declaration of correct information by the applicant," he said.Explaining the procedure followed when inconsistencies are detected, Jaiswal said, "If at any stage a discrepancy is noted or reported by authorities, which amounts to suppression of facts, then we issue a show cause notice to the applicant to explain his or her point of view," he said.He further clarified that the notice against Das followed inputs from law enforcement agencies. "Based on reports that we received from the relevant law enforcement authorities, a show-cause notice was issued by RPO Chennai to Saurav Das on November 23 seeking his clarification within seven days regarding his place of birth," he added.PTI citing sources indicated that the CJP leader had obtained his passport from the Chennai Regional Passport Office, where officials subsequently flagged inconsistencies concerning his place of birth.Jaiswal also said Das had been advised against using the passport until he submitted his response to the notice.Meanwhile, Das claimed that immigration officials stopped him at the Delhi airport while he was completing departure formalities for his London-bound flight.What did Das' lawyer tell the court?Representing Das before the Delhi High Court, his lawyer told the bench that immigration officials had prevented his client from travelling without providing any formal order or restriction notice."I was stopped at immigration. No order was shown to me. No LOC, no prohibition by any authority from letting me travel. I am seeking listing of a fresh petition today. I can still make it to the United Kingdom on November 27, which is where my arrangements are," Das's counsel submitted in the High Court.The lawyer informed the court that Das's scheduled flight was on Thursday. Responding to the submission, the bench said, "Let it be (heard) tomorrow."Das slams govtEarlier, in a social media post on Monday night, Das accused the government of deliberately preventing his UK visit to stop him from speaking to students at universities abroad."This coward government did not allow me to board my flight to London where I was invited by prestigious universities like Oxford, Cambridge, LSE, Edinburgh to deliver talks on the cockroach movement," he said.He further alleged that the authorities were apprehensive about his engagement with international academic institutions, adding, "Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual govt was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions!," he alleged.Das was due to depart for London on a flight scheduled for 1 am on Tuesday.

headline: ASR district records 59.61% voter turnout in first phase of panchayat elections
content: PADERU The first phase of Gram Panchayat elections in Alluri Sitharama Raju district concluded on Thursday, with an overall voter turnout of 59.61% across G.K. Veedhi, Koyyuru and Chinthapalli mandals, according to figures released by the district administration. Counting of votes is under way. Koyyuru mandal recorded the highest voter turnout at 67.35%, followed by Chinthapalli (56.05%) and G.K. Veedhi (55.45%). District Collector and District Election Officer T. Nishanthi reviewed the conduct of the first phase with Returning Officers and other election personnel soon after polling ended. She monitored the counting process from the control room and directed officials to clearly explain the procedures to political party representatives before it began. Reviewing preparedness for the second phase on November 29, she asked officials to complete staff training, and to arrange for transport, food and other amenities for polling personnel, alongside ensuring the secure storage of ballot boxes. The second phase of polling will cover 87 gram panchayats and 880 wards across Pedabayalu, Munchingiputtu, Ananthagiri and G. Madugula mandals.

headline: Karnataka allows Tulu in government offices in Udupi, Dakshina Kannada
content: Mangaluru: The Karnataka government has issued an order permitting the use of Tulu as an additional language alongside Kannada for administrative purposes in Udupi and Dakshina Kannada districts.According to the order, the Kannada script will be adopted for Tulu. Implementation units will be established in the district administration offices, and translators will be appointed to facilitate the use of Tulu for administrative purposes in district and taluk offices.The government has ordered the appointment of two translators each at the offices of the Deputy Commissioners in both districts. In addition, one translator each will be appointed at the offices of tahsildars in all 16 taluks, nine in Dakshina Kannada and seven in Udupi.An honorarium of Rs 30,000 per month per translator, inclusive of all expenses, has been fixed. .Clear pending loan applications, submit rejection details within a week: Dakshina Kannada MP Chowta to banks.The order stipulates that public offices in both districts must accept petitions and applications in Tulu and provide information and responses in Tulu alongside Kannada.Important orders issued at the Deputy Commissioner level and prominent public notice boards in the two districts must also be published in Tulu in addition to Kannada. The measure aims to promote the Tulu language and facilitate access to government services for Tulu-speaking citizens, sources said.The order has been issued in accordance with the decision taken at the State Cabinet meeting held in Mangaluru on September 18.

headline: Delhi, Bihar to start regular bus services on 18 routes
content: Delhi and Bihar governments are set to sign an agreement to launch year-round interstate bus services on 18 routes, easing year-round connectivity for nearly 20 lakh people from Bihar and Purvanchal living in the Capital. The proposed agreement will allow organised bus services between Delhi and various destinations in Bihar, including Araria, Bhagalpur, Buxar, Darbhanga, East Champaran, Gaya, Kishanganj, Madhubani, Muzaffarpur, Nawada, Patna and Purnia. Both states are set to have 12 permits each on every route. Delhi Transport Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh said the agreement would provide relief to passengers, particularly during peak travel seasons when people face difficulties due to limited availability of train tickets and overcrowding in buses. “I am particularly happy about this initiative as I myself hail from Purvanchal. The agreement will bring considerable convenience to people travelling between the two states. Both the state governments will mutually finalise the timings and schedules to ensure that passengers can access these services conveniently,” he added. The agreement marks a shift from festival-specific bus arrangements to a structured, year-round interstate transport system. During Diwali and Chhath Puja this year, around 76 buses were operated on routes connecting Bihar with Delhi. The response to these services and the growing demand for travel between the two states have highlighted the need for a permanent arrangement, officials said. Singh said the Bihar State Road Transport Corporation has procured 75 non-AC and 74 AC buses for interstate operations. Another 150 buses are proposed to be deployed under the public-private partnership model. According to officials, around 200 AC and non-AC Volvo buses will start operations on the 18 routes. The fares are likely to be around Rs 2,000 to Rs 3,000 for sleeper and non-sleeper categories, respectively, they added.

headline: BSP sounds poll bugle, promises to pull Punjab out of crisis
content: The BSP on Thursday sounded the poll bugle for the Assembly elections by organising a massive state-level ‘Punjab Sambhalo’ rally in Phillaur on the Constitution Day.Addressing a gathering, BSP national convenor Akash Anand expressed confidence that the party would secure an impressive mandate and form the next government in Punjab, promising to pull the state out of the crises of drug abuse, unemployment and mounting debt and transform it into a leading state in the country.BSP chief sector in-charges Ramji Gautam and Suresh Rao, along with central in-charge Vipul Kumar, were also present. The rally was presided over by BSP Punjab president and former MP Dr Avtar Singh Karimpuri.Beginning his address by paying tributes to Dr BR Ambedkar and BSP founder Kanshi Ram, Anand said BSP president Mayawati had implemented the Constitution’s ideals at the grassroots level during her tenure as Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister.Taking on the Congress, Shiromani Akali Dal-BJP alliance and the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), Anand alleged that successive governments had failed to fulfil their promises on eliminating drugs, delivering justice in sacrilege cases, controlling inflation, generating employment and improving healthcare and education. He claimed that these parties had made tall promises before elections but failed to deliver once in power.Questioning the AAP government’s campaigns, including ‘Rangla Punjab’ and ‘Yudh Nashian Virudh’, Anand alleged that these initiatives had remained largely confined to publicity, while drug abuse continued to spread across the state. Referring to the case of Mansa-based Parvinder Singh Jhotta, he alleged that those raising their voices against the drug menace were being targeted and that the government had surrendered before the drug mafia.He further alleged that traders, shopkeepers, farmers and ordinary citizens were increasingly feeling insecure under the present dispensation. Unemployment, he said, was forcing young people to leave their families and migrate abroad in search of better opportunities. Raising questions over recruitment policies, he alleged that permanent employment opportunities were being replaced by contractual appointments and that reservation provisions were being undermined.Highlighting the concerns of government employees and pensioners, Anand said nearly 3.5 lakh employees and four lakh pensioners in Punjab were struggling for their pending demands. He also criticised the BJP and AAP governments over their alleged failure to fulfil commitments made to farmers, adding that around 700 farmers had lost their lives during the agitation against the three farm laws and that the demand for a legal guarantee of Minimum Support Price (MSP) remained unresolved.

headline: ‘Promises forgotten after polls’: Punjab CM Mann tears into previous governments
content: Moga, Nov 26 (PTI) Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann on Thursday lashed out at the Congress, SAD and the BJP, saying these parties ruled the state for years, took turns in power, blamed one another, made promises and then forgot the people of the state after elections. “Now they are coming together because they are worried about the work being done by the Aam Aadmi Party government. The people of Punjab know their history and will not be misled by their new political arrangements,” Mann asserted. Mann was addressing the Punjab Khushaal rally ahead of the 2027 state Assembly polls. “Today, I want to speak directly to the people of Punjab about the work we have done and the promises we have fulfilled. Those who ruled this state for decades must also tell the people what they did for Punjab. “They had years in power, but the state continued to face problems. Our government is presenting its report card before the people because we believe that a government must be answerable to the public,” Mann said. Noting that the people of Punjab know their history, the chief minister expressed confidence that they will not be misled by new political arrangements.

headline: GAIL (India) plans to set up a data centre in Faridabad
content: Government-owned leading natural gas maker, GAIL (India), is entering the data centre segment with plans to set up a facility in Haryana. The firm is planning to set up a 5 MW data centre in Faridabad, Haryana. PSU will develop the project under a 50:50 joint venture (JV) with an experienced strategic partner. An expression of interest (EoI) has been floated to identify and select a strategic partner. The JV partner will have to manage power and water, and handle construction, operations, and commercialisation. headline: Manish Kumar Launches Digital Marketing Course in Delhi NCR With Practical AI Training
content: VMPLNew Delhi [India], November 26: SEO and digital marketing professional Manish Kumar has launched a Digital Marketing Course in Delhi NCR for students, freshers, working professionals, freelancers, entrepreneurs and business owners. Enrolment for the first batch is now open, and interested learners can attend a free demo session before joining.The programme covers SEO, Local SEO, Google Ads, social media marketing, Meta Ads, content planning, landing pages, analytics, lead generation and the responsible use of artificial intelligence. Course information and enrolment details are available at https://manishseo.co.in/digital-marketing-course-in-delhi/Training is designed around the way marketing activities work together in real business situations. Learners will study customer search behaviour, campaign planning, website experience, conversion paths and performance measurement rather than treating each platform as an isolated tool."Most freshers I meet can run a keyword tool, but very few can explain why a page isn't ranking. That's the gap this course is built around," said Manish Kumar.Practical AI Training With Human ReviewAI is included as a supporting tool across research, content planning and campaign preparation. Learners will explore how it can assist with audience-question research, keyword organisation, content briefs, advertising concepts, landing-page ideas and reporting summaries.The programme also addresses the limitations of AI-generated material. Learners will be encouraged to check accuracy, protect confidential information, review originality and adapt outputs to the intended audience and business objective.The aim is to help participants use AI more responsibly and efficiently without treating it as a replacement for marketing strategy, reliable data or human judgment.Job-Oriented Learning and Initial Career SupportThe course includes practical exercises based on activities commonly encountered in entry-level digital marketing, SEO, paid-media, content and agency-support roles.Assignments may include reviewing websites, researching keywords, planning campaigns, evaluating landing pages, preparing content briefs and interpreting performance information.Initial career support and guidance are also included.
